|language=en}}</ref>

=== 2019–present: ''The Kingdom'' trilogy ===
After the release of ''The House That Jack Built'', Trier planned to produce ''Études'', an anthology film consisting of ten black and white segments, each ten minutes long, inspired by the [[Étude|musical form]], though it never came to fruition.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sharf |first=Zack |date=2018-04-16 |title=Lars von Trier Plans to Direct 10 Short Films After 'House That Jack Built' Left Him With Terrible Anxiety |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2018/04/lars-von-trier-short-films-etudes-house-that-jack-built-1201953115/ |access-date=2022-11-06 |website=IndieWire |language=en}}</ref> In December 2020, it was announced he would produce a belated third and final season of ''[[The Kingdom (TV miniseries)|The Kingdom]]'', titled ''The Kingdom Exodus'', with [[Søren Pilmark]] returning as Jørgen 'Hook' Krogshøj, [[Ghita Nørby]] as Rigmor Mortensen, alongside a new cast including [[Mikael Persbrandt]] as Dr. Helmer, Jr. It was shot in 2021, consisting of five episodes released in November 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://theplaylist.net/lars-von-trier-the-kingdom-season-3-20201220/|title='The Kingdom': Lars Von Trier Returns To His Cult '90s Series With Third Season|website=theplaylist.net|date=20 December 2020 |access-date=31 December 2020|archive-date=20 December 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201220145337/https://theplaylist.net/lars-von-trier-the-kingdom-season-3-20201220/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pXWcl6OuVw8|title=Lars von Trier: The Burden From Donald Duck &#124; Louisiana Channel|date=24 December 2020 |via=www.youtube.com|access-date=31 December 2020|archive-date=10 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210110153446/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pXWcl6OuVw8&gl=US&hl=en|url-status=live}}</ref> The miniseries premiered out of competition at the [[79th Venice International Film Festival|Venice Film Festival]] as a five-hour feature-length film. It received mixed reviews from critics.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sondermann |first=Selina |title=Venice Film Festival 2022: The Kingdom: Exodus (Riget: Exodus) {{!}} Review |url=https://www.theupcoming.co.uk/2022/09/05/venice-film-festival-2022-the-kingdom-exodus-riget-exodus-review/ |access-date=2022-10-06 |website=The Upcoming|date=5 September 2022 }}</ref>

In 2024, Trier announced he was working on a new film titled ''After'' which will benefit from funding from the Danish Film Institute. [[Stellan Skarsgård]] was cast as the film's lead.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Scanu |first=John |date=2024-09-18 |title=Lars von Trier, the Danish director's next film will be titled &quot;After&quot; |url=https://www.unionesarda.it/en/lars-von-trier-the-danish-director39-s-next-film-will-be-titled-quot-afterquot-pdhy1drd |access-date=2025-01-16 |website=L'Unione Sarda English |language=en}}</ref> Filming was expected to begin in summer 2025, with von Trier's health conditions reflected in the plot of the film.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/features/lars-von-trier-david-lynch-gaspar-noe-b2706607.html | title=Lars von Trier is exciting and enraging – his Parkinson's spells doom for cinema | website=[[Independent.co.uk]] | date=3 March 2025 }}</ref>

== Aesthetics, themes, and style of working ==

=== Themes ===
Trier's films deal with themes of religious imagery and his treatment of subjects<ref name="scancan.net2" /> such as mercy,<ref name="BT" /> sacrifice, and [[mental health]],<ref name="LV" /> confrontational examination of [[Existentialism|existential]], social,<ref name="LB" /><ref name="NR" /> and political<ref name="kinema.uwaterloo.ca2" /><ref name="scancan.net2" /> issues. Most of the films depicted in various forms of politics and religions, such as [[Nazism]] in ''[[Europa (1991 film)|Europa]]'', [[Christianity]] in ''[[Breaking the Waves]]'' and ''[[The House That Jack Built (2018 film)|The House that Jack Built]]'', [[atheism]] in ''[[Dogville]]'', and [[Anti-capitalism|anti-bourgeois]] in ''[[The Idiots (1998 film)|The Idiots]]''.

=== Influences ===
Trier is heavily influenced by the work of [[Carl Theodor Dreyer]]<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UHJZAAAAMAAJ |title=Lars von Trier |last=Stevenson |first=Jack |publisher=British Film Institute |year=2002 |isbn=978-0-85170-902-4 |page=23 |quote=During work on a TV adaptation of the never-filmed Dreyer script, Medea, in 1988, Trier claimed to have a telepathic connection with him. He even claimed his golden retriever, Kajsa, was also in spiritual contact with Dreyer ... |access-date=11 October 2010 |archive-date=5 June 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130605005113/http://books.google.com/books?id=UHJZAAAAMAAJ |url-status=live }}</ref> and the film ''[[The Night Porter]]''.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=b9iP9OWEqncC&pg=PA195 |title=Alien sex: the body and desire in cinema and theology |last=Loughlin |first=Gerard |publisher=Wiley-Blackwell |year=2004 |isbn=978-0-631-21180-8 |page=195 |author-link=Gerard Loughlin |access-date=11 October 2010 |archive-date=4 June 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130604110910/http://books.google.com/books?id=b9iP9OWEqncC&pg=PA195 |url-status=live}}</ref> He was so inspired by the short film ''[[The Perfect Human]]'', directed by [[Jørgen Leth]], that he challenged Leth to redo the short five times in the feature film ''[[The Five Obstructions]]''.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hev6YYxFpYgC |title=The Routledge companion to philosophy and film |last2=Plantinga |first2=Carl R. |date=3 December 2008 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-0-415-77166-5 |pages=631–40 |chapter=58 |last1=Livingston |first1=Paisley |first3=Mette |last3=Hjort |access-date=11 October 2010 |archive-date=4 June 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130604020549/http://books.google.com/books?id=hev6YYxFpYgC |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Writing ===
Trier's writing style has been heavily influenced by his work with actors on set, as well as the [[Dogme 95]] manifesto that he co-authored.<ref name="CSinterview">{{cite web |url=https://creativescreenwriting.com/my-films-are-a-little-dark-right-lars-von-trier/ |title='My films are a little dark, right?' Lars von Trier |last=Taylor |first=Elayne |date=2001 |website=Creative Screenwriting |access-date=18 December 2018 |archive-date=19 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181219044557/https://creativescreenwriting.com/my-films-are-a-little-dark-right-lars-von-trier/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In an interview with ''Creative Screenwriting'', he described his process as "writing a sketch and keep[ing] the story simple...then part of the script work is with the actors."<ref name="CSinterview" /> He again cites Dreyer as an influence, pointing to his method of overwriting his scripts, then significantly cutting the length down.<ref name="CSinterview" /> Reflecting on the storytelling across his body of work, Trier said, "all the stories are about a realist who comes into conflict with life. I'm not crazy about real life, and real life is not crazy about me."<ref name="CSinterview" />

=== Filming techniques ===
Trier has said that "a film should be like a stone in your shoe".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bell |first1=Emma |title=Lars von Trier: Anti-American? Me? |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/features/lars-von-trier-anti-american-me-321010.html |access-date=22 December 2018 |work=The Independent |date=21 October 2005 |archive-date=22 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181222183142/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/features/lars-von-trier-anti-american-me-321010.html |url-status=live}}</ref> To create original art he feels that filmmakers must distinguish themselves stylistically from other films, often by placing restrictions on the film making process. The most famous such restriction is the cinematic "vow of chastity" of the [[Dogme95|Dogme 95]] movement. In ''[[Dancer in the Dark]]'', he used jump shots<ref>{{cite book |last=Hurbis-Cherrier |first=Mick |title=Voice & vision: a creative approach to narrative film and DV production |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=X_ZIihJ_WpMC&pg=PA82 |access-date=11 October 2010 |date=13 March 2007 |publisher=Focal Press |isbn=978-0-240-80773-7 |page=82 |quote=Lars von Trier uses jump cuts as an aesthetic device throughout Dancer in the Dark |archive-date=4 June 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130604014146/http://books.google.com/books?id=X_ZIihJ_WpMC&pg=PA82 |url-status=live }}</ref> and dramatically different color palettes and camera techniques for the "real world" and musical portions of the film.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Rudolph |first=Pascal |date=2020-11-15 |title=Björk on the Gallows: Performance, Persona, and Authenticity in Lars von Trier's Dancer in the Dark |url=https://iaspmjournal.net/index.php/IASPM_Journal/article/view/993 |journal=IASPM Journal |language=en |volume=10 |issue=1 |pages=22–42 |doi=10.5429/2079-3871(2020)v10i1.3en |s2cid=228960719 |issn=2079-3871|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Trier often shoots [[digital cinematography|digitally]] and operates the camera himself, preferring to continuously shoot the actors in-character without stopping between takes. In ''Dogville'', because there were no walls between the "buildings" on the set, actors needed to stay in character for hours, even when not part of the scene being filmed.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Lumholdt |first1=Jan |title=Lars von Trier: Interviews |date=2003 |publisher=University of Mississippi |page=212}}</ref> These techniques often put great strain on the actors, most famously with [[Björk]] during the filming of ''Dancer in the Dark''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://theplaylist.net/bjork-sexual-harassment-danish-director-20171017/ |title=Björk further details 'paralyzing' sexual harassment from Lars von Trier |last=Jagernauth |first=Kevin |date=17 October 2017 |website=The Playlist |access-date=21 March 2019 |archive-date=20 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190320201348/https://theplaylist.net/bjork-sexual-harassment-danish-director-20171017/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

Trier would later return to explicit images in ''[[Antichrist (film)|Antichrist]]'' (2009), exploring darker themes, but he ran into problems when he tried once more with ''[[Nymphomaniac (film)|Nymphomaniac]]'', which had 90 minutes cut out (reducing it from five-and-one-half to four hours) for its international release in 2013 in order to be commercially viable,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dfi-film.dk/nymphomaniac-long |title=DFI-FILM – Stensgaard & von Trier |website=www.dfi-film.dk |access-date=9 May 2017 |archive-date=10 February 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170210110043/http://www.dfi-film.dk/nymphomaniac-long |url-status=live }}</ref> taking nearly a year to be shown complete anywhere in an uncensored director's cut.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.kino.dk/film/n/ny/nymphomaniac-directors-cut |title=Nymphomaniac: Director's cut |date=21 August 2014 |access-date=9 May 2017 |archive-date=9 July 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170709234726/http://www.kino.dk/film/n/ny/nymphomaniac-directors-cut |url-status=live}}</ref>

While Trier commissioned new musical compositions for his early films, his more recent work has made use of existing music.<ref name="Rudolph 1">{{Cite book |last=Rudolph |first=Pascal |url=https://www.nomos-elibrary.de/10.5771/9783967077582/praeexistente-musik-im-film?page=1 |title=Präexistente Musik im Film |date=2022-10-14 |publisher=edition text + kritik im Richard Boorberg Verlag |isbn=978-3-96707-757-5 |pages=45 |language=de |doi=10.5771/9783967077582|s2cid=253055339 }}</ref> With ''Nymphomaniac'', the principle of musical eclecticism is also applied within the film.<ref name="Rudolph 1" /> He often heavily edits compositions to manipulate and provoke the audience.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Rudolph |first=Pascal |date=2023 |title=The Musical Idea Work Group: Production and Reception of Pre-existing Music in Film |journal=Twentieth-Century Music |volume=20 |issue=2 |language=en |pages=136–156 |doi=10.1017/S1478572222000214 |s2cid=252138641 |issn=1478-5722|doi-access=free}}</ref>

=== Approach to actors ===
In an interview for [[IndieWire]], Trier compared his approach to actors with "how a chef would work with a potato or a piece of meat", clarifying that working with actors has differed on each film based on the production conditions.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.indiewire.com/2009/10/lars-von-trier-i-think-working-with-actors-is-a-little-bit-how-a-chef-would-work-with-a-potato-246359/ |title=Lars von Trier: "I think working with actors is a little bit how a chef would work with a potato…" - IndieWire |first=Brian |last=Brooks |website=www.indiewire.com |date=20 October 2009 |access-date=9 May 2017 |archive-date=24 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170824012453/http://www.indiewire.com/2009/10/lars-von-trier-i-think-working-with-actors-is-a-little-bit-how-a-chef-would-work-with-a-potato-246359/ |url-status=live}}</ref> He has occasionally courted controversy by his treatment of his lead actresses.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |url=https://www.npr.org/2011/11/06/142026288/lars-von-trier-a-problematic-sort-of-ladies-man|title=Lars Von Trier: A Problematic Sort Of Ladies' Man?|website=NPR.org|access-date=9 May 2017|archive-date=26 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170426063617/http://www.npr.org/2011/11/06/142026288/lars-von-trier-a-problematic-sort-of-ladies-man|url-status=live|last=Dowell|first=Pat|date=6 November 2011}}</ref> He and [[Björk]] famously fell out during the shooting of ''[[Dancer in the Dark]]'', to the point where she would abscond from filming for days at a time.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.digitalspy.com/movies/a818243/movie-feuds-bruce-willis-megan-fox/ |title=The 8 most notorious feuds between stars and their directors |last=Fletcher |first=Rosie |publisher=Hearst Magazines UK |date=6 June 2018 |website=digitalspy.com |access-date=21 March 2019 |archive-date=20 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190320202059/https://www.digitalspy.com/movies/a818243/movie-feuds-bruce-willis-megan-fox/ |url-status=live }}</ref> She said of Trier, who shattered a monitor while it was next to her, that "you can take quite sexist film directors like [[Woody Allen]] or [[Stanley Kubrick]] and still they are the one that provide the soul to their movies. In Lars von Trier's case it is not so and he knows it. He needs a female to provide his work soul. And he envies them and hates them for it. So he has to destroy them during the filming. And hide the evidence."<ref name="LT" />

[[Nicole Kidman]], who starred in Trier's ''[[Dogville]]'', said in an interview with [[Radio National|ABC Radio National]] that she tried to quit the film several times in response to comments Trier made on set, often while inebriated, "but I say this laughing...I didn't do the sequel but I'm still very good friends with him, strangely enough, because I admire his honesty and I see him as an artist, and I say, my gosh, it's such a hard world now to have a unique voice, and he certainly has that."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/radionational/invalid/movietime/interview-with-nicole-kidman-actor-margot-at-the/3292346|title=Interview with Nicole Kidman, actor, 'Margot At The Wedding'|date=2 November 2006|website=ABC Radio National|access-date=8 December 2021|archive-date=8 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211208183623/https://www.abc.net.au/radionational/invalid/movietime/interview-with-nicole-kidman-actor-margot-at-the/3292346|url-status=live}}</ref>

However, other actresses he has worked with, such as [[Kirsten Dunst]] and [[Charlotte Gainsbourg]] have spoken out in defence of his approach.<ref name="LT">{{cite web |url=https://www.gq.com/story/lars-von-trier-gq-interview-bjork-john-c-reilly-kirsten-dunst-nicole-kidman-extras/ |title=Lars von Trier Interview GQ October 2011 |first=Chris |last=Heath |date=17 October 2011 |access-date=9 May 2017 |archive-date=7 May 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170507230543/http://www.gq.com/story/lars-von-trier-gq-interview-bjork-john-c-reilly-kirsten-dunst-nicole-kidman-extras |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.lemonde.fr/culture/article/2014/01/28/charlotte-gainsbourg-je-suis-prete-a-excuser-beaucoup-chez-lars_4355449_3246.html |title=Charlotte Gainsbourg : " Je suis prête à excuser beaucoup chez Lars " |first=Isabelle |last=Regnier |newspaper=Le Monde.fr |date=28 January 2014 |via=Le Monde |access-date=16 October 2017 |archive-date=16 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171016230040/http://www.lemonde.fr/culture/article/2014/01/28/charlotte-gainsbourg-je-suis-prete-a-excuser-beaucoup-chez-lars_4355449_3246.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.indiewire.com/2014/03/charlotte-gainsbourg-on-being-lars-von-triers-nymphomaniac-i-was-disturbed-embarrassed-and-a-little-humiliated-28659/ |title=Charlotte Gainsbourg On Being Lars von Trier's 'Nymphomaniac': 'I was disturbed, embarrassed and a little humiliated…' - IndieWire |first=Boyd van |last=Hoeij |website=www.indiewire.com |date=25 March 2014 |access-date=16 October 2017 |archive-date=5 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171005212134/http://www.indiewire.com/2014/03/charlotte-gainsbourg-on-being-lars-von-triers-nymphomaniac-i-was-disturbed-embarrassed-and-a-little-humiliated-28659/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Nymphomaniac'' star [[Stacy Martin]] has stated that he never forced her to do anything that was outside her comfort zone. She said "I don't think he's a misogynist. The fact that he sometimes depicts women as troubled or dangerous or dark or even evil; that doesn't automatically make him anti-feminist. It's a very dated argument. I think that Lars loves women."<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2014/feb/06/nymphomaniac-charlotte-gainsbourg-stacy-martin-lars-von-trier |title=Nymphomaniac stars: 'Lars isn't a misogynist, he loves women' |first=Xan |last=Brooks |newspaper=The Guardian |date=6 February 2014 |via=www.theguardian.com |access-date=16 October 2017 |archive-date=16 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171016225808/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2014/feb/06/nymphomaniac-charlotte-gainsbourg-stacy-martin-lars-von-trier |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Sexual harassment allegations with Björk ===

In October 2017, in the wake of dozens of [[Harvey Weinstein sexual abuse cases|sexual abuse cases]] brought against film producer [[Harvey Weinstein]], [[Björk]] posted on her [[Facebook]] page that she had been sexually harassed by a Danish film director.<ref>{{cite news |last=Nyren |first=Erin |url=https://variety.com/2017/film/news/bjork-sexual-harassment-danish-director-1202590429/ |title=Björk Shares Experience of Harassment By 'Danish Director:' He Created 'An Impressive Net of Illusion' |work=Variety |date=15 October 2017 |access-date=17 October 2017}}</ref> She commented:
{{blockquote|It was extremely clear to me when I walked into the actresses profession that my humiliation and role as a lesser sexually harassed being was the norm and set in stone with the director and a staff of dozens who enabled it and encouraged it. I became aware of that it is a universal thing that a director can touch and harass his actresses at will and the institution of film allows it. When I turned the director down repeatedly he sulked and punished me and created for his team an impressive net of illusion where I was framed as the difficult one. ...
and in my opinion he had a more fair and meaningful relationship with his actresses after my confrontation so there is hope. Let's hope this statement supports the actresses and actors all over. Let's stop this. There is a wave of change in the world.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.facebook.com/bjork/posts/10155777444371460 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171016011740/https://www.facebook.com/bjork/posts/10155777444371460 |author=Björk |title=i am inspired by the women everywhere who are speaking up online to tell about my experience with a danish director |publisher=Facebook |date=15 October 2017 |access-date=16 October 2017 |archive-date=16 October 2017}}</ref>}}
The ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' found evidence identifying him as Lars von Trier.<ref>{{cite news |last=D'Zurilla |first=Christie |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/la-et-entertainment-news-updates-bjork-sexual-harassment-lars-von-1508261125-htmlstory.html |title=Björk details alleged harassment; Lars von Trier denies accusations |work=Los Angeles Times |date=17 October 2017 |access-date=17 October 2017}}</ref> Von Trier has rejected Björk's allegation that he sexually harassed her during the making of the film ''Dancer in the Dark'', and said "That was not the case. But that we were definitely not friends, that's a fact", to Danish daily ''[[Jyllands-Posten]]'' in its online edition.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Enggaard |first=Michael |date=2017-10-16 |title=Lars von Trier: Der er intet i den sag |url=https://jyllands-posten.dk/kultur/film/ECE9953026/lars-von-trier-der-er-intet-i-den-sag/ |access-date=2023-08-28 |website=Jyllands-Posten |language=da}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite news|title='Not the case': Lars Von Trier denies sexually harassing Björk|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2017/oct/17/not-the-case-lars-von-trier-denies-sexually-harassing-bjork|work=The Guardian|date=2017-10-19|access-date=2025-11-29|issn=0261-3077|language=en-GB|last=Staff}}</ref> [[Peter Aalbæk Jensen]], the producer of ''Dancer in the Dark'', told ''Jyllands-Posten'' that "as far as I remember we [Lars von Trier and I] were the victims. That woman was stronger than both Lars von Trier and me and our company put together. She dictated everything and was about to close a movie of 100m kroner [$16m]".<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Enggaard |first=Michael |date=2017-10-15 |title=Peter Aalbæk afviser Björk-anklager om sexchikane: »Vi var ofrene« |url=https://jyllands-posten.dk/kultur/film/ECE9952454/peter-aalbaek-afviser-bjoerkanklager-om-sexchikane-vi-var-ofrene/ |access-date=2023-08-28 |website=Jyllands-Posten |language=da}}</ref> After Trier's statement, Björk published further allegations against the director via her personal Facebook page.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.facebook.com/story.php?story_fbid=10155782628166460&id=6747251459&_ft_=top_level_post_id.10155782628166460:tl_objid.10155782628166460:throwback_story_fbid.10155782628166460&__tn__=,; |title=Björk |website=www.facebook.com}}</ref>

''[[The Guardian]]'' later alleged that Jensen's studio, Zentropa, with which Trier frequently collaborated, had had an endemic culture of sexual harassment. Jensen stepped down from CEO position of Zentropa as further harassment allegations were published in 2017.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Lars von Trier producer: 'I'll stop slapping asses' in wake of #MeToo|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2018/may/10/lars-von-trier-producer-peter-aalbaek-jensen-stop-slapping-asses|work=The Guardian|date=2018-05-10|access-date=2025-11-29|issn=0261-3077|language=en-GB|first=Andrew|last=Pulver}}</ref>

=== Sex and violence in films ===
Several of his films – ''[[The Idiots (1998 film)|The Idiots]]'' (1998), ''[[Antichrist (film)|Antichrist]]'' (2009), ''[[Nymphomaniac (film)|Nymphomaniac]]'' (2013) and ''[[The House That Jack Built (2018 film)|The House That Jack Built]]'' (2018) – contain explicit content that has generated controversy;<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lazic |first=Manuela |date=2018-12-14 |title=The Hell That Lars von Trier Built |url=https://www.theringer.com/movies/2018/12/14/18139814/the-house-that-jack-built-lars-von-trier-review-dogville-nymphomaniac-antichrist-dance-in-the-dark |access-date=2023-02-03 |website=The Ringer |language=en}}</ref> the first faced widespread backlash upon its release as one film critic, [[Mark Kermode]], was ejected from The Idiots premiere screening at Cannes for heckling, and the film was heavily censored for subsequent releases.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-12 |title='The Idiots': Lars Von Trier's Controversial Film Gets 25th Anniversary Theatrical Release |url=https://collider.com/the-idiots-movie-release-date-remastered/ |access-date=2023-06-03 |website=Collider |language=en}}</ref> At the [[2018 Cannes Film Festival]], approximately 100 audience members walked out of the premiere of ''The House That Jack Built''.<ref name="JB" />

== Personal life ==
=== Family ===
[[File:Fritz Michael Hartmann.gif|thumb|180px|Fritz Michael Hartmann ({{c.|1950}})]]
In 1989, Trier's mother confessed to him on her deathbed that his biological father was not the man who raised him, but her former employer, {{ill|Fritz Michael Hartmann|da}} (1909–2000),<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=f9kpAQAAIAAJ |title=Medien Wissenschaft |date=2004 |publisher=Niemeyer |page=112 |language=de |author1=Philipps-Universität Marburg |author2=Universität-Gesamthochschule-Siegen |access-date=11 October 2010 |archive-date=4 June 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130604003753/http://books.google.com/books?id=f9kpAQAAIAAJ |url-status=live }}</ref> who was descended from a long line of Danish classical musicians. Hartmann's grandfather was [[Emil Hartmann]], and his great-grandfather [[Johan Peter Emilius Hartmann|J. P. E. Hartmann]]. His uncles included [[Niels Gade]] and [[Johan Ernst Hartmann]], and [[Niels Viggo Bentzon]] was his cousin. She stated that she did this to give her son "artistic genes".<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qRpxLdn7C4EC&pg=PA124 |title=Visual authorship: creativity and intentionality in media |last2=Laursen |first2=Iben Thorving |publisher=Museum Tusculanum Press |year=2005 |isbn=978-87-635-0128-6 |page=124 |last1=Grodal |first1=Torben Kragh |access-date=11 October 2010 |archive-date=5 June 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130605005625/http://books.google.com/books?id=qRpxLdn7C4EC&pg=PA124 |url-status=live }}</ref> Trier has jokingly said, by reference to the distant German origin of the Hartmann family, that while he believed he had a Jewish background, he is "really more of a Nazi."<ref name="Nicodemus">{{cite news |url=http://www.signandsight.com/features/465.html |title=Lars von Trier, Katja Nicodemus: 'I am an American woman' (17/11/2005) – signandsight |last=Nicodemus |first=Katja |date=10 November 2005 |work=[[Die Zeit]] |access-date=14 October 2010 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120910/http://www.signandsight.com/features/465.html |archive-date=10 September 2012 |url-status=live}}</ref>

During the [[German occupation of Denmark]], Hartmann in fact joined a [[Danish resistance movement|resistance group]], actively counteracting any pro-German and pro-Nazi colleagues in his civil service department.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://modstand.natmus.dk/Person.aspx?43138 |title=Entry on Fritz Michael Hartmann in the Database of the Danish Resistance Movement |language=da |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120526/http://modstand.natmus.dk/Person.aspx?43138 |archive-date=26 May 2012 |url-status=live }}</ref> Another member of this resistance group was Hartmann's colleague [[Viggo Kampmann]], who would later become prime minister of Denmark.<ref>{{cite journal |year=2004 |title=Viggo Kampmann under besættelsen |url=http://130.225.142.181/fileadmin/saxo-abstract-uploads/viggo_kampmann_under_besaettelsen_2004_4.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110810135641/http://130.225.142.181/fileadmin/saxo-abstract-uploads/viggo_kampmann_under_besaettelsen_2004_4.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=10 August 2011 |journal=Siden Saxo |language=da |issue=4 |page=39 |last1=Skov |first1=Jesper |access-date=21 May 2011}}</ref> After Trier had four awkward meetings with his biological father, Hartmann refused further contact.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.smh.com.au/articles/2003/12/22/1071941658741.html |title=Stranger and fiction |date=22 December 2003 |work=The Sydney Morning Herald |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120912/http://www.smh.com.au/articles/2003/12/22/1071941658741.html |archive-date=12 September 2012 |url-status=live }}</ref>

From 1987 to 1995, Trier was married to producer and actress {{ill|Cæcilia Holbek|da|Cæcilia Holbek Trier}}, with whom he has two daughters, Agnes and Selma (both producers like their parents), and from 1997 to 2015 to Bente Frøge, with whom he has two sons.

=== Family background and political and religious views ===
Trier's mother considered herself a [[Communism|communist]], while Ulf Trier was a [[Social democracy|social democrat]]. Both were committed [[Naturist|nudist]]s, and Trier went on several childhood holidays to [[Nudist community|nudist camp]]s. They regarded the disciplining of children as reactionary. Trier has noted that he was brought up in an [[atheism|atheist]] family, and that although Ulf Trier was Jewish, he was not religious. His parents did not allow much room in their household for "feelings, religion, or enjoyment", and also refused to make any rules for their children.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://visit-copenhagen.com/about-copenhagen/lars-von-trier.htm |title=Copenhagen: Lars von Trier |publisher=Visit-copenhagen.com |access-date=15 July 2010 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120716/http://visit-copenhagen.com/about-copenhagen/lars-von-trier.htm |archive-date=16 July 2012 |url-status=dead  }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.signandsight.com/features/465.html |title=Lars von Trier, Katja Nicodemus: 'I am an American woman' (17/11/2005) – signandsight |last=Nicodemus |first=Katja |date=10 November 2005 |work=[[Die Zeit]] |quote=I come from a family of communist nudists. I was allowed to do or not do what I liked. My parents were not interested in whether I went to school or got drunk on white wine. After a childhood like that, you search for restrictions in your own life. |access-date=14 October 2010 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120910/http://www.signandsight.com/features/465.html |archive-date=10 September 2012 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In a 2005 interview with ''[[Die Zeit]]'', Trier said, "I don't know if I'm all that Catholic really. I'm probably not. Denmark is a very [[Protestant]] country. Perhaps I only turned [[Catholic Church|Catholic]] to piss off a few of my countrymen."<ref name="Nicodemus" /> In 2009, he said, "I'm a very bad Catholic. In fact I'm becoming more and more of an atheist."<ref>Fielder, Miles (4 August 2009). {{cite web |url=http://www.bigissuescotland.com/features/view/104 |title=Lars von Trier |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090818042256/http://www.bigissuescotland.com/features/view/104 |archive-date=18 August 2009 |url-status=dead |access-date=11 September 2011}}. ''The Big Issue Scotland''. Retrieved 11 September 2011.</ref>

In August 2023, Trier published on [[Instagram]] a critical entry against the delivery of [[General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon|F-16]] fighters to [[Ukraine]], ending his post by saying "Russian lives matter also!"<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|title=Lars von Trier defends 'Russian lives matter also' comment|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2023/aug/25/lars-von-trier-defends-russian-lives-matter-also-comment|work=The Guardian|date=2023-08-25|access-date=2025-11-29|issn=0261-3077|language=en-GB|first=Sian|last=Cain}}</ref> The entry immediately became publicized in official [[Russia]]n media and by the Russian media executive [[Margarita Simonyan]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=ČTK |title=Lars von Trier zaujal Kyjev i Moskvu výrokem, že na ruských životech také záleží {{!}} ČeskéNoviny.cz |url=https://www.ceskenoviny.cz/zpravy/lars-von-trier-zaujal-kyjev-i-moskvu-vyrokem-ze-na-ruskych-zivotech-take-zalezi/2404508 |website=www.ceskenoviny.cz |access-date=23 September 2023 |language=cs}}</ref> [[Oleksiy Danilov]], head of Ukraine's [[National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine|National Security and Defense Council]], responded on [[Twitter]], criticising Trier's comments, saying, "The choice between the executioner and the victim becomes a tragedy when the artist chooses the side of the executioner."<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{cite web |last1=Murray |first1=Tom |title=Ukrainian official eviscerates Lars von Trier for 'Russian lives also matter' post |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/news/lars-von-trier-movies-russia-twitter-b2398520.html |website=The Independent |access-date=23 September 2023 |language=en |date=24 August 2023}}</ref> Two days later, Trier then made another post on Instagram, saying, "I support Ukraine with every beat of my heart! I was just stating the obvious: that all lives in this world matter!"<ref name=":2" />

=== Health ===
====Mental health====
Trier suffers from various fears and [[phobia]]s, including an intense [[fear of flying]]. This fear frequently places severe constraints on him and his crew, necessitating that virtually all of his films be shot in either Denmark or Sweden.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2007/may/13/film.filmnews |title=Guardian UK interview 2007 |last=Burke |first=Jason |date=13 May 2007 |work=[[The Guardian]] |location=London, England |access-date=5 September 2010 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120920/http://www.guardian.co.uk/world/2007/may/13/film.filmnews |archive-date=20 September 2012 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On numerous occasions, he has stated that he suffers from occasional [[major depressive disorder|depression]] which renders him incapable of doing his work and unable to fulfill social obligations.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lR6sIjOBE_AC&pg=PA118 |title=Global auteurs: politics in the films of Almodóvar, von Trier, and Winterbottom |last=Goss |first=Brian Michael |date=2009 |publisher=[[Peter Lang (publisher)|Peter Lang]] |location=Bern, Switzerland |isbn=978-1-4331-0134-2 |page=118 |access-date=11 October 2010 |archive-date=6 June 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130606040813/http://books.google.com/books?id=lR6sIjOBE_AC&pg=PA118 |url-status=live}}</ref>

====Parkinson's disease====
On 8 August 2022, it was announced that Trier had been diagnosed with [[Parkinson's disease]].<ref>{{cite news|url = https://deadline.com/2022/08/lars-von-trier-parkinsons-disease-1235087333/|title = Lars Von Trier Diagnosed With Parkinson's Disease, Work On 'The Kingdom Exodus' Continues|work = [[Deadline Hollywood]]|date = 8 August 2022|accessdate = 8 August 2022|last = Goodfellow|first = Melanie|archive-date = 8 August 2022|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20220808171204/https://deadline.com/2022/08/lars-von-trier-parkinsons-disease-1235087333/|url-status = live}}</ref> According to ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'', Trier plans to take a break from filmmaking to adjust to his new life with the disease, saying: "I will take a little break and find out what to do, but I certainly hope that my condition will be better. It's a disease you can't take away; you can work with the symptoms, though."<ref>{{Cite magazine |title=Lars von Trier on Working With Parkinson's Disease: 'I Just Have to Get Used to That I Shake and Not Be Shameful in Front of People' |first=Naman |last=Ramachandran |url=https://variety.com/2022/tv/global/lars-von-trier-parkinsons-disease-the-kingdom-exodus-1235356789/ |date=1 September 2022 |access-date=2022-11-25 |magazine=Variety}}</ref> On 12 February 2025, [[Zentropa]] producer [[Louise Vesth]] announced via [[Instagram]] that Trier had been admitted to a care facility for the condition.<ref>{{Cite news |last=AFP |date=2025-02-12 |title=Lars von Trier admitted to a care centre following Parkinson's diagnosis |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2025/feb/12/lars-von-trier-admitted-to-a-care-centre-following-parkinsons-diagnosis |access-date=2025-02-14 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB}}</ref>

=== Frequent collaborators ===
Trier often works more than once with actors and production members. [[Manon Rasmussen]] was the only crew member as a costume designer to collaborate with Trier in all of his works (except ''[[Medea (1988 film)|Medea]]'' and ''[[The Idiots (1998 film)|The Idiots]]'') since ''[[The Element of Crime]]'' (1984). His first, but initial acting collaborator for ''[[The Element of Crime]]'' was [[:sv:Leif Magnusson|Leif Magnusson]], who appeared in his role as a hotel guest, yet continued to appear again in the last two films as different minor roles for his first trilogy until his acting retirement in the early 1990s. His main crew members and producer team has remained intact since [[Europa (1991 film)|''Europa'']]. Many of his recurring actors have expressed their devotion<ref name="skarsgard">{{Cite Trier.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.elle.com/culture/celebrities/news/a7745/kirsten-dunst-on-lars-von-trier-feeling-free-32465/ |title=Kirsten Dunst on Lars von Trier & Feeling Free |date=11 == Awards and honors ==
{{Main|List of awards and nominations received by Lars von Trier}}
Among his more than 100 awards and 200 nominations at film festivals worldwide, Trier has received: the [[Palme d'Or]] (for ''[[Dancer in the Dark]]''), the [[Grand Prix (Cannes Film Festival)|Grand Prix]] (for ''[[Breaking the Waves]]''), the [[Jury Prize (Cannes Film Festival)|Prix du Jury]] (for ''[[Europa (1991 film)|Europa]]''), and the Technical Grand Prize (for ''[[The Element of Crime]]'' and ''Europa'') at the [[Cannes Film Festival]]. Trier has also received both [[Golden Globe Awards|Golden Globe Award]] and [[Academy Awards|Academy Award]] nominations for the former.

* In Trier's second trilogy, ''Golden Heart'', is the first franchise or trilogy to have won both [[Bodil Award for Best Actress in a Leading Role|Bodil]] and [[Robert Award for Best Actress in a Leading Role|Robert]] for Best Actress in a Leading Role, respectively [[Emily Watson]], [[Bodil Jørgensen|Bodil Jorgensen]], and [[Björk]], while Watson and Björk also have won the [[European Film Award for Best Actress|European]] for Best Actress.{{citation needed|date=September 2024}}
** Also in ''Golden Heart'', three of them have nominated the [[Palme d'Or]], with the latter won.{{citation needed|date=September 2024}}
* In Trier's fourth trilogy, ''Depression'', is the first franchise or trilogy to have sweep the Robert for [[Robert Award for Best Danish Film|Best Danish Film]], [[Robert Award for Best Director|Best Director]], [[Robert Award for Best Screenplay|Best Screenplay]], [[Robert Award for Best Cinematography|Best Cinematography]], [[Robert Award for Best Editing|Best Editing]], [[Robert Award for Best Sound Design|Best Sound]], and [[Robert Award for Best Visual Effects|Best Visual Effects]].{{citation needed|date=September 2024}}

======================================================================
WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE: List of 20th-century films considered the worst
======================================================================

{{Short description|none}}
{{about|films considered the worst from the 20th century|21st-century films considered the worst|List of 21st-century films considered the worst|other uses|Lists of films considered the worst}}
{{protection padlock|reason=Persistent [[WP:Disruptive editing|disruptive editing]]|small=yes}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=November 2022}}
{{Use American English|date=March 2023}}
{{Dynamic list}}
[[File:Reefer Madness (1936).jpg|220px|thumb|''[[Reefer Madness]]'' (1936), one of the earliest films to garner particularly negative reviews<ref name="psmag">{{cite magazine|last=Lincoln|first=Kevin|title=The Benefits of Being the Worst Movie Ever Made|url=https://psmag.com/economics/benefits-worst-movie-ever-made-84813|access-date=October 23, 2017|magazine=[[Pacific Standard]]|date=July 2, 2014|archive-date=October 23, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023115728/https://psmag.com/economics/benefits-worst-movie-ever-made-84813|url-status=live}}</ref>]]

The [[film]]s listed below have been ranked by a number of critics in varying media sources as being among the worst films ever made in the 20th century. Examples of such sources include [[Metacritic]], [[Roger Ebert]]'s list of most-hated films, ''[[The Golden Turkey Awards]]'', ''[[Leonard Maltin's Movie Guide]]'', [[Rotten Tomatoes]], [[pop culture]] writer [[Nathan Rabin]]'s ''[[My Year of Flops|My World of Flops]]'', the [[Stinkers Bad Movie Awards]], the cult TV series ''[[Mystery Science Theater 3000]]'' (alongside spinoffs ''[[Cinematic Titanic]]'', ''[[The Film Crew]]'' and ''[[RiffTrax]]''), and the [[Golden Raspberry Awards]] (aka the "Razzies"). Films on these lists are generally [[feature film|feature-length films]] that are [[commerce|commercial]]/[[art film|artistic]] in nature (intended to turn a profit, express personal statements or both), professionally or independently produced (as opposed to [[amateur]] productions, such as [[home movie]]s), and released in theaters, then on home video. There are 57 films listed below, with 103 across both lists.

== 1930s ==

=== ''Maniac'' (1934) ===
{{Main|Maniac (1934 film){{!}}''Maniac'' (1934 film)}}
[[File:Maniac5.jpg|thumb|''[[Maniac (1934 film)|Maniac]]'' (1934) is one of the many [[pre-Code]] exploitation films from the 1930s featuring sex, violence and drugs.]]
''Maniac'', also known as ''Sex Maniac'', is a [[pre-Code]] [[exploitation film|exploitation]]-[[horror film]] directed by [[Dwain Esper]]. The story is a loose adaptation of the [[Edgar Allan Poe]] story "[[The Black Cat (short story)|The Black Cat]]" and follows a [[vaudeville]] impersonator who becomes an assistant to a [[mad scientist]]. Promoted as a documentary on [[mental illness]], ''Maniac'' was criticized for its gratuitous footage of women undressing and for plagiarizing horror sequences from the 1922 silent film ''[[Häxan]]''. [[Danny Peary]] believes that ''Maniac'' is the worst film ever made, and [[Charlie Jane Anders]] of [[Gawker Media]]{{'}}s ''[[io9]]'' described it as "possibly the worst movie in history."<ref>{{Cite book|last=Peary|first=Danny|author-link=Danny Peary|title=Cult Midnight Movies: Discover the 37 Best Weird, Sleazy, Sexy, and Crazy Good Cinema Classics|publisher=[[Workman Publishing Company]]|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=TTsPBAAAQBAJ&q=Maniac+%281934%29+Dwain+Esper|year=2014|isbn=9780761181699|access-date=October 2, 2020|archive-date=October 25, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231025172439/https://books.google.com/books?id=TTsPBAAAQBAJ&q=Maniac+%281934%29+Dwain+Esper#v=snippet&q=Maniac%20(1934)%20Dwain%20Esper&f=false|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://io9.gizmodo.com/did-the-worst-movie-of-all-time-come-out-75-years-ago-5161275 |title=Did The Worst Movie Of All Time Come Out 75 Years Ago? |publisher=[[io9]] |last=Anders |first=Charlie Jane |date=February 26, 2009 |access-date=February 18, 2019 |archive-date=February 18, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190218201930/https://io9.gizmodo.com/did-the-worst-movie-of-all-time-come-out-75-years-ago-5161275 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Rotten Tomatoes]] placed ''Maniac'' on its list of movies "So Bad They're Unmissable",<ref name="sobad">{{cite web |url=https://editorial.rottentomatoes.com/article/25-movies-so-bad-theyre-unmissable/|title=25 Movies So Bad They're Unmissable |last=Adams |first=Michael |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |publisher=[[Fandango Media|Fandango]] |date=January 30, 2010 |access-date=January 25, 2015 }}</ref> ''[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]'' included the film on its list of the 20 worst movies ever and it is featured in [[John J. B. Wilson]]'s book ''[[The Official Razzie Movie Guide: Enjoying the Best of Hollywood's Worst]]''.<ref name="italianvanity">{{cite news|url=https://www.vanityfair.it/show/cinema/2018/02/25/20-film-piu-brutti-di-sempre|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220108083603/https://www.vanityfair.it/show/cinema/2018/02/25/20-film-piu-brutti-di-sempre |work=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]|title=I 20 film più brutti di sempre|last=Pellegrini|first=Francesca|language=it|date=February 25, 2018|access-date=February 18, 2019|archive-date=January 8, 2022}}</ref>

=== ''Reefer Madness'' (1936) ===
{{Main|Reefer Madness{{!}}''Reefer Madness''}}
[[File:ReeferMadness_13.jpg|thumb|Originally titled ''Tell Your Children'', the anti-[[cannabis (drug)|cannabis]] film ''[[Reefer Madness]]'' was called "the grand-daddy of all 'Worst' movies" by [[Leonard Maltin]].]]
''Reefer Madness'' (originally released as ''Tell Your Children'' and sometimes titled or subtitled as ''The Burning Question'', ''Dope Addict'', ''Doped Youth'', and ''Love Madness'') is a 1936 American [[exploitation film]] and [[propaganda|propaganda work]] revolving around the melodramatic events that ensue when high school students are lured by pushers to smoke [[cannabis (drug)|cannabis]] and consequently become addicted and involved in various crimes such as a [[Hit and run (vehicular)|hit and run accident]], [[manslaughter]], [[murder]], attempted rape, descent into madness, association with organized crime, and suicide.

''[[Pacific Standard]]'' wrote that ''Reefer Madness'' was "one of the first films ever to be considered transcendentally bad"<ref name="psmag"/> and [[Leonard Maltin]] has called it "the grand-daddy of all 'Worst' movies".<ref name="Maltin01211">{{cite book |last=Maltin |first=Leonard |author-link=Leonard Maltin |title=Leonard Maltin's Movie and Video Guide 2004 |publisher=Signet |year=2003 |isbn=0-451-20940-0 |url=https://archive.org/details/leonardmaltinsmo00leon }}</ref> <!--Dead source, no archive available except the deprecated archive.today, thus [[WP:V|unverifiable]]: ''[[Las Vegas CityLife]]'' named it the "worst ever" runner-up to ''[[Plan 9 from Outer Space]]'',<ref>{{cite news |url=http://archives.lasvegascitylife.com/articles/2009/09/24/ae/stage/iq_31362594.txt |date=September 24, 2009 |last=McKee |first=David |work=Las Vegas CityLife |access-date=November 17, 2013 |title=What's the Worst Movie Ever? }}</ref> and--> [[News.com.au]] considered it a "disastrous flop turned cult classic" due to its "terrible acting and exaggerated drug-addicted stereotypes".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.news.com.au/national/nsw-act/when-hollywoods-worst-films-become-cult-classics/news-story/792f3f09aba66809245d65328c73921c|title=When Hollywood's worst films become cult classics|work=[[News.com.au]]|first=Troy|last=Lennon|date=December 7, 2017|access-date=January 20, 2019|archive-date=January 21, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190121064145/https://www.news.com.au/national/nsw-act/when-hollywoods-worst-films-become-cult-classics/news-story/792f3f09aba66809245d65328c73921c|url-status=live}}</ref> Natalli Amato of ''[[The Daily Dot]]'' included ''Reefer Madness'' on her list of the best worst movies, writing that it "may be one of the worst movies of all time for the fact that it accomplished the exact opposite of its intended goal" by becoming a cult classic among stoners.<ref>{{cite web |last=St-Amand |first=Vanessa |title=Ranked: The best worst movies you need to watch |url=https://www.dailydot.com/upstream/best-worst-movies/ |website=[[The Daily Dot]] |access-date=July 8, 2022 |date=March 29, 2022 |archive-date=June 19, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220619224037/https://www.dailydot.com/upstream/best-worst-movies/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[Leafly]]''{{'}}s Danté Jordan also wrote that it may be "the worst movie of all time", criticizing its many inaccuracies regarding marijuana use and calling it "easily one of the most uncreative and [[tone-deaf]] pieces of anti-cannabis propaganda".<ref>{{cite web |last=Jordan |first=Danté |title=We watched 'Reefer Madness' to confirm it's still complete garbage |url=https://www.leafly.com/news/lifestyle/reasons-why-reefer-madness-is-complete-garbage |website=[[Leafly]] |access-date=July 8, 2022 |language=en |date=January 27, 2020 |archive-date=July 8, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220708065233/https://www.leafly.com/news/lifestyle/reasons-why-reefer-madness-is-complete-garbage |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== ''The Terror of Tiny Town'' (1938) ===
{{Main|The Terror of Tiny Town{{!}}''The Terror of Tiny Town''}}
''The Terror of Tiny Town'', directed by [[Sam Newfield]] and produced by [[Jed Buell]], remains the only [[musical film|musical]] [[Western (genre)|Western]] with an all-[[Dwarfism|dwarf]] cast.<ref name="tinyterror"/> The film was pulled from obscurity as a [[camp (style)|camp classic]] after appearing in college and [[midnight film|midnight screenings]] in the early 1970s.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Terror of Tiny Town (1938)|url=https://www.tcm.com/tcmdb/title/92598/the-terror-of-tiny-town|access-date=December 16, 2020|website=Turner Classic Movies|language=en|archive-date=June 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210614012516/https://www.tcm.com/tcmdb/title/92598/the-terror-of-tiny-town|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 1978, it was included in [[Michael Medved]]'s book ''[[The Fifty Worst Films of All Time]]'',<ref name="tinyterror">{{cite web|url=https://filmthreat.com/uncategorized/the-terror-of-tiny-town-dvd/|title=The Terror of Tiny Town (DVD)|work=Film Threat|date=June 17, 2005|access-date=March 23, 2020|archive-date=March 24, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200324034956/https://filmthreat.com/uncategorized/the-terror-of-tiny-town-dvd/|url-status=live}}</ref> and it has since been listed as one of the worst films ever made by ''[[Flavorwire]]'',<ref name="Flavorwire"/> Rotten Tomatoes,<ref name="sobad"/> and ''[[The Golden Turkey Awards]]''.<ref name="tinyterror"/> [[Melvin Defleur]] referred to it as "Perhaps the worst film of all time",<ref>{{Cite book|last=Defleur|first=Melvin|author-link=Melvin Defleur|title=Understanding Mass Communication: A Liberal Arts Perspective|publisher=[[Houghton Mifflin Harcourt]]|edition=6|year=1998|page=160}}</ref> and critic Gabriel Ricard listed it as the worst film ever made; stating, "not only is it pretty terrible, but ''Tiny Town'' is also pretty endearing."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://culturedvultures.com/best-worst-movies/|title=20 Best Worst Movies Of All Time|work=Cultured Vultures|last=Richard|first=Gabriel|date=June 5, 2019|access-date=March 23, 2020|archive-date=December 9, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191209080410/https://culturedvultures.com/best-worst-movies/|url-status=live}}</ref> In 1986, ''The Terror of Tiny Town'' was the first film featured on ''[[Canned Film Festival]]'', a [[late night television]] show featuring the worst movies ever made.<ref name="cannedfilm">{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1986-06-20-8602140300-story.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220507001443/https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1986-06-20-8602140300-story.html|title=A 'Terror' Kicks Off World's Worst Film Festival|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|last=Terry|first=Clifford|date=June 20, 1989|access-date=March 23, 2020|archive-date=May 7, 2022}}</ref>

== 1940s ==

=== ''The Babe Ruth Story'' (1948) ===
{{Main|The Babe Ruth Story{{!}}''The Babe Ruth Story''}}
[[File:William_Bendix_1960.JPG|thumb|left|upright|Actor [[William Bendix]], who played The Great Bambino in ''[[The Babe Ruth Story]]'' (1948), cited as one of the worst [[biopics]] ever made]]
''The Babe Ruth Story'' is a 1948 [[baseball film]] biography of [[Babe Ruth]], starring [[William Bendix]], [[Claire Trevor]] and [[Sam Levene]].<ref>{{Citation|last1=Del Ruth|first1=Roy|title=The Babe Ruth story|date=2010|publisher=Warner Home Video|language=en|oclc=694103117|last2=Considine|first2=Bob|last3=Callahan|first3=George|last4=Bendix|first4=William|last5=Trevor|first5=Claire|last6=Bickford|first6=Charles|last7=Frawley|first7=William|last8=Levene|first8=Sam|last9=Allied Artists Productions}}</ref> ''[[The New York Times]]'' describes it as "the ''[[Plan 9 from Outer Space]]'' of baseball biopics".<ref>{{cite news |title=The Babe Ruth Story (1948)|url=https://www.nytimes.com/movies/movie/3535/The-Babe-Ruth-Story/overview |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131219200719/http://www.nytimes.com/movies/movie/3535/The-Babe-Ruth-Story/overview |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 19, 2013 |department=Movies & TV Dept.|work=[[The New York Times]]|first=Hal|last=Erickson|author-link=Hal Erickson (author)|date=2013|access-date=November 30, 2013}}</ref> It was rushed into release while Ruth was still alive. One infamous scene features Ruth promising a dying child that he will hit two [[home run]]s; the child is subsequently cured of his ailments after Ruth delivers on the promise.<ref name="homerun"/>

[[Baseball Hall of Fame]]r [[Ted Williams]] believed it to be the worst movie he had ever seen. ''[[The Washington Times]]'' stated that it "stands as possibly the worst movie ever made".<ref>{{cite news |title=Duke as Williams? A Prince of an Idea |first=Dan |last=Shaughnessy |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=XscSAAAAIBAJ&pg=7230,788739&dq=babe+ruth+story+worst+film |newspaper=Spokane Chronicle |date=April 3, 1986 |access-date=November 30, 2013 |archive-date=August 16, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220816054117/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=XscSAAAAIBAJ&pg=7230,788739&dq=babe+ruth+story+worst+film |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Heller |first=Dick |title=Clinic and reception in the works to honor NBA pioneer Lloyd |newspaper=The Washington Times |date=July 23, 2000 |url-access=subscription |url=http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=WT&p_theme=wt&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0EB08BFA289BE4FB&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D |access-date=November 30, 2013 |archive-date=November 1, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181101055233/http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=WT&p_theme=wt&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0EB08BFA289BE4FB&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[The Spokesman-Review]]'' included the film on its list of the worst films of all time, while Paul Newberry of the [[Associated Press]] wrote that the film's place on "nearly every list of the worst movies ever made" was "with good reason".<ref>{{cite web |last=Apple |first=Charles |title=Some of the worst movies of all-time |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2020/sep/22/some-worst-movies-all-time/ |website=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |access-date=July 10, 2022 |language=en |date=September 22, 2020 |archive-date=July 10, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220710190457/https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2020/sep/22/some-worst-movies-all-time/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Newberry |first=Paul |title=Counting down baseball's worst movie locales |url=https://www.providencejournal.com/story/sports/2019/08/10/counting-down-baseballs-worst-movie-locales/4492519007/ |website=[[The Providence Journal]] |access-date=July 10, 2022 |date=August 10, 2019 |archive-date=June 25, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220625165504/https://www.providencejournal.com/story/sports/2019/08/10/counting-down-baseballs-worst-movie-locales/4492519007/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[Newsday]]''{{'}}s Jack Mathews similarly wrote that ''The Babe Ruth Story'' was "what many people consider to be the worst sports movie of all time".<ref>{{cite journal |last=Dunne |first=Michael |title=Post-War Cultural Construction in "The Babe Ruth Story" |journal=Studies in Popular Culture |date=October 1996 |volume=19 |issue=1 |pages=1–7 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23413739 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220710190457/https://www.jstor.org/stable/23413739 |url-status=live }}</ref> It also was called one of the worst sports films ever, by both ''Newsday'' and ''[[The A.V. Club]]'',<ref>{{cite news |last=Isaacs |first=Stan |title=Out ofLeft Field – The 10 Worst Sports Movies Of All Time |newspaper=Newsday |date=February 26, 1989 |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/278087041 |access-date=November 30, 2013 |archive-date=December 3, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203051629/http://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/newsday/doc/278087041.html?FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT&type=current&date=Feb%2026,%201989&author=Stan%20Isaacs&pub=Newsday%20%28Combined%20editions%29&edition=&startpage=&desc=OUT%20OF%20LEFT%20FIELD%20The%2010%20Worst%20Sports%20Movies%20Of%20All%20Time |id={{ProQuest|278087041}} |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="homerun">{{Cite web|url=https://www.avclub.com/the-home-run-that-cured-cancer-16-amazing-movie-sports-1798214998|title=The home run that cured cancer: 16 Amazing Movie Sports Feats|last1=Mincher|first1=Chris|last2=Bahn|first2=Christopher|date=October 6, 2008|website=[[The A.V. === ''No Orchids for Miss Blandish'' (1948) ===
{{Main|No Orchids for Miss Blandish (film){{!}}''No Orchids for Miss Blandish'' (film)}}
''No Orchids for Miss Blandish'', a British [[gangster film]] adapted from the 1939 [[No Orchids for Miss Blandish (novel)|novel]] by [[James Hadley Chase]], received a very hostile reception from the press. This was mainly due to the film's high (for the time) implied level of violence and rape, but also because its attempt to portray Americans using a largely British cast (including an early role for [[Sid James]])<ref name="goodwin">{{cite book |first=Cliff |last=Goodwin |title=Sid James: A Biography |publisher=Random House |year=2011 |isbn=978-0-7535-4682-6 |pages=67–68 }}</ref> was seen as unconvincing.<ref name="bmc">{{cite book |last=McFarlane |first=Brian |year=1999 |chapter=Outrage: No Orchids for Miss Blandish |title=British Crime Cinema |editor-first=Steve |editor-last=Chibnall |editor-first2=Robert |editor-last2=Murphy |publisher=Routledge |isbn=0-415-16870-8 |pages=37–50 }}</ref>

The British film journal ''[[Monthly Film Bulletin]]'' called it "the most sickening exhibition of brutality, perversion, sex and sadism ever to be shown on a cinema screen".<ref name="bmc"/> The ''[[Sunday Express]]'' film reviewer called ''No Orchids for Miss Blandish'' "the worst film I have ever seen".<ref name="hfg">{{cite book |title=Halliwell's Film Guide |publisher=HarperPerennial |year=1994 |isbn=978-0-06-273318-4 |page=781 }}</ref> The Australian newspaper ''[[The Age]]'' also gave a harsh review: "''No Orchids for Miss Blandish'' is not only a disgrace to the studio that made it, but it also reflects on the British industry as a whole ... the entire production is unpardonable."<ref>{{cite news |title=Question of Propriety for the Censor |url=https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/205685128/19598563 |access-date=2024-12-13 |work=The Age |date=1948-11-27 |location=Melbourne |page=9 |via=Trove}}</ref>

Cliff Goodwin, discussing ''No Orchids for Miss Blandish''{{'}}s initial reception, notes it was "unanimously dubbed 'the worst film ever made{{'"}}.<ref name="goodwin"/> Later reviews of the film were equally antipathetic. ''No Orchids for Miss Blandish'' was described by British film reviewer [[Leslie Halliwell]] as a "hilariously awful gangster film ... one of the worst films ever made".<ref name="hfg"/> ''[[Leonard Maltin's Movie Guide|Leonard Maltin's Classic Movie Guide]]'' states that ''No Orchids for Miss Blandish'' "aspires to be a Hollywood [[film noir]] and misses by a mile."<ref>{{cite book |last=Maltin |first=Leonard |year=2011 |title=Leonard Maltin's Classic Movie Guide: From The Silent Era Through 1965 |edition=Second |publisher=Penguin |isbn=978-0-452-29577-3 |page=474 }}</ref>

Despite (or because) of the condemnation, the film was commercially successful<ref>"Outrage: No Orchids for Miss Blandish" by Brian McFarlane in ''British Crime Cinema'', edited by Steve Chibnall, Robert Murphy. Routledge, 1999. {{ISBN|0-415-16870-8}} (pg. 37-50).</ref> and broke box office records in Britain in areas where it was not banned.<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=xtGIAgAAQBAJ&dq=hungry+hill+film+box+office&pg=PA209 Robert Murphy, ''Realism and Tinsel: Cinema and Society in Britain 1939-48'' 2003 p210]</ref>

== 1950s ==

=== ''Glen or Glenda'' (1953) ===
{{Main|Glen or Glenda{{!}}''Glen or Glenda''}}
''Glen or Glenda'' starred [[Ed Wood]] as Glen, a transvestite who cross-dresses as Glenda. Wood also directed the film. After a [[dream sequence]], Glen undergoes psychotherapy to help "cure" him of his [[transvestism]].

[[Leonard Maltin]] wrote that ''Glen or Glenda'' was worse than Wood's later ''[[Plan 9 from Outer Space]]'' and considered it "possibly the worst movie ever made".<ref name="Maltin01211"/> Julien Allen of ''[[IndieWire|Reverse Shot]]'' similarly wrote that it was "widely considered to be an atrocity" and "the most catastrophic failure of [Wood's] singularly bad career".<ref>{{cite web |last=Allen |first=Julien |title=Simply the Worst: Edward D. Wood Jr.'s 'Glen or Glenda?' |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2011/09/simply-the-worst-edward-d-wood-jr-s-glen-or-glenda-224683/ |website=[[IndieWire]] |access-date=July 8, 2022 |language=en |date=September 7, 2011 |archive-date=July 8, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220708193054/https://www.indiewire.com/2011/09/simply-the-worst-edward-d-wood-jr-s-glen-or-glenda-224683/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Richard Barrios described ''Glen or Glenda'' as "one of the funniest and worst movies ever made".<ref>Richard Barrios, ''Screened Out: Playing Gay in Hollywood from Edison to Stonewall'', Psychology Press, 2003, {{ISBN|0-415-92328-X}}, Page 235.</ref>

=== ''Robot Monster'' (1953) ===
{{Main|Robot Monster{{!}}''Robot Monster''}}
''Robot Monster'' is a [[science-fiction film]] produced and directed by [[Phil Tucker]] and originally shot and exhibited in [[3-D film|3D]]. Its title character, which is "a man in a gorilla suit wearing what looks like a diving helmet sprouting TV antennae", was given the Most Ridiculous Monster in Screen History award in ''The Golden Turkey Awards''.<ref name="newcastlerobot"/> It is also featured in ''[[The Book of Lists]]''{{'}} 10 worst movies list,{{sfn|Book of Lists|page=208}} ''The Fifty Worst Films of All Time'' and Michael Sauter's book ''The Worst Movies of All Time''.{{sfn|Sauter|page=326}}<ref name="newcastlerobot">{{cite web |last=Cerabona |first=Ron |title=So bad it's good: retro sci-fi's monster appeal |url=https://www.newcastleherald.com.au/story/449342/so-bad-its-good-retro-sci-fis-monster-appeal/ |website=[[The Newcastle Herald]] |access-date=July 22, 2022 |language=en-AU |date=October 30, 2012 |archive-date=July 22, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220722140503/https://www.newcastleherald.com.au/story/449342/so-bad-its-good-retro-sci-fis-monster-appeal/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Robot Monster'' was featured in an episode of the movie-mocking TV show ''[[Mystery Science Theater 3000]]'',<ref name="newcastlerobot"/> as well as ''Canned Film Festival''.<ref name="cannedfilm"/> The film is remembered fondly by horror novelist [[Stephen King]], who quotes, and agrees with, a review in ''[[Castle of Frankenstein]]'' magazine ("certainly among the finest terrible movies ever made", "one of the most laughable [[Poverty Row|poverty row]] quickies").<ref>{{cite book |first=Stephen |last=King |author-link=Stephen King |title=Danse Macabre |year=1981 |publisher=Everest House |location=New York |isbn=978-0-89696-076-3|title-link=Danse Macabre (King book) }}</ref> Chris Barsanti in ''The Sci-Fi Movie Guide'' writes: "[''Robot Monster''] gives ''Plan 9 From Outer Space'' a run as the worst movie of all time."<ref>{{cite book |last=Barsanti |first=Chris |title=The Sci-Fi Movie Guide: The Universe of Film from Alien to Zardoz |date=2014 |publisher=[[Visible Ink Press]] |isbn=978-1578595334 |pages=312}}</ref>

=== ''The Conqueror'' (1956) ===
{{Main|The Conqueror (1956 film){{!}}''The Conqueror'' (1956 film)}}
[[File:The_Conqueror_(1956)_film_poster.jpg|thumb|The 1956 [[epic film|film epic]] ''[[The Conqueror (1956 film)|The Conqueror]]'' featured [[John Wayne]] as Asian warlord [[Genghis Khan]], cited as one of the most miscast roles ever<ref name="terrible10">{{cite web |last=Walters |first=Jack |title=10 Terrible Movies You Don't Have To See To Know They're Bad |url=https://screenrant.com/terrible-movies-not-see-know-bad/ |website=[[Screen Rant]] |access-date=March 29, 2024 |language=en |date=26 July 2023}}</ref>]]
[[Howard Hughes]] funded ''[[The Conqueror (1956 film)|The Conqueror]]'', an [[epic film]] featuring [[John Wayne]] as [[Mongolia]]n chieftain [[Genghis Khan]] and the redheaded [[Susan Hayward]] as a [[Tatars|Tatar]] princess. The movie was filmed near [[St. George, Utah]], downwind from a [[Nevada Test Site|nuclear testing range]] in [[Nevada]], and is often blamed for the [[cancer]] deaths of many of the cast and crew, including Hayward, Wayne, [[Agnes Moorehead]], [[Pedro Armendáriz]], and director [[Dick Powell]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Adams |first=Cecil |title=Did John Wayne die of cancer caused by a radioactive movie set? |publisher=The Straight Dope |date=October 26, 1984 |url=http://www.straightdope.com/classics/a2_016.html |access-date=March 7, 2011 |archive-date=July 3, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080703225341/http://www.straightdope.com/classics/a2_016.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> In addition to filming near the testing range, truckloads of the red sands were transported back to the studios for interior scenes<ref name="telekhan"/> and by 1980, 91 of the 220 (over 41%) cast and crew members had been diagnosed with cancer.<ref name=geng>{{cite news|last=von Tunzelmann|first=Alex|title=The Conqueror: Hollywood gives Genghis Khan a kicking he won't forget|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/filmblog/2013/may/03/the-conqueror-hollywood-genghis-khan|newspaper=The Guardian|date=May 3, 2013|location=London|access-date=December 12, 2016|archive-date=June 23, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130623112047/http://www.guardian.co.uk/film/filmblog/2013/may/03/the-conqueror-hollywood-genghis-khan|url-status=live}}</ref>

The film made the ten-worst list in ''The Book of Lists'',{{sfn|Book of Lists|page=208}} appears in Michael Sauter's ''The Worst Movies of All Time'',{{sfn|Sauter|page=68–71}} and was among those listed in ''The Fifty Worst Films of All Time''. Additionally, the ''[[Aldergrove Star]]'' described ''The Conqueror'' as the worst ever made and ''[[Complex (magazine)|Complex]]'' listed it as the worst biopic ever made.<ref>{{cite web |last=Grewal |first=Joti |title=Former Aldergrove Star editor releases book, soon-to-be documentary about 'worst movie ever made' |url=https://www.aldergrovestar.com/home/former-aldergrove-star-editor-releases-book-soon-to-be-documentary-about-worst-movie-ever-made/ |website=[[Aldergrove Star]] |access-date=July 26, 2022 |date=September 27, 2021 |archive-date=March 7, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230307010926/https://www.aldergrovestar.com/home/former-aldergrove-star-editor-releases-book-soon-to-be-documentary-about-worst-movie-ever-made/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Barone |first=Matt |title=The 10 Worst Biopic Movies Of All Time |work=[[Complex (magazine)|Complex]] |date=November 12, 2012 |url=http://www.complex.com/pop-culture/2012/11/10-worst-biopic-movies-of-all-time/ |access-date=July 7, 2017 |archive-date=August 13, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170813211848/http://www.complex.com/pop-culture/2012/11/10-worst-biopic-movies-of-all-time/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[The Guardian]]'' called the choice of Wayne for Khan – a role originally written for [[Marlon Brando]] – "one of the worst casting decisions of all time".<ref name="geng"/> Despite Wayne having lobbied for the lead role after reading the script,<ref>{{cite book |last=Monush |first=Barry |title=Screen World Presents the Encyclopedia of Hollywood Film Actors: From the Silent Era to 1965 |publisher=Hal Leonard Corporation |year=2003 |page=773 |isbn=1-55783-551-9}}</ref> he later lamented having taken it, stating, "Don't make an ass of yourself trying to play parts you are not suited for."<ref name="telekhan">{{cite web |last=Bell |first=Chris |title=The movie so toxic it killed John Wayne: the tragedy of The Conqueror |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/films/0/movie-toxic-killed-john-wayne-tragedy-conqueror/ |website=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |access-date=July 23, 2022 |date=January 17, 2017 |archive-date=July 8, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220708152313/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/films/0/movie-toxic-killed-john-wayne-tragedy-conqueror/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]'' writes: "by absolutely every conceivable metric – financially, critically, historically, ethnically, and even body count – it would come to be known as one of the biggest disasters in cinematic history."<ref name="telekhan"/> ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' described the film as the worst decision in movie history.<ref name="50decisions">{{cite magazine |last=Greene |first=Andy |title=The 50 Worst Decisions in Movie History |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-lists/the-50-worst-decisions-in-movie-history-1234824872/the-conqueror-casts-john-wayne-as-genghis-khan-films-on-a-nuclear-testing-site-1234827135/ |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |access-date=October 25, 2023 |date=September 25, 2023 |archive-date=October 1, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231001221023/https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-lists/the-50-worst-decisions-in-movie-history-1234824872/the-conqueror-casts-john-wayne-as-genghis-khan-films-on-a-nuclear-testing-site-1234827135/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Hughes, one of the world's wealthiest people at the time, had previously produced the successful dramatic films ''[[Hell's Angels (film)|Hell's Angels]]'', ''[[Scarface (1932 film)|Scarface]]'', and ''[[The Outlaw]]''.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/onthisday/hi/dates/stories/april/5/newsid_4739000/4739940.stm |title=BBC On This Day &#124; 5 &#124; 1976: Billionaire Howard Hughes dies |work=BBC News |date=April 7, 1976 |access-date=November 18, 2013 |archive-date=December 16, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171216160139/http://news.bbc.co.uk/onthisday/hi/dates/stories/april/5/newsid_4739000/4739940.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> After viewing ''The Conqueror'', Hughes bought every existing print for $12 million and refused to let the film be seen on TV until 1974, reportedly out of guilt over the decision to shoot at such a hazardous location.<ref>{{cite book |title=My Year of Flops |last=Rubin |first=Nathan |year=2010 |publisher=[[Charles Scribner's Sons|Scribner]] |isbn=978-1-4391-5312-3 |url=https://archive.org/details/myyearofflopsavc0000rabi }}</ref> This was the last film Hughes produced.<ref name="telekhan"/>

=== ''Fire Maidens from Outer Space'' (1956) ===
{{Main|Fire Maidens from Outer Space{{!}}''Fire Maidens from Outer Space''}}
''Fire Maidens from Outer Space'', a low-budget British [[space opera]] film (known in the US as ''Fire Maidens of Outer Space''), is about a group of astronauts visiting an all-female society on a moon of [[Jupiter]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dvddrive-in.com/reviews/e-h/firemaidensofouterspaceblu56.htm|title=Fire Maidens of Outer Space|website=dvddrive-in.com|access-date=July 18, 2021|archive-date=June 3, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210603133337/http://dvddrive-in.com/reviews/e-h/firemaidensofouterspaceblu56.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> This film developed a negative reputation for its poor special effects (including a scene on the alien planet in which an automobile is visible driving past).<ref name="dt">{{Cite web |url=https://www.dvdtalk.com/reviews/61441/fire-maidens-of-outer-space/ |title=Fire Maidens Of Outer Space |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200812024858/https://www.dvdtalk.com/reviews/61441/fire-maidens-of-outer-space/ |archive-date=August 12, 2020 |work=DVD Talk |date=August 13, 2013 |access-date=January 21, 2014}}</ref> Leslie Halliwell described ''Fire Maidens from Outer Space'' as "a strong contender for the title of the worst movie ever made, with diaphanously clad English gals striking embarrassed poses against cardboard sets".<ref>John Walker (ed.) ''Halliwell's Film and Video Guide 2000'', London and New York; HarperCollins, 1999, {{ISBN|0-06-273645-0}} (p.287).</ref> British film historian I.Q. Hunter included it in his list of candidates for "the worst British film ever made".<ref name="iqh">I. Q Hunter, "From Window Cleaner to Potato Man" in ''British Comedy Cinema'', edited by I.Q. Hunter and Laraine Porter. Routledge, 2012. {{ISBN|0-415-66667-8}}. (p.154)</ref> The [[DVD Talk]] website's review claimed it "may be among the worst-ever professionally produced science fiction films".<ref name="dt"/> Paul Welsh of the ''[[Borehamwood & Elstree Times]]'' wrote that it was "probably the worst [film] ever produced".<ref>{{cite web |last=Welsh |first=Paul |title=The worst film ever made? |url=https://www.borehamwoodtimes.co.uk/news/19747083.fire-maidens-outer-space---worst-film-ever-made/ |website=[[Borehamwood & Elstree Times]] |access-date=July 10, 2022 |language=en |date=November 28, 2021 |archive-date=July 10, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220710191835/https://www.borehamwoodtimes.co.uk/news/19747083.fire-maidens-outer-space---worst-film-ever-made/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In his book ''Operation Hollywood: How the Pentagon Shapes and Censors the Movies'', David L. Robb wrote that the film's director [[Cy Roth]] is "widely regarded as one of the worst filmmakers of all time", adding that, out of the three films he made, "the worst was ''Fire Maidens from Outer Space''...which is often cited as one of the ten worst movies ever made".<ref>{{cite book |last=Robb |first=David L. |title=Operation Hollywood: How the Pentagon Shapes and Censors the Movies |date=2004 |publisher=Prometheus Books |location=Amherst, NY |isbn=9781591021827 |page=321 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=j1wbAQAAIAAJ |access-date=July 13, 2022 |archive-date=October 25, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231025172902/https://books.google.com/books?id=j1wbAQAAIAAJ |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== ''Plan 9 from Outer Space'' (1957) ===
{{Main|Plan 9 from Outer Space{{!}}''Plan 9 from Outer Space''}}
[[Ed Wood]]'s ''Plan 9 from Outer Space'', a [[science fiction]] film about aliens resurrecting the dead, was labeled the "Worst Film Ever" by ''The Golden Turkey Awards'' in 1980.<ref name="Rabin9">{{cite web |last=Rabin |first=Nathan |author-link=Nathan Rabin |title=Control Nathan Rabin 4.0 #126 Plan 9 From Outer Space (1957) |url=https://www.nathanrabin.com/happy-place/2020/9/16/control-nathan-rabin-40-126-plan-9-from-outer-space-1957 |website=Nathan Rabin's Happy Place |access-date=July 10, 2022 |date=September 16, 2020 |archive-date=October 10, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221010212057/https://www.nathanrabin.com/happy-place/2020/9/16/control-nathan-rabin-40-126-plan-9-from-outer-space-1957 |url-status=live }}</ref> Wood had shot only a small amount of unrelated footage featuring top-billed star [[Bela Lugosi]] before Lugosi's death. Wood incorporated the footage into the film and cast [[Tom Mason (actor, born 1920)|Tom Mason]] as Lugosi's [[body double]]; Mason, a personal acquaintance of Wood, bore little resemblance to Lugosi and played his scenes holding the character's cape in front of his face. Although ''Golden Turkey Awards'' author Michael Medved credits Lugosi's top billing with its enduring legacy,<ref>{{cite web |last=Liebenson |first=Donald |title=Plan 9 from Outer Space Lands in TCM Classic Film Festival |url=https://www.tcm.com/articles/Article/021336/plan-9-from-outer-space-lands-in-tcm-classic-film-festival/ |date=May 7, 2021 |access-date=July 10, 2022 |publisher=[[Turner Classic Movies]] |archive-date=July 10, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220710104952/https://www.tcm.com/articles/Article/021336/plan-9-from-outer-space-lands-in-tcm-classic-film-festival/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[The Independent]]'' listed various other shortcomings: "A [[UFO]] dangling in the sky has been variously said to be either a car hubcap or a paper plate. Actors read from scripts on their lap; sound microphones wobble in and out of shot. Fake trees and cemetery headstones wobble as the actors brush past them. Characters go into scenes when it's night time and leave five minutes later into daylight. ... the plot itself appears to be the product of insanity."<ref name="independent9">{{cite web |last=Barnett |first=David |title=In defence of the so-called Worst Movie Ever Made |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/features/in-defence-of-the-socalled-worst-movie-ever-made-plan-9-from-outer-space-a7660961.html |website=[[The Independent]] |access-date=August 3, 2022 |language=en |date=March 31, 2017 |archive-date=August 3, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220803103027/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/features/in-defence-of-the-socalled-worst-movie-ever-made-plan-9-from-outer-space-a7660961.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Emanuel Levy]] notes the film has been dubbed "the epitome of so-bad-it's-good cinema" and has gained a [[cult following]] since appearing in ''The Golden Turkey Awards''.<ref>{{cite web |last=Levy |first=Emanuel |author-link=Emanuel Levy |title=Plan 9 from Outer Space (1959) |url=https://emanuellevy.com/review/plan-9-from-outer-space-1959-ed-woods-sci-fi-horror/ |website=emanuellevy.com |access-date=July 11, 2022 |date=February 1, 2021 |archive-date=July 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220711095637/https://emanuellevy.com/review/plan-9-from-outer-space-1959-ed-woods-sci-fi-horror/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[My Year of Flops]]'' author [[Nathan Rabin]] wrote that: "It's hard to overstate the role ''Plan 9 From Outer Space'' and its eccentric creator have played in the birth and evolution of bad movie culture... ''Plan 9'' was the original best worst movie."<ref name="Rabin9"/> [[BBC]] writer Nicholas Barber wrote that "it stands as the epitome of cinematic awfulness. And that's why so many people love it."<ref name="BBC9">{{cite web |last=Barber |first=Nicholas |title=Is this the worst film ever made? |url=https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20220107-is-this-the-worst-film-ever-made |publisher=[[BBC]] |access-date=July 21, 2022 |date=January 10, 2022 |language=en |archive-date=July 20, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220720114337/https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20220107-is-this-the-worst-film-ever-made |url-status=live }}</ref> Glenn Kenny of ''[[RogerEbert.com]]'' and ''The [[Radio Times]] Guide to Films'' each described it as the worst movie ever made,<ref>''Radio Times Guide to Films 2014''.
