''[[Radio Times]]'', London, 2013. {{ISBN|0-9567523-6-5}} (p.947).</ref><ref name="glennkenny">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/dirty-grandpa-2016|title=Dirty Grandpa Movie Review & Film Summary (2016)|last=Kenny|first=Glenn|website=[[RogerEbert.com]]|language=en|access-date=February 17, 2019}}</ref> and [[IGN]] wrote: "''Plan 9 from Outer Space'' was the undisputed best worst movie ever made for decades until films like ''[[Troll 2]]'' and ''[[The Room (film)|The Room]]'' got notorious, and it's still a legitimate contender".<ref name="IGN: BestWorstMovies"/>

It holds a 66% rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on 38 reviews, with the consensus stating that it is "justly celebrated for its staggering ineptitude".<ref>{{cite web |title=Plan 9 From Outer Space |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/plan-9-from-outer-space |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |access-date=July 21, 2022 |publisher=[[Fandango Media|Fandango]] |language=en |archive-date=November 14, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161114165703/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/plan-9-from-outer-space/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Phil Hall of ''[[Film Threat]]'' contends that the film is "far too entertaining to be considered as the very worst film ever made",<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/plan-9-from-outer-space/reviews/|title=Plan 9 from Outer Space – Movie Reviews|website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]]|publisher=[[Fandango Media|Fandango]]|access-date=April 16, 2019|archive-date=April 16, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190416083129/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/plan-9-from-outer-space/reviews/|url-status=live}}</ref> and [[Kim Newman]] states that, "The worst thing you can say about a film is that it's boring, and ''Plan 9'' is a fairly entertaining movie."<ref name="independent9"/> Although ''Flavorwire'' included it on its list of the 50 worst movies ever made (in the 50th spot), writer Jason Bailey described ''The Golden Turkey Awards''{{'}} assessment of it as "a label that stuck" and opined that he did not think it was even Wood's worst film.<ref name="Flavorwire"/> Likewise, John Wirt of ''The Advocate'' goes as far as to call it "the ultimate cult flick",<ref name=":2"/> and ''Videohound's Complete Guide to Cult Flicks and Trash Pics'' states, "In fact, the film has become so famous for its own badness that it's now beyond criticism."<ref>{{cite book |last=Schwartz |first=Carol |title=Videohound's Complete Guide to Cult Flicks and Trash Pics |publisher=Visible Ink Press |year=1995 |isbn=978-0-7876-0616-9}}</ref> Barber credits ''Plan 9''{{'}}s cult following to the film having some "halfway decent" elements, such as the film's title and screen presence of actors [[Tor Johnson]] and [[Maila Nurmi]], while film historian Rodney F. Hill considers the film to be a "campy, cult masterpiece" with a "minimalist [[avant-garde]] aesthetic".<ref name="BBC9"/>

== 1960s ==

=== ''The Creeping Terror'' (1964) ===
{{Main|The Creeping Terror{{!}}''The Creeping Terror''}}
The science-fiction/horror film ''The Creeping Terror'' was directed, produced, and edited by Vic Savage (under the pseudonym A.J. Nelson or Arthur Nelson,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://talkfilmsociety.com/columns/schlock-value-the-creeping-terror-1964|title=Schlock Value: The Creeping Terror (1964)|website=Talk Film Society|date=September 11, 2017|access-date=February 1, 2022|archive-date=February 1, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220201235735/https://talkfilmsociety.com/columns/schlock-value-the-creeping-terror-1964|url-status=live}}</ref> but kept his name when credited as an actor). The movie is about a large slug-like alien that lands on Earth and terrorizes a small town in California.<ref>Medved, Harry and Michael (1986). ''Son of Golden Turkey Awards''. New York: Random House/Villard Books. {{ISBN|0-394-74341-5}}. p. 197.</ref> The film is memorable for its use of some bargain-basement effects: stock footage of a rocket launch played in reverse to depict the landing of an alien spacecraft, and the "monster" appears to be composed of a length of shag carpet draped over several actors. Notably, the creature's victims inexplicably stand perfectly still as the slow-moving monster approaches them.

''[[ComingSoon.net]]'' declared it "widely considered the worst picture ever made", calling ''Plan 9 From Outer Space'' "a bona fide magnum opus" compared to ''The Creeping Terror''.<ref>{{cite web |last=Alexander |first=Chris |title=Creep Behind the Camera Blu-ray Review |url=https://www.comingsoon.net/horror/reviews/886917-the-creep-behind-the-camera-blu-ray-review |website=[[ComingSoon.net]] |access-date=February 2, 2022 |date=September 12, 2017 |archive-date=February 2, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220202022353/https://www.comingsoon.net/horror/reviews/886917-the-creep-behind-the-camera-blu-ray-review |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[Montreal Gazette]]'' and [[Dread Central]] also report that it has a reputation as being one of the worst films ever made.<ref name="montgaz"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Synapse Films Getting Creepy This September with Dario Argento's Creepers, The Creep Behind the Camera, and The Creeping Terror Blu-rays |url=https://www.dreadcentral.com/news/236216/synapse-films-getting-creepy-september-dario-argentos-creepers-creep-behind-camera-creeping-terror-blu-rays/ |website=[[Dread Central]] |access-date=February 2, 2022 |date=June 21, 2017 |archive-date=February 2, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220202000344/https://www.dreadcentral.com/news/236216/synapse-films-getting-creepy-september-dario-argentos-creepers-creep-behind-camera-creeping-terror-blu-rays/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The film was featured in ''The Golden Turkey Awards'',{{sfn|Golden Turkey Awards|pages=18}} and its follow-up book, ''Son of Golden Turkey Awards''.<ref name="montgaz">{{cite web |title=Fantasia 2014: The Creep Behind the Camera was scarier than the carpet monster from outer space |url=https://montrealgazette.com/entertainment/movies/fantasia-2014-the-creep-behind-the-camera-was-scarier-than-the-carpet-monster-from-outer-space |website=[[Montreal Gazette]] |access-date=February 2, 2022 |language=en-CA |archive-date=February 1, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220201235307/https://montrealgazette.com/entertainment/movies/fantasia-2014-the-creep-behind-the-camera-was-scarier-than-the-carpet-monster-from-outer-space |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Mystery Science Theater 3000'' featured ''The Creeping Terror'' in its sixth season and British film magazine ''[[Total Film]]'' included it on its list of the 66 worst films ever made.<ref name="TotalFilm">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/66-worst-movies-of-all-time/|title=66 Worst Movies Of All Time|date=February 15, 2012 |work=[[Total Film]]|publisher=[[GamesRadar]]|access-date=September 30, 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://rottentomatoes.com/m/the-creeping-terror-dangerous-charter-the-crawling-monster/ |title=The Creeping Terror (Dangerous Charter) (The Crawling Monster) |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |publisher=[[Fandango Media|Fandango]] |access-date=November 18, 2013 |archive-date=October 14, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131014100058/http://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/the-creeping-terror-dangerous-charter-the-crawling-monster/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

A documentary directed by Pete Schuermann about the making of the film, ''The Creep Behind The Camera'', was released in 2014.<ref name="montgaz"/>

=== ''Santa Claus Conquers the Martians'' (1964) ===
{{Main|Santa Claus Conquers the Martians{{!}}''Santa Claus Conquers the Martians''}}
[[File:Santa_Claus_Conquers_the_Martians_1.jpg|thumb|''[[Santa Claus Conquers the Martians]]'' is the only film to be featured on all three of the following shows: ''[[Mystery Science Theater 3000]]'', ''[[Rifftrax]]'' and ''[[Cinematic Titanic]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/movies/rifftrax-a-guide-to-holiday-riffing/|title=RiffTrax: A Guide to Christmas and Holiday Episodes|date=December 18, 2020|website=Den of Geek|access-date=July 18, 2021|archive-date=July 18, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718210136/https://www.denofgeek.com/movies/rifftrax-a-guide-to-holiday-riffing/|url-status=live}}</ref>]]
The sci-fi movie ''Santa Claus Conquers the Martians'' was the creation of TV director [[Nicholas Webster]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://vimeo.com/32952750|title=SANTA CLAUS CONQUERS THE MARTIANS (Nicholas Webster, 1964)|date=December 1, 2011|via=Vimeo|access-date=May 10, 2020|archive-date=May 17, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220517185308/https://vimeo.com/32952750|url-status=live}}</ref> Because [[Martian]] children only get to see [[Santa Claus]] on TV signals beamed from Earth, their parents decide to abduct Santa to make them happy. The film was criticized for its oddity and poor special effects. It is also known for starring a very young [[Pia Zadora]].<ref name="ft1111">{{cite web|url=https://filmthreat.com/features/1295/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121130200629/https://filmthreat.com/features/1295/|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 30, 2012|title=Film Threat – The Bootleg Files: "Santa Claus Conquers The Martians"|work=Filmthreat.com|access-date=May 4, 2012}}</ref> [[BBC]] critic Nick Cramp described it as "possibly the worst film ever made".<ref>{{cite web |title=Santa Claus Conquers the Martians (1964) |publisher=[[BBC]] |url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/films/2000/12/11/santa_claus_conquers_the_martians_1964_review.shtml |last=Cramp |first=Nick |date=December 11, 2020 |access-date=March 25, 2020 |archive-date=June 30, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200630130524/http://www.bbc.co.uk/films/2000/12/11/santa_claus_conquers_the_martians_1964_review.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref> The film is cited on a 10-worst list in ''The Book of Lists'' and in ''The Fifty Worst Films of All Time''.{{sfn|Book of Lists|page=208}} It has been featured in ''Mystery Science Theater 3000'',<ref>{{cite web |title=Mystery Science Theater 3000 – Santa Claus Conquers the Martians |work=TV.com |url=http://www.tv.com/mystery-science-theater-3000/santa-claus-conquers-the-martians/episode/46920/summary.html?tag=ep_list;title;47/ |access-date=March 7, 2011 |archive-date=August 22, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090822232331/http://www.tv.com/mystery-science-theater-3000/santa-claus-conquers-the-martians/episode/46920/summary.html?tag=ep_list%3Btitle%3B47%2F |url-status=dead }}</ref> ''Canned Film Festival'', ''Rifftrax'' and ''[[Cinematic Titanic]]'' (another spin-off of ''MST3K'' that revisited the film in 2008).<ref name="cannedfilm"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://cinematictitanic.twinvision.com/products/ |title=Cinematic Titanic &#124; The Store |work=Cinematictitanic.twinvision.com |date=October 11, 2012 |access-date=November 18, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131015034626/https://cinematictitanic.twinvision.com/products/ |archive-date=October 15, 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://shoutfactory.com/|title=Shout! Factory Store|website=Shout! Factory|access-date=October 1, 2023|archive-date=October 1, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231001193317/https://shoutfactory.com/|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== ''The Incredibly Strange Creatures Who Stopped Living and Became Mixed-Up Zombies'' (1964) ===
{{main|The Incredibly Strange Creatures Who Stopped Living and Became Mixed-Up Zombies{{!}}''The Incredibly Strange Creatures Who Stopped Living and Became Mixed-Up Zombies''}}
''The Incredibly Strange Creatures Who Stopped Living and Became Mixed-Up Zombies'' (sometimes shortened to ''The Incredibly Strange Creatures'') is a 1964 American monster movie written and directed by [[Ray Dennis Steckler]]. Steckler also starred in the film, billed under the pseudonym "Cash Flagg". In the film, three friends visit a carnival and stumble onto a group of occultists and disfigured monsters. Produced on a $38,000 budget, much of it takes place at [[The Pike]] amusement park in [[Long Beach, California]], which resembles [[Brooklyn]]'s [[Coney Island]]. The film was billed as the first "monster musical", beating out ''[[The Horror of Party Beach]]'' by a mere month in release date. The [[Music journalism|music critic]] [[Lester Bangs]] wrote an appreciative 1973 [[essay]] about ''Incredibly Strange Creatures'' in which he tries to explain and justify the movie's value: "This flick doesn't just rebel against, or even disregard, standards of taste and art. In the universe inhabited by ''The Incredibly Strange Creatures Who Stopped Living and Became Mixed-Up Zombies'', such things as standards and responsibility have never been heard of. It is this lunar purity which largely imparts to the film its classic stature. Like ''[[Beyond the Valley of the Dolls]]'' and a very few others, it will remain as an artifact in years to come to which scholars and searchers for truth can turn and say, {{'}}''This'' was trash!{{'"}}<ref name="Bangs">{{cite book |last=Bangs |first=Lester |author-link = Lester Bangs |editor-first = Greil |editor-last = Marcus |title = Psychotic Reactions and Carburetor Dung |year = 1987 |publisher = Random House |location = New York |isbn = 0-394-53896-X |chapter = The Incredibly Strange Creatures Who Stopped Living and Became Mixed-Up Zombies, or, The Day The Airwaves Erupted |page = 122}}</ref> The 2004 DVD ''The 50 Worst Movies Ever Made'' listed this film as the worst film of all time.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Grobaty|first=Tim|title=Location Filming in Long Beach|publisher=[[Arcadia Publishing]]|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=jWR_CQAAQBAJ&dq=The+Incredibly+Strange+Creatures+Who+Stopped+Living+and+Became+Mixed-Up+Zombies!!%3F+2004+50+Worst+Movies+Ever+Made%27&pg=PT65|year=2012|isbn=978-1614237754|access-date=March 27, 2023|archive-date=April 7, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230407010802/https://books.google.com/books?id=jWR_CQAAQBAJ&dq=The+Incredibly+Strange+Creatures+Who+Stopped+Living+and+Became+Mixed-Up+Zombies%21%21%3F+2004+50+Worst+Movies+Ever+Made%27&pg=PT65|url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[Time Out (magazine)|Time Out]]'' and ''Flavorwire'' included it on their respective worst film lists.<ref name="timeoutlist">{{cite web |last1=Singer |first1=Matthew |last2=McGeady |first2=Sean |title=The 40 best bad movies ever made |url=https://www.timeout.com/film/the-best-bad-movies-ever-made |website=[[Time Out (magazine)|Time Out]] |date=September 7, 2022 |access-date=May 6, 2023 |archive-date=May 23, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230523020505/https://www.timeout.com/film/the-best-bad-movies-ever-made |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Flavorwire"/>

=== ''Monster a Go-Go!'' (1965) ===
{{Main|Monster a Go-Go!{{!}}''Monster a Go-Go!''}}
''Monster a Go-Go!'' began as ''Terror at Halfday'' by [[Bill Rebane]]. The production ran out of money and the film was abandoned. [[Herschell Gordon Lewis]], who reportedly needed a second feature to compose a double bill, purchased and completed it for a minimal amount of money. Several of the film's actors were unable to return, so Lewis simply replaced their parts with new characters who mysteriously appear and fill the roles of the missing characters. One of the actors Lewis managed to rehire had gained weight, gone bald, and grown a goatee, so Lewis recast him as the brother of the original character.<ref name="agony">{{cite web |date=June 16, 2003 |url=http://www.agonybooth.com/monster_a_go_go/default.asp?Page=5 |title=Recap: Monster A-Go Go (1965) |work=The Agony Booth |access-date=January 21, 2007 |archive-date=October 23, 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061023063604/http://www.agonybooth.com/monster_a_go_go/default.asp?Page=5 |url-status=live }}</ref> The picture consists mostly of lengthy dialogue sequences concerning the apparent mutation of an astronaut into a monster portrayed by the {{cvt|7|ft|6+3/4|in|cm|0|order=flip|adj=mid|-tall}} [[Henry Hite]]. Poor audio quality makes much of the dialogue unintelligible, and when the film is overexposed, several characters' faces appear as bright white, glowing circles. During the climax of the movie, as soldiers prepare to confront the mutated astronaut, he abruptly vanishes and the narrator informs the audience, "there was no monster", and that the astronaut has, in fact, been in the [[Atlantic Ocean]] the entire time.<ref>{{cite web |last=Beldin |first=Fred |title=Monster A Go-Go! |work=AllMovie |url=https://allmovie.com/movie/monster-a-go-go%21-v33169/review |access-date=September 12, 2012 |archive-date=August 2, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120802155607/http://www.allmovie.com/movie/monster-a-go-go%21-v33169/review |url-status=live }}</ref>

''[[NJ.com]]'' notes that many [[cinemaphile]]s consider it to be the worst film of all time, including the film's original director Rebane.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Voger |first1=Mark |title='Monster A-Go Go': A cult favorite guaranteed to make you cringe |url=https://www.nj.com/entertainment/2010/10/monster_a-go_go_a_cult_favorit.html |website=[[NJ.com]] |access-date=December 7, 2024 |language=en |date=October 26, 2010}}</ref> Matt Brunson of ''Film Frenzy'' agrees with its designation as one of the worst films ever made, stating it belongs in the "exalted pantheon of immortal atrocities like ''Plan 9 from Outer Space'', ''Robot Monster'' and ''[[Manos: The Hands of Fate]]''".<ref>{{cite web |title=Monster A-Go-Go |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/monster_a_gogo/reviews |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |access-date=December 7, 2024 |language=en}}</ref> Meanwhile, ''[[MovieWeb]]'' writer B. Alan Orange believes it to be the second-worst movie ever made, after ''[[Superbabies: Baby Geniuses 2]]''.<ref name="movieweborange">{{cite web |last1=Orange |first1=B. Alan |title=Bill Rebane Looks Back at Monster a Go-Go! [Exclusive] |url=https://movieweb.com/exclusive-bill-rebane-looks-back-at-monster-a-go-go/ |website=[[MovieWeb]] |access-date=December 2, 2024 |language=en |date=October 25, 2010}}</ref> It was also featured on ''Mystery Science Theater 3000'', where writer [[Paul Chaplin]] called the dialogue "garbled beyond recognition" and declared it to be the worst movie they ever featured on the program.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mystery Science Theater 3000 – Monster A Go-Go |website=Castle Forrester |url=http://www.castleforrester.com/media/guide/0421.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081120215055/http://www.castleforrester.com/media/guide/0421.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 20, 2008 |access-date=March 7, 2011}}</ref> ''Total Film'' later included it on its list of the worst films ever made.<ref name=TotalFilm/>

=== ''Manos: The Hands of Fate'' (1966) ===
{{Main|Manos: The Hands of Fate{{!}}''Manos: The Hands of Fate''}}
[[File:The_Master%E2%80%94_Manos_tHoF.jpg | thumb | ''Manos: The Hands of Fate'' (1966) went unnoticed until the cult TV series ''[[Mystery Science Theater 3000]]'' aired the film in 1993.]]
The low-budget horror film ''Manos: The Hands of Fate'', made by [[El Paso, Texas|El Paso]] insurance and fertilizer salesman Hal P. Warren,<ref>{{cite book |title=The Joy of Trash: Nathan Rabin's Happy Place's Definitive Guide to the Very Wortst of Everything |date=December 16, 2021 |page=154 |publisher=Independently published |isbn=979-8-7859-1421-6 |url=https://www.amazon.com/Joy-Trash-Nathan-Definitive-Everything/dp/B09NR9NTB4 |access-date=December 29, 2021 |archive-date=December 29, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211229034841/https://www.amazon.com/Joy-Trash-Nathan-Definitive-Everything/dp/B09NR9NTB4 |url-status=live }}</ref> concerns a vacationing family kidnapped by a [[polygamous cult]] of [[paganism|pagans]]. The film was conceived after Warren bet Academy Award-winning screenwriter [[Stirling Silliphant]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nathanrabin.com/happy-place/2019/9/16/control-nathan-rabin-40-69-manos-the-hands-of-fate-1966|title=Exploiting our Archives: Control Nathan Rabin 4.0 #69 Manos: The Hands of Fate (1966)|website=Nathan Rabin's Happy Place|date=May 13, 2023|access-date=December 29, 2021|archive-date=December 29, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211229033553/https://www.nathanrabin.com/happy-place/2019/9/16/control-nathan-rabin-40-69-manos-the-hands-of-fate-1966|url-status=live}}</ref> that anyone could make a horror movie.<ref name="EW2">{{cite magazine |url=https://ew.com/article/2005/06/06/worst-movie-ever-made/ |title=The Worst Movie Ever Made |page=2 |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |date=June 6, 2005 |access-date=December 3, 2019 |first=Dalton |last=Ross |archive-date=January 4, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220104025540/https://ew.com/article/2005/06/06/worst-movie-ever-made/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Warren was convinced by the film's cinematographer and stunt coordinator that most of its glaring mistakes could be fixed in a [[Dallas]] post-production studio, when in reality the two wanted to quickly wrap the production because they were not being paid.<ref name="EW2"/> Several technical gaffes made it into the film, including scenes filmed out of focus, a marking slate being seen in one shot, the scarf on the female lead's head disappearing and reappearing, and an insect bumping the camera lens.<ref name="EW2"/>{{sfn|Adams|pages=91–2}} The film was shot with a camera that could not record sound and had a 32-second maximum shot length. All dialogue was later dubbed by Warren and four others, including a grown woman who dubbed the voice for a seven-year-old girl.{{sfn|Adams|pages=91–2}}<ref name="NBC">{{cite web |url=http://entertainment.nbcnews.com/_news/2012/08/13/12645253-torgo-lives-mystery-science-alums-revisit-worst-movie-ever-manos-the-hands-of-fate |title=Torgo lives! 'Mystery Science' alums revisit worst movie ever, 'Manos: The Hands of Fate' |last=Fashingbauer Cooper |first=Gael |date=August 13, 2012 |work=[[NBC News]] |access-date=March 4, 2013 |archive-date=January 3, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130103195520/http://entertainment.nbcnews.com/_news/2012/08/13/12645253-torgo-lives-mystery-science-alums-revisit-worst-movie-ever-manos-the-hands-of-fate |url-status=dead }}</ref>

''Manos'' opens with nine minutes of monotonous driving scenes reportedly intended to be overlaid with [[opening credits]] that were never added.<ref name="NBC"/> The movie includes dialogue spoken while all characters are facing away from the camera, a character complaining about it getting dark while the sun is brightly shining, and the character Torgo, a [[satyr]] with overly large thighs, that three women attempt to massage to death.<ref name="EW2"/><ref name="NBC"/><ref name="ElPaso">{{cite news |title=Hero Massaged to Death in 'Manos-- The Hands of Fate' |first=Betty |last=Pierce |url=http://www.mst3ktemple.com/images/manos_review-post-x.jpg |newspaper=[[El Paso Herald-Post]] |date=November 11, 1966 |access-date=March 1, 2013 |archive-date=December 17, 2005 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051217154836/http://www.mst3ktemple.com/images/manos_review-post-x.jpg |url-status=usurped }}</ref> The film gained notoriety and cult popularity by being featured on ''[[Mystery Science Theater 3000]]'',<ref>{{cite web |title=Mystery Science Theater 3000 – Manos: The Hands of Fate |work=TV.com |url=http://www.tv.com/mystery-science-theater-3000/manos-the-hands-of-fate/episode/46947/summary.html?tag=ep_list;title;74/ |access-date=March 7, 2011 |archive-date=June 28, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110628235129/http://www.tv.com/mystery-science-theater-3000/manos-the-hands-of-fate/episode/46947/summary.html?tag=ep_list%3Btitle%3B74%2F |url-status=dead }}</ref> and was the show's most popular episode.<ref name="EW2"/> The film has a rare 0% approval rating on [[Rotten Tomatoes]],<ref>{{Rotten Tomatoes|qid=Q691828|title=Manos – the Hands of Fate |access-date=July 2, 2018}}</ref> and ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' says the movie is "widely regarded as, quite simply, the worst movie ever made".<ref name="EW2"/> Even Warren himself would later admit his film was one of the worst ever, suggesting it might make a passable comedy if redubbed.<ref>{{cite news |first=Richard |last=Brandt |url=http://www.jophan.org/mimosa/m18/brandt.htm |title=The Hand That Time Forgot |work=Mimosa |date=May 1996 |access-date=August 17, 2006 |pages=35–38 |archive-date=October 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181006083628/http://www.jophan.org/mimosa/m18/brandt.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> The film was later restored<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.npr.org/2011/12/12/143573040/manos-the-hands-of-fate-carefully-restoring-the-opposite-of-a-masterpiece|title='Manos: The Hands Of Fate': Carefully Restoring The Opposite Of A Masterpiece|first=Chris|last=Heller|date=December 12, 2011|website=NPR|access-date=March 16, 2020|archive-date=May 29, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200529014421/https://www.npr.org/2011/12/12/143573040/manos-the-hands-of-fate-carefully-restoring-the-opposite-of-a-masterpiece|url-status=live}}</ref> and released on Blu-ray in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.avclub.com/read-this-the-battle-over-the-infamous-cult-classic-ma-1798284742|title=Read this: The battle over the infamous cult classic Manos: The Hands of Fate|date=September 25, 2015|website=The A.V. Club|access-date=July 13, 2022|archive-date=August 15, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220815104028/https://www.avclub.com/read-this-the-battle-over-the-infamous-cult-classic-ma-1798284742|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.synapsefilms.com/product/manos-the-hands-of-fate-special-edition-blu-ray/|title=Manos: The Hands of Fate [Special Edition] [Blu-ray] – Synapse Films|date=October 13, 2015|access-date=July 13, 2022|archive-date=July 13, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220713142423/https://www.synapsefilms.com/product/manos-the-hands-of-fate-special-edition-blu-ray/|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== ''A Place for Lovers'' (1968) ===
{{Main|A Place for Lovers{{!}}''A Place for Lovers''}}
''A Place for Lovers'' is a French-Italian [[romantic film]] directed by [[Vittorio De Sica]] (a filmmaker known for acclaimed [[Italian neorealism|neorealist]] works, such as ''[[Umberto D]]'' and ''[[The Bicycle Thieves]]''), starring [[Faye Dunaway]] as a terminally ill American fashion designer in [[Venice, Italy]], and [[Marcello Mastroianni]] as a race car driver who has a whirlwind affair with her. [[Roger Ebert]] of the ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'' called it the "most godawful piece of pseudo-romantic slop I've ever seen!"<ref>{{cite news |last=Ebert |first=Roger |title=A Place for Lovers |newspaper=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |date=December 16, 1969 |url=https://rogerebert.com/reviews/a-place-for-lovers-1969 |access-date=October 19, 2013 |archive-date=October 20, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131020094319/http://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/a-place-for-lovers-1969 |url-status=live }}</ref> and [[Charles Champlin]] of the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' referred to it as "the worst movie I have seen all year and possibly since 1926".<ref>{{cite news |title=A Place For Lovers Film 'Worst' One Critic's Seen |last=Champlin |first=Charles |author-link=Charles Champlin |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=FmlkAAAAIBAJ&pg=1127,904508&dq=a+place+for+lovers+dunaway+worst |newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=December 18, 1969 |access-date=August 19, 2013 |archive-date=July 9, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220709123728/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=FmlkAAAAIBAJ&pg=1127%2C904508&dq=a+place+for+lovers+dunaway+worst |url-status=live }}</ref> Leonard Maltin noted Ebert's comments in his review, and offered that the film was "low points for all concerned".<ref name="Maltin01211"/> ''A Place for Lovers'' was included as one of the choices in ''The Fifty Worst Films of All Time,'' and ''[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]'' listed it as one of the 20 worst movies ever made.<ref name="italianvanity"/>

=== ''They Saved Hitler's Brain'' (1968) ===
{{Main|They Saved Hitler's Brain{{!}}''They Saved Hitler's Brain''}}
''They Saved Hitler's Brain'' is a [[science fiction film]] directed by [[David Bradley (director)|David Bradley]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tcm.com/tcmdb/title/92846/they-saved-hitlers-brain |title=They Saved Hitler's Brain (1964) |publisher=Turner Classic Movies |access-date=March 27, 2020 |archive-date=March 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200327112754/http://www.tcm.com/tcmdb/title/92846/They-Saved-Hitler-s-Brain/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> It was [[made-for-TV movie|adapted for TV]] from a shorter 1963 theatrical [[feature film]], ''Madmen of Mandoras'', and was lengthened by about 20 minutes with additional footage shot by [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]] students at the request of the distributor. In the film, [[Adolf Hitler]]'s head was severed from his body at the end of [[World War II]] and the head plans to rule over a [[Fourth Reich|new Third Reich]] from [[South America]]. It has a 0% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, based on five reviews from critics, with an average rating of 1.3/10.<ref name="hitlersbrain">{{cite web |url = http://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/they_saved_hitlers_brain/ |title = They Saved Hitler's Brain | work = [[Rotten Tomatoes]] |publisher = [[Fandango Media|Fandango]] |access-date = March 26, 2020 |archive-date = October 21, 2019 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20191021085728/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/they_saved_hitlers_brain/ |url-status = live }}</ref> ''[[TV Guide]]'' called it "One of the all-time worst",<ref name="hitlersbrain"/> while Danny Peary said it was "A legitimate candidate for Worst Film Ever Made title."<ref>{{Cite book|last=Peary|first=Danny|author-link=Danny Peary|title=Guide for the Film Fanatic|publisher=[[Simon & Schuster]]|page=430|year=1986|isbn=0671610813}}</ref> In 1979, it won the World's Worst Film Festival in [[Ottawa, Canada]], which reportedly delighted Bradley.<ref name="aslide">{{Cite book|last=Slide|first=Anthony|author-link=Anthony Slide|title=Magnificent Obsession: The Outrageous History of Film Buffs, Collectors, Scholars, and Fanatics|publisher=[[University Press of Mississippi]]|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ep9GDwAAQBAJ&q=they+saved+hitler%27s+brain+&pg=PT105|year=2018|isbn=978-1496810533|access-date=October 2, 2020|archive-date=October 25, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231025172940/https://books.google.com/books?id=ep9GDwAAQBAJ&q=they+saved+hitler%27s+brain+&pg=PT105#v=snippet&q=they%20saved%20hitler's%20brain&f=false|url-status=live}}</ref> It has been featured in ''The Golden Turkey Awards'' and ''Canned Film Festival'',<ref name="cannedfilm"/> and has been spoofed on ''[[The Simpsons]]'' multiple times.<ref name="aslide"/>

== 1970s ==

=== ''Myra Breckinridge'' (1970) ===
{{Main|Myra Breckinridge (film){{!}}''Myra Breckinridge'' (film)}}
[[File:GoreVidalVanVechten1.jpg|thumb|upright|''[[Myra Breckinridge (film)|Myra Breckinridge]]'' and ''[[Caligula (film)|Caligula]]'' were based on works by author and political commentator [[Gore Vidal]], who disowned both adaptations.]]

The 1970 comedy film ''Myra Breckinridge'', based on the [[Myra Breckinridge|book of the same name]] by [[Gore Vidal]], directed by [[Mike Sarne|Michael Sarne]]<ref>[https://www.filmcomment.com/blog/queer-now-then-1970/ Queer & Now & Then: 1970 – Film Comment Magazine]</ref> and starring [[Raquel Welch]], [[Rex Reed]], [[Mae West]], [[John Huston]] and [[Farrah Fawcett]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Myra Breckinridge |url=https://variety.com/1969/film/reviews/myra-breckinridge-1117793381/ |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |access-date=January 18, 2022 |date=January 1, 1970 |archive-date=September 24, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210924071014/https://variety.com/1969/film/reviews/myra-breckinridge-1117793381/ |url-status=live }}</ref> provoked controversy due to a scene in which Welch forcibly sodomizes a bound man while clips from various classic films play onscreen. The film was initially [[X-rated|rated X]] before edits and an appeal to the [[Motion Picture Association of America|MPAA]] brought it down to an R. It also used [[collage film|the technique of inserting clips]] from [[Classical Hollywood cinema|Golden Age]] movies in such a way that the dialogue took on sexual undertones. The film was a critical failure, with ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' magazine saying, "''Myra Breckinridge'' is about as funny as a child molester."<ref>{{cite news |title=Cinema:Some Sort of Nadir |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |date=July 6, 1970 |url=http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,878382,00.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080513095014/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,878382,00.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 13, 2008 |access-date=March 7, 2011}}</ref> Leonard Maltin gave it a BOMB (the lowest score possible) and stated that it was "as bad as any movie ever made".<ref name="Maltin01211"/> ''[[The Miami News]]'' critic Herb Kelly nominated ''Myra Breckinridge'' as the worst film ever made.<ref>{{cite news |title='Breckinridge' Worst Ever |last=Kelly |first=Herb |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/40395524/ |newspaper=[[The Miami News]] |date=August 29, 1970 |access-date=August 17, 2013 |archive-date=October 25, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231025172959/https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-miami-news-herb-kelly-columnbrecke/40395524/ |url-status=live }}</ref> It was also included in ''The Book of Lists''{{'}} worst movies of all time, which claimed that there was something in it to offend absolutely everyone.{{sfn|Book of Lists|page=208}} Likewise, ''The Fifty Worst Films of All Time'' and ''Vanity Fair'' also listed it as one of the worst movies ever made.<ref name="italianvanity"/> Gore Vidal disowned it, calling it "an awful joke",<ref>{{cite book |last1=Hoberman |first1=J. |author-link1=J. Hoberman |last2=Rosenbaum |first2=Jonathan |author-link2=Jonathan Rosenbaum |title=Midnight Movies |publisher=Da Capo Press |year=1991 |isbn=0-306-80433-6 |page=268}}</ref> and blamed the movie for a decade-long drought in the sale of the original book.<ref>{{cite book |last=Conner |first=Floyd |title=Hollywood's Most Wanted: The Top 10 Book of Lucky Breaks, Prima Donnas, Box Office Bombs, and Other Oddities |publisher=Brassey's |year=2002 |isbn=1-57488-480-8 |page=[https://archive.org/details/hollywoodsmostwa0000conn/page/65 65] |url=https://archive.org/details/hollywoodsmostwa0000conn/page/65 }}</ref>

=== ''Zaat'' (1971) ===
{{Main|Zaat{{!}}''Zaat''}}
Directed by Don Barton,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/entertainment/news/one-and-done-8-filmmakers-who-have-only-directed-a-single-movie/ar-AA108Iqg?ocid=msedgntp&cvid=8a77fc93804d4808bab665cceffcb034 |title=One and Done: 8 Filmmakers Who Have Only Directed a Single Movie – Collider on msn.com |website=[[MSN]] |access-date=July 30, 2022 |archive-date=July 30, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220730222838/https://www.msn.com/en-us/entertainment/news/one-and-done-8-filmmakers-who-have-only-directed-a-single-movie/ar-AA108Iqg?ocid=msedgntp&cvid=8a77fc93804d4808bab665cceffcb034 |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Zaat'' was also known under various titles including ''Hydra'', ''Attack of the Swamp Creatures'', ''Legend of the Zaat Monster'', and ''The Blood Waters of Dr. Z'' (the name under which it was lampooned on ''Mystery Science Theater 3000''). The film follows a Nazi [[mad scientist]] who injects himself with a formula that turns him into a mutated catfish. ''[[Florida Times-Union]]'' critic Matt Soergel quipped that ''Zaat'' "could very well be the best film ever made about a mutated catfish".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://jacksonville.com/tu-online/stories/061201/enm_zaat.html|title=Locally made sci-fi thriller is all 'Zaat' and then some|date=June 12, 2001|access-date=September 30, 2013|archive-date=August 13, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170813183130/http://jacksonville.com/tu-online/stories/061201/enm_zaat.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Critic Jeffrey Kauffman said, "this is the sort of film Ed Wood, Jr. might have made—on a bad day" and added, "Lovers of fantastically bad films rate ''Zaat'' one of the worst".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blu-ray.com/movies/Zaat-Blu-ray/35923/#Review|title=Zaat Blu Ray|date=February 21, 2012|last=Kauffman|first=Jeffrey|access-date=September 30, 2013|archive-date=July 11, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180711203907/http://www.blu-ray.com/movies/Zaat-Blu-ray/35923/#Review|url-status=live}}</ref> Patrick Naugle of [[DVD Verdict]] stated, "The acting in ''Zaat'' is below subpar. Actors seem to be whispering their lines and trying hard not to fully comprehend that they're in one of the worst films ever made", while Michael Rubino of DVD Verdict also claimed, "''Zaat'' may be one of the worst films ever created".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dvdverdict.com/printer/zaatbluray.php|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131002180849/https://dvdverdict.com/printer/zaatbluray.php|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 2, 2013|title=DVD Verdict Review – Zaat (Blu Ray)|date=February 12, 2012|last=Naugle|first=Patrick|work=[[DVD Verdict]]|access-date=September 30, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://dvdverdict.com/reviews/mst3kxvii.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100225160816/https://dvdverdict.com/reviews/mst3kxvii.php |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 25, 2010 |title=DVD Verdict Review – Mystery Science Theater 3000 |date=February 22, 2010 |last=Rubino |first=Michael |work=[[DVD Verdict]] |access-date=September 30, 2013 }}</ref> [[NPR]] called it a "sci-fi fiasco" when it became "the winner — er, loser —" on IMDb's Bottom 100.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=101056819|title=10 Reasons Why We Love Making Lists|date=February 24, 2009|last=Weeks|first=Linton|work=[[NPR]]|access-date=September 30, 2013|archive-date=October 20, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131020082139/http://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=101056819|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Zaat'' appeared on ''Mystery Science Theater 3000'', which gave it significant exposure,<ref>{{cite web |author=Sampo |url=http://www.mst3kinfo.com/?p=5866 |title=Season 10 Episode Guide! |publisher=MST3Kinfo |date=May 20, 2010 |access-date=December 19, 2013 |archive-date=December 18, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131218085901/http://www.mst3kinfo.com/?p=5866 |url-status=live }}</ref> and was also featured on [[RedLetterMedia]]'s show ''Half in the Bag'' where the hosts called it one of their favorite "[[so bad it's good]]" films.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://redlettermedia.com/half-in-the-bag-zaat/|title=Half in the Bag:Zaat!|date=April 30, 2012|work=[[RedLetterMedia]]|access-date=September 30, 2013|archive-date=March 27, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200327104101/http://redlettermedia.com/half-in-the-bag-zaat/|url-status=dead}}</ref> ''Total Film'' included it in their list of the 66 worst films of all time.<ref name="TotalFilm"/>

=== ''An American Hippie in Israel'' (1972) ===
{{Main|An American Hippie in Israel{{!}}''An American Hippie in Israel''}}
The 1972 Israeli film ''An American Hippie in Israel'' is about an American [[hippie]] traveling to [[Israel]] after being involved with the [[Vietnam War]], befriending Israeli [[flower child]]ren, and encountering "menacing" [[Mime artist|mimes]] along the way. The film was presumed [[Lost film|lost]], but after resurfacing 38 years after its production, it became a "midnight sensation" in [[Tel Aviv]] and developed a cult following<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://vimeo.com/76605726|title=An American Hippie in {{Typo|Isreal}} [sic]|author=Cork International Film Festival|date=October 10, 2013|via=Vimeo|access-date=April 25, 2020|archive-date=February 2, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230202035330/https://vimeo.com/76605726|url-status=live}}</ref> akin to ''[[The Rocky Horror Picture Show]]''. It was then released internationally on home video by [[Grindhouse Releasing]]. Gil Shefler of ''[[The Jewish Daily Forward]]'' described it as "perfectly awful", offering that it "probably is the worst Israeli movie ever made, and a serious candidate for the worst movie of all time".<ref>{{cite news |newspaper=[[The Jewish Daily Forward]] |url=http://forward.com/articles/134946/finding-new-life-as-a-cult-classic/ |date=January 26, 2011 |last=Shefler |first=Gil |access-date=August 14, 2013 |title=Finding New Life As a Cult Classic |archive-date=October 18, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151018024531/http://forward.com/articles/134946/finding-new-life-as-a-cult-classic/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Its description as "a serious candidate for the worst movie of all time" was echoed by Josh Olson in ''[[IndieWire]]''.<ref>{{cite web |last=Olson |first=Josh |title=Trailers from Hell: Josh Olson on Little Known Comedy 'An American Hippie in Israel' |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2013/12/trailers-from-hell-josh-olson-on-little-known-comedy-an-american-hippie-in-israel-194709/ |website=[[IndieWire]] |access-date=July 13, 2022 |language=en |date=December 9, 2013 |archive-date=July 13, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220713060658/https://www.indiewire.com/2013/12/trailers-from-hell-josh-olson-on-little-known-comedy-an-american-hippie-in-israel-194709/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Ben Hartman of ''[[The Jerusalem Post]]'' stated the film was "surely one of the worst films ever made in Israel, or beyond".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.jpost.com/Arts-and-Culture/Entertainment/Horrendous-Israeli-70s-film-becomes-a-cult-favorite |date=January 9, 2011 |last=Harman |first=Ben |work=[[The Jerusalem Post]] |access-date=August 29, 2013 |title='Horrendous' Israeli '70s film becomes a cult favorite |archive-date=August 30, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180830142226/https://www.jpost.com//Arts-and-Culture/Entertainment/Horrendous-Israeli-70s-film-becomes-a-cult-favorite |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[Nana 10]]'' said it claims the title of "worst Israeli film and most amusing".<ref>{{Cite web|language=he |url=http://news.nana10.co.il/Article/?ArticleID=766710 |title=News article from Nana 10 | work=nana 10 - חדשות |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170808053515/http://news.nana10.co.il/Article/?ArticleID=766710 |archive-date=August 8, 2017 |access-date=August 26, 2013}}</ref>

=== ''Bat Pussy'' (circa 1973) ===
{{Main|Bat Pussy{{!}}''Bat Pussy''}}
A loose spoof of the 1966 ''[[Batman (TV series)|Batman]]'' television series cited as one of the earliest examples of a [[pornographic parody film]], the presumably-1970s [[pornographic film]] ''Bat Pussy'' has been described as the worst pornographic film ever made due to "some incredibly unarousing sex and a general attitude of awfulness".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/men/the-filter/11395280/The-rise-of-parody-porn-the-Chaucer-of-our-times.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220111/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/men/the-filter/11395280/The-rise-of-parody-porn-the-Chaucer-of-our-times.html |archive-date=2022-01-11 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |title=The rise of parody porn, 'the Chaucer of our times' |newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |author=Merz, Theo |date=February 23, 2015}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref name="BP73io9">{{cite web |url=http://io9.gizmodo.com/5914178/the-bizarre-history-of-superhero-porn-nsfw |title=The Bizarre History of Superhero Porn [NSFW] |author=Anders, Charlie Jane |date=May 30, 2012 |publisher=[[io9]] |access-date=March 21, 2016 |archive-date=March 27, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160327103621/http://io9.gizmodo.com/5914178/the-bizarre-history-of-superhero-porn-nsfw |url-status=live }}</ref> Possessing no credits or copyright information, there is no known record of ''Bat Pussy''{{'}}s existence prior to the mid-1990s, when it was discovered in the storeroom of an [[adult movie theater]] in [[Memphis, Tennessee]], and subsequently released on home video by [[exploitation film]] distributor [[Something Weird Video]]. [[Gawker Media]]{{'}}s ''[[io9]]'' proclaimed the film to be "the absolute nadir of pornography, period. Not just Batman-themed pornography. ALL pornography", deriding its "obese [[redneck]]" cast as rendering the film "[[masturbation|wank]]-proof".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://io9.gizmodo.com/5545416/a-brief-history-of-batman-themed-pornography-nsfw |title=A brief history of Batman-themed pornography (NSFW) |publisher=[[io9]] |author=Lamar, Cyriaque |date=May 22, 2010 |access-date=March 21, 2016 |archive-date=March 7, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160307104420/http://io9.gizmodo.com/5545416/a-brief-history-of-batman-themed-pornography-nsfw |url-status=live }}</ref> ''PornParody.com'', a website dedicated to the genre, acknowledged its status as "the worst adult movie of all time", describing ''Bat Pussy'' as "renowned for its technical ineptness and anti-eroticism" due to its "physically unappealing" actors.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://pornparody.com/2014/10/bat-pussy-the-first-superhero-porn-parody/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141008174205/http://pornparody.com/2014/10/bat-pussy-the-first-superhero-porn-parody/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 8, 2014 |title=Bat Pussy – the first superhero porn parody? |date=October 6, 2014 |publisher=PornParody.com}}</ref> ''AV Maniacs'' contested ''Bat Pussy''{{'}}s categorization as pornography on the grounds of the lead actor's visible [[erectile dysfunction]] and instead labeled the film "anti-porn", asking "How else do you categorize an adult film that completely and utterly fails to elicit even the minutest amount of arousal in its viewers?"<ref name="BPAVClub">{{cite web |url=http://avmaniacs.com/features/bat_pussy.html |title=Deep Inside Bat Pussy |author=Allison, Matthew |publisher=AV Maniacs |access-date=March 24, 2016 |archive-date=October 26, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151026200719/http://avmaniacs.com/features/bat_pussy.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The book ''The Many More Lives of Batman'' by [[William Uricchio]] and [[Will Brooker]] also labeled ''Bat Pussy'' "the worst porn film ever made", criticizing its poor adaptation of the source material.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lj3-rQEACAAJ&q=%22Bat+Pussy%22&pg=PA115 |title=The Many More Lives of Batman |author1=Pearson, Rebecca |author2=Brooker, Will |author3=Uriccho, William |date=2015 |isbn=978-1844577644 |publisher=[[British Film Institute]] |access-date=February 27, 2024 |archive-date=February 27, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240227175609/https://books.google.com/books?id=lj3-rQEACAAJ&q=%22Bat+Pussy%22&pg=PA115 |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== ''At Long Last Love'' (theatrical version, 1975) ===
{{Main|At Long Last Love{{!}}''At Long Last Love''}}
[[File:Peter Bogdanovich.jpg|thumb|left|Filmmaker [[Peter Bogdanovich]] initially apologized for ''[[At Long Last Love]]'', once described as "the worst musical extravaganza in Hollywood history", but an updated cut of the film has met with critical reevaluation.]]
''At Long Last Love'' was renowned director [[Peter Bogdanovich]]'s musical homage to great 1930s Hollywood musicals. It features songs by [[Cole Porter]] and stars [[Cybill Shepherd]] and [[Burt Reynolds]]. ''[[Film Threat]]'' wrote that it received "the most withering reviews any film ever received", while ''[[The Guardian]]'' reported that it was "savaged by critics at the time and viewed as one of the worst films ever".<ref>{{cite web |title=The Bootleg Files: At Long Last Love |url=https://filmthreat.com/uncategorized/the-bootleg-files-at-long-last-love/ |work=[[Film Threat]] |access-date=July 19, 2022 |date=May 5, 2006 |archive-date=July 19, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220719171530/https://filmthreat.com/uncategorized/the-bootleg-files-at-long-last-love/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Peter Bogdanovich: a life in pictures |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/gallery/2022/jan/06/peter-bogdanovich-a-life-in-pictures |website=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=July 13, 2022 |date=January 6, 2022 |archive-date=July 13, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220713143336/https://www.theguardian.com/film/gallery/2022/jan/06/peter-bogdanovich-a-life-in-pictures |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Richard Brody]] of ''[[The New Yorker]]'' compared it to the later critical failures of ''[[Heaven's Gate (film)|Heaven's Gate]]'' and ''[[Ishtar (film)|Ishtar]]'', writing: "critics of the time heaven's-gated [''At Long Last Love''], leaving Bogdanovich ishtarred and feathered".<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Brody |first=Richard |author-link=Richard Brody |title=How Peter Bogdanovich Shaped the Backstory of Modern Cinema |url=https://www.newyorker.com/culture/postscript/how-peter-bogdanovich-shaped-the-backstory-of-modern-cinema |magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |access-date=July 13, 2022 |date=January 7, 2022 |archive-date=May 30, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220530220647/https://www.newyorker.com/culture/postscript/how-peter-bogdanovich-shaped-the-backstory-of-modern-cinema |url-status=live }}</ref> Such reviews included [[Hollis Alpert]]'s, in which he said that "This failure is so dismal that it goes beyond failure",<ref>{{cite book |last=Tookey |first=Christopher |title =Named and Shamed: The World's Worst and Wittiest Movie Reviews from Affleck to Zeta-Jones |publisher =Troubador Publishing |year =2010 |page =34 |isbn =978-1-84876-560-3}}</ref> and ''[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire]]'' critic [[John Simon (critic)|John Simon]]'s, who said that "it may be the worst movie musical of this – or any – decade".<ref name=PictureShows>{{cite book |last=Yule |first=Andrew |title =Picture shows: the life and films of Peter Bogdanovich |publisher =[[Hal Leonard Corporation]] |year =1992 |page =[https://archive.org/details/pictureshowslife00yule/page/90 90] |isbn =0-87910-153-9 |url =https://archive.org/details/pictureshowslife00yule/page/90 }}</ref> Meanwhile, ''[[Buffalo News]]'' film critic Jeff Simon wrote, "About 45 minutes in, it became apparent to one and all that this was one of the worst and most embarrassing major-talent turkeys of all time."<ref name="BufNews">{{cite news |title=Wisecrack Addicts Laughing at the Not-So-Bad |url=http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=BN&p_theme=bn&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0EAF994638769706&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D |newspaper=[[The Buffalo News]] |date=May 24, 1996 |author=Simon, Jeff |access-date=October 11, 2011 |archive-date=November 1, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181101095439/http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=BN&p_theme=bn&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0EAF994638769706&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D |url-status=live }}</ref> Bogdanovich, who was also the screenwriter, sent press releases to newspapers across the country apologizing for the film.<ref name=SinginANewTune/>

[[CNN]] later noted that it had attained a legacy as being "the worst musical extravaganza in Hollywood history",<ref name="longlastcnn">{{cite news|url=http://www.cnn.com/2013/07/10/showbiz/movies/big-bombs-revisited|title=Picking up the pieces on Hollywood's biggest bombs|last=Leopold|first=Todd|date=July 11, 2013|access-date=August 23, 2013|publisher=[[CNN]]|archive-date=August 18, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130818030235/http://www.cnn.com/2013/07/10/showbiz/movies/big-bombs-revisited|url-status=live}}</ref> and [[Jay Cocks]] has said the film was "regarded as the great [[white elephant]] catastrophe of its time".<ref name=SinginANewTune>{{cite book |last=Muir |first=John Kenneth |title =Singing a new tune:the rebirth of the modern film musical, from Evita to De-lovely and beyond |publisher =[[Hal Leonard Corporation]] |year =2005 |page =[https://archive.org/details/singingnewtunere0000muir/page/58 58] |isbn =1-55783-610-8 |url =https://archive.org/details/singingnewtunere0000muir/page/58 }}</ref> Lester J. Keyser wrote that it was "justly included on most lists of the ten worst films ever made",<ref>{{cite book |last=Keyser |first=Lester J. |title=Hollywood in the Seventies |date=1981 |publisher=A.S. Barnes |location=Los Angeles, California |isbn=0498025454 |page=85}}</ref> as it was included in Michael Sauter's ''The Worst Films of All Time'', ''The Golden Turkey Awards'' and ''Vanity Fair'''s worst film list.{{sfn|Medved|1978|p=37}}<ref name=Goldenturkeys>{{cite book |last=Medved |first=Michael |title =The Golden Turkey Awards |publisher =[[G. P. Putnam's Sons]] |year =1980 |page =209 |isbn =0-399-50463-X|title-link =The Golden Turkey Awards }}</ref><ref name="italianvanity"/>

Bogdanovich lamented being influenced by studio previews to cut the film before its theatrical release. Unbeknownst to Bogdanovich, a studio editor who preferred the director's first cut constructed his own based on the test screening version that he once had access to. This version subsequently aired on cable TV and streamed on [[Netflix]] in place of the theatrical cut. When news of this reached Bogdanovich, he contacted Fox and made a few finishing touches, resulting in a better received director's cut that debuted on [[home video]] in 2013.<ref>{{cite web|last=McWeeny |first=Drew |url=http://www.hitfix.com/blogs/motion-captured/posts/peter-bogdanovich-screens-new-cut-of-at-long-last-love-and-tells-story-behind-it |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120217194802/http://www.hitfix.com/blogs/motion-captured/posts/peter-bogdanovich-screens-new-cut-of-at-long-last-love-and-tells-story-behind-it |title=Peter Bogdanovich screens new cut of At Long Last Love and tells story behind it |website=[[Hitfix]] |date=January 9, 2012 |access-date=March 5, 2014 |archive-date=February 17, 2012}}</ref><ref name=longlastcnn/>

=== ''Exorcist II: The Heretic'' (1977) ===
{{Main|Exorcist II: The Heretic{{!}}''Exorcist II: The Heretic''}}
''Exorcist II: The Heretic'' is the sequel to [[William Friedkin]]'s [[Academy Awards|Oscar]]-winning [[The Exorcist|1973 film]], this time directed by [[John Boorman]]. Friedkin opted not to return to direct the sequel and ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]'' states that Boorman "hated the original" and intended ''The Heretic'' to be an "antidote [...] to wash away the evil of Friedkin's film."<ref name="exorcist2">{{cite web |last=Fordy |first=Tom |title='The worst film ever made'? Why Exorcist II: The Heretic is truly the sequel from hell |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/films/0/exorcist-2-the-heretic-linda-blair-richard-burton/ |website=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |access-date=October 28, 2023 |date=October 3, 2023 |archive-date=October 28, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231028125349/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/films/0/exorcist-2-the-heretic-linda-blair-richard-burton/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Set four years after the first film, [[Linda Blair]] reprised her role as [[Regan MacNeil]], who is revealed to have healing powers, and [[Richard Burton]] stars as Father Philip Lamont, who believes that the demon [[Pazuzu (The Exorcist)|Pazuzu]] targets those with healing abilities.<ref name="guardianworst"/> Blair agreed to return for the sequel as long as she did not have to wear the possession make-up from the first film, leading to the use of an unconvincing [[body double]], while Burton read his lines off cue cards.<ref name="exorcist2"/> Despite [[Lankester Merrin|his character]] dying in the original film, [[Max von Sydow]] returned for flashback sequences set in Africa, where Lamont flies to on the back of a [[locust]].<ref name="exorcist2"/>

''The Daily Telegraph'' notes that some consider it the worst film ever made.<ref name="exorcist2"/> British film critic [[Mark Kermode]] called the original film his favorite film of all time but believes the sequel to be the worst film ever made, stating, "This is a film that trashes a work of art. It's like someone deciding to do a ''[[Mona Lisa]] 2'', but with a moustache."<ref name="guardianworst">{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2004/jul/02/1 |title='If I'd made that, I'd change my name' |access-date=December 1, 2013 |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |archive-date=December 3, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203135052/http://www.theguardian.com/film/2004/jul/02/1 |url-status=live }}</ref> The ''Golden Turkey Awards'' named it the second-worst film ever made, after ''Plan 9 from Outer Space'', and it also appeared in ''The Official Razzie Movie Guide''. ''[[The A.V. Club]]'' listed it as the worst sequel of all time and critic Bill Chambers stated it was "Possibly the worst film ever made and surely the worst sequel ever made."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/exorcist_ii_the_heretic/reviews/ |title=Exorcist II – The Heretic Reviews |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |publisher=[[Fandango Media|Fandango]] |access-date=April 16, 2019 |archive-date=April 28, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190428150130/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/exorcist_ii_the_heretic/reviews/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The 25 worst sequels of all time |url=https://www.avclub.com/the-25-worst-sequels-of-all-time-1850799210/slides/26 |website=The A.V. Club |access-date=October 28, 2023 |language=en |date=September 8, 2023 |archive-date=October 28, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231028125412/https://www.avclub.com/the-25-worst-sequels-of-all-time-1850799210/slides/26 |url-status=live}}</ref> Friedkin believed the sequel diminished the value of the original film and called it "the worst piece of shit I've ever seen" and "a fucking disgrace."<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.cinemablend.com/news/2464836/original-exorcist-director-says-the-sequel-was-the-worst-movie-hes-ever-seen |title=Original Exorcist Director Says The Sequel Was The Worst Movie He's Ever Seen |publisher=[[CinemaBlend]] |date=January 9, 2019 |access-date=January 20, 2019 |last=Libbey |first=Dirk |archive-date=January 21, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190121064119/https://www.cinemablend.com/news/2464836/original-exorcist-director-says-the-sequel-was-the-worst-movie-hes-ever-seen|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.blastr.com/2013-4-15/exorcist-director-says-sequel-one-worst-films-ive-ever-seen |title=Exorcist director says sequel is 'one of the worst films I've ever seen' |access-date=December 1, 2013 |date=April 15, 2013 |first=Don |last=Kaye |publisher=[[Blastr]] |archive-date=August 4, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130804174243/http://www.blastr.com/2013-4-15/exorcist-director-says-sequel-one-worst-films-ive-ever-seen |url-status=dead}}</ref> Eventually, the film garnered so much hate that Boorman disowned it. In an interview with Bob McCabe for the book ''The Exorcist: Out of the Shadows'', he confessed, "The sin I committed was not giving the audience what it wanted in terms of horror."<ref>{{cite book |last=McCabe |first=Bob |title=The Exorcist: Out of the Shadows |publisher=[[Omnibus Press]] |date=1999 |page=164 |isbn=9780711975095}}</ref> A third installment in the [[The Exorcist (franchise)|''Exorcist'' franchise]], ''[[The Exorcist III: Legion]]'', was released in 1990 and would in later years gain a cult following,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://bloody-disgusting.com/editorials/3578046/masterpiece-exorcist-iii-nearly-turns-30-finally-getting-due/ |title=Nearly 30 Years Later, Masterpiece 'The Exorcist III' is Finally Getting Its Due |last=Kurland |first=Daniel |website=[[Bloody Disgusting]] |date=August 16, 2019}}</ref> with author Nat Segaloff writing that, "The first rule of ''Exorcist III'' is: you do not talk about ''Exorcist II''."<ref name="exorcist2"/>

=== ''The Swarm'' (1978) ===
{{Main|The Swarm (1978 film){{!}}''The Swarm'' (1978 film)}}
''The Swarm'' is a 1978 horror film about a [[Africanized bee|killer bee]] invasion of [[Texas]], directed and produced by [[Irwin Allen]]. Despite its all-star cast (including [[Michael Caine]], [[Henry Fonda]], [[Richard Widmark]] and [[Olivia de Havilland]]), it was a box-office failure and was excoriated by reviewers.<ref name="ts">''Halliwell's film and video guide 2002'' edited by John Walker. London. HarperCollins Entertainment, 2001. {{ISBN|0-00-712265-9}} (p. 804).</ref> On its UK release, ''[[The Sunday Times]]'' described ''The Swarm'' as "simply the worst film ever made".<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/culture/2001/apr/26/artsfeatures2 |title=The worst movie ever? |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131111042603/http://www.theguardian.com/culture/2001/apr/26/artsfeatures2 |archive-date=November 11, 2013 |work=The Guardian |date=April 26, 2001 |access-date=March 29, 2014}}</ref> [[Leslie Halliwell]] described it as a "very obvious disaster movie with risible dialogue".<ref name="ts"/> ''[[The Guardian]]'' article on ''The Swarm'' stated, "You could pass it all off as a sick joke, except it cost twelve million dollars, twenty-two million bees, and several years of someone's life."<ref name="ts"/> [[Barry Took]], reviewing it for ''[[Punch (magazine)|Punch]]'', stated, "the story is of a banality matched only by the woodenness of the acting".<ref name="ts"/> ''[[Time Out (magazine)|Time Out]]'' magazine called ''The Swarm'' a "risibly inadequate disaster movie".<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.timeout.com/london/film/the-swarm |title=The Swarm |work=Time Out London |date=September 10, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191115053443/https://www.timeout.com/london/film/the-swarm |archive-date=November 15, 2019 |access-date=March 29, 2014}}</ref> ''The Swarm'' is included in several "worst movie" books, including the Medved brothers' ''The Golden Turkey Awards'',<ref>Mikel J. Koven, ''Film, Folklore and Urban Legends''. Scarecrow Press, 2008 {{ISBN|0-8108-6025-2}} (p. 91)</ref> and ''The Official Razzie Movie Guide''.<ref name="Wilson 2005">{{cite book|last=Wilson|first=John|title=The Official Razzie Movie Guide: Enjoying the Best of Hollywood's Worst |year=2005|publisher=Grand Central Publishing|isbn=0-446-69334-0}}</ref> It soon gained a [[cult following|cult status]] (enough so that [[Warner Archive]] released the extended version on [[Blu-ray]]).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bloody-disgusting.com/home-video/3517106/warner-archive-releasing-extended-version-1978s-swarm-blu-ray/|title=Warner Archive Releasing Extended Version of 1978's 'The Swarm' on Blu-ray|first=John|last=Squires|date=August 22, 2018|access-date=January 11, 2019|archive-date=January 12, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190112044300/https://bloody-disgusting.com/home-video/3517106/warner-archive-releasing-extended-version-1978s-swarm-blu-ray/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://addictedtohorrormovies.com/2017/07/14/on-this-day-in-horror-history-the-mind-boggling-the-swarm-hit-theaters/|title=On This Day in Horror History: The Mind Boggling 'The Swarm' Hit Theaters|date=July 14, 2017|access-date=January 11, 2019|archive-date=January 11, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190111232542/https://addictedtohorrormovies.com/2017/07/14/on-this-day-in-horror-history-the-mind-boggling-the-swarm-hit-theaters/|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== ''I Spit on Your Grave'' (1978) ===
{{Main|I Spit on Your Grave{{!}}''I Spit on Your Grave''}}
''I Spit on Your Grave'' became controversial for its graphic violence and lengthy depictions of gang rape.<ref>{{cite web |last=Floorwalker |first=Mike |title=Roger Ebert's Most Brutal Movie Takedowns Of All Time |url=https://www.grunge.com/125308/roger-eberts-most-brutal-movie-reviews-ever/ |website=[[Grunge.com]] |access-date=January 17, 2022 |date=June 7, 2018 |archive-date=January 28, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220128122409/https://www.grunge.com/125308/roger-eberts-most-brutal-movie-reviews-ever/ |url-status=live }}</ref> It was initially unable to find a distributor until 1980 when it received a wider release. Luke Y. Thompson of the ''[[New Times LA|New Times]]'' stated, "Defenders of the film have argued that it's actually pro-woman, due to the fact that the female lead wins in the end, which is sort of like saying that cockfights are pro-rooster because there's always one left standing".<ref name="Spiton">{{cite web|url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/i_spit_on_your_grave|title=I Spit on Your Grave (Day of the Woman)|website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]]|publisher=[[Fandango Media|Fandango]]|access-date=April 16, 2019|archive-date=April 14, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190414200846/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/i_spit_on_your_grave|url-status=live}}</ref> Critic David Keyes named ''I Spit on Your Grave'' the worst film of the 1980s and James Livingston wrote in ''The World Turned Inside Out'' that it was "a terrifically bad movie".<ref>{{cite book |url=http://hnn.us/articles/121079.html#:~:text=The%20excerpt%20that%20follows%20is%20drawn%20from%20Chapters,Intellectual%20History%20Conference%20at%20CUNY%20on%20November%2012th |first=James |last=Livingston |title=The World Turned Inside Out: American Thought and Culture at the End of the 20th Century |publisher=[[Rowman & Littlefield]] |year=2011 |isbn=978-0742535428 |page=189 |access-date=August 10, 2020 |archive-date=September 24, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210924182041/http://hnn.us/articles/121079.html#:~:text=The%20excerpt%20that%20follows%20is%20drawn%20from%20Chapters,Intellectual%20History%20Conference%20at%20CUNY%20on%20November%2012th |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Spiton"/> Scott Tobias of ''The A.V. Club'' called it "one of the era's most abhorrent pieces of exploitation trash"<ref>{{cite news |url=https://avclub.com/article/emi-spit-on-your-graveem-2010-53367 |title=I Spit On Your Grave (2010) |first=Scott |last=Tobias |date=March 21, 2011 |newspaper=[[The A.V. Club]] |access-date=November 12, 2019 |archive-date=October 25, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231025172917/https://www.avclub.com/i-spit-on-your-grave-2010-1798224700 |url-status=live }}</ref> and Patrick Naugle of DVD Verdict stated, "It's one of the most soulless, vile, and morally reprehensible things I've ever had to sit through."<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://dvdverdict.com/reviews/dontmesssister.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040426083712/https://dvdverdict.com/reviews/dontmesssister.php |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 26, 2004 |title=Don't Mess With My Sister |first=Patrick |last=Naugle |date=February 15, 2002 |publisher=[[DVD Verdict]] }}</ref> Roger Ebert gave the film no stars, referring to it as "A vile bag of garbage ... without a shred of artistic distinction," adding, "Attending it was one of the most depressing experiences of my life"<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/i-spit-on-your-grave-1980 |title=Review of ''I Spit on Your Grave'' |access-date=October 11, 2020 |first=Roger |last=Ebert |author-link=Roger Ebert |date=July 16, 1980 |newspaper=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |archive-date=October 24, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211024112255/https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/i-spit-on-your-grave-1980 |url-status=live }}</ref> and considered it the worst movie ever made.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://beaconnews.suntimes.com/news/2247859-418/ebert-movie-chaz-roger-writer.html |title=Movie, journalism fans queue up to see Ebert |access-date=March 20, 2007 |first=Steve |last=Lord |date=November 7, 2010 |newspaper=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101111153312/http://beaconnews.suntimes.com/news/2247859-418/ebert-movie-chaz-roger-writer.html |archive-date=November 11, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Video Q&A |last=Ebert |first=Roger |author-link=Roger Ebert |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=0U9IAAAAIBAJ&pg=2655,5621128&dq=roger+ebert+i+spit+on+your+grave+worst+ever |newspaper=[[The Ledger]] |date=May 28, 1998 |access-date=November 3, 2013 |archive-date=February 13, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220213185938/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=0U9IAAAAIBAJ&pg=2655%2C5621128&dq=roger+ebert+i+spit+on+your+grave+worst+ever |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Gene Siskel]] also considered it one of the worst films ever made.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://chicagotribune.newspapers.com/clip/80954901/gene-siskel-movie-reviewsthe-man-who/ |title='Man Who Wasn't There' would best be left unseen |access-date=January 3, 2023 |first=Gene |last=Siskel |author-link=Gene Siskel |date=August 17, 1983 |newspaper=[[Chicago Tribune]] |archive-date=January 3, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230103203334/https://chicagotribune.newspapers.com/clip/80954901/gene-siskel-movie-reviewsthe-man-who/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Film Racket'' featured it as their first entry in to their "Worst Movie Ever?" series,<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://filmracket.com/worst-movie-ever-i-spit-on-your-grave/ |title=Worst Movie Ever? I Spit On Your Grave |first=Pete |last=Croatto |date=May 1, 2013 |work=Film Racket |access-date=July 31, 2015 |archive-date=September 11, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150911070207/http://filmracket.com/worst-movie-ever-i-spit-on-your-grave/ |url-status=usurped }}</ref> while ''Vanity Fair'' and ''Flavorwire'' included it in their worst film lists.<ref name="italianvanity"/><ref name="Flavorwire"/> Despite the intense negative reception from some critics, the film has a 53% rating on Rotten Tomatoes,<ref name="Spiton"/> with ''[[IGN]]'' critic R.L. Shaffer arguing that whether the film is repulsive and exploitative or ingenious depends on what the viewer wants from the movie: "Admittedly, ''I Spit on Your Grave'' is a gruesome, deplorable little exploitation picture that, on the surface, seems to enjoy its rape sequences just as much, if not more, than the vengeance-filled finale. But on a more subtle level, the film is a surprisingly well-executed revenge story that plays like a brutally raw nerve – a terrifyingly stark view of the real horror of rape, painted by bizarre, skewed cinematography, gory violence, and a keen sense of creeping atmosphere and dread."<ref>{{cite web |last=Shaffer |first=R. L. |title=I Spit on Your Grave (1978) Blu-Ray Review |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2011/02/04/i-spit-on-your-grave-1978-blu-ray-review |website=[[IGN]] |access-date=February 1, 2022 |date=February 4, 2011 |archive-date=February 1, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220201230500/https://www.ign.com/articles/2011/02/04/i-spit-on-your-grave-1978-blu-ray-review |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== ''Caligula'' (theatrical version, 1979) ===
{{Main|Caligula (film){{!}}''Caligula'' (film)}}
The 1979 erotic historical drama ''Caligula'', directed by [[Tinto Brass]] about the infamous Roman emperor [[Caligula]], was in part financed by ''[[Penthouse magazine|Penthouse]]'' founder [[Bob Guccione]]. The film, featuring a prestigious cast ([[Malcolm McDowell]], [[Helen Mirren]], [[Peter O'Toole]], and [[John Gielgud]]) is notorious for explicit scenes of sex and violence, including six minutes of hardcore porn footage filmed by Guccione and another editor without Brass' approval. ''Caligula'' earned some pre-release controversy after [[Gore Vidal]], who had written the script, distanced himself from the film,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://siskelebert.org/?p=6694|title=The Worst Movies of 1980 – Siskel and Ebert Movie Reviews|website=siskelebert.org|access-date=April 14, 2021|archive-date=April 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210414233852/https://siskelebert.org/?p=6694|url-status=live}}</ref> and actress [[Maria Schneider (actress)|Maria Schneider]], who objected to the nude scenes, walked off the set and was replaced with then-unknown [[Teresa Ann Savoy]].<ref name="timevidal">{{cite magazine |title=Show Business: Will the Real Caligula Stand Up? |url=https://content.time.com/time/subscriber/article/0,33009,947822-1,00.html |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |access-date=January 18, 2022 |date=January 3, 1977 |archive-date=January 18, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220118183135/http://content.time.com/time/subscriber/article/0,33009,947822-1,00.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Upon its release, Vidal stated that it was "easily one of the worst films ever made".<ref name="timevidal"/>

''Caligula'' also received strongly hostile reviews from critics, who denounced its extreme scenes of sex and violence and lack of narrative coherence.<ref name="ebert19800922">{{cite news |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/caligula-1980 |title=Caligula movie review & film summary (1980) |newspaper=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |first=Roger |last=Ebert |author-link=Roger Ebert |date=September 22, 1980 |access-date=October 11, 2020 |archive-date=October 7, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201007010030/https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/caligula-1980 |url-status=live }}</ref> Roger Ebert gave ''Caligula'' a zero-star rating, dubbing it "sickening, utterly worthless, shameful trash", accusing it of being artistically vulgar in its depiction of sex and violence, and of having technically incompetent direction and structure.<ref name="ebert19800922"/> It was one of the few films Ebert ever walked out on (two hours into its 170-minute running time), after describing himself as feeling "disgusted and unspeakably depressed".<ref name="ebert19800922"/><ref>{{cite news|url=http://blogs.suntimes.com/ebert/2008/10/dont_read_me_first.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081018181430/http://blogs.suntimes.com/ebert/2008/10/dont_read_me_first.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 18, 2008 |title=Don't read me first! |first=Roger |last=Ebert |author-link=Roger Ebert |date=October 16, 2008 |work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |access-date=June 9, 2012}}</ref> Ebert also placed it on his "Most Hated" list and Michael Sauter selected it for ''The Worst Movies of All Time''.<ref name="eberthated">{{cite news|url=https://www.rogerebert.com/roger-ebert/eberts-most-hated |title=Ebert's Most Hated |work=[[RogerEbert.com]] |date=August 11, 2005 |last=Ebert |first=Roger |author-link=Roger Ebert |access-date=January 17, 2011}}</ref>{{sfn|Sauter|page=266}} Australian newspaper ''[[The Age]]'' stated that ''Caligula'' was being "billed by critics everywhere as one of the worst films ever made".<ref>{{cite news |title=News Diary |journal=[[The Age]] |date=June 8, 1981 |page=2}}</ref> ''[[The Hamilton Spectator]]'' later referred to ''Caligula'' as "possibly the worst movie ever made".<ref>{{cite news |title=Lowest: 100 Really Bad Moments in 20th Century Entertainment |journal=[[The Hamilton Spectator]] |date=July 24, 1999 |page=W17}}</ref> Joe Holleman, in an article in the ''[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]]'' discussing historical films set in Ancient Rome, argued, "two of the worst movies made in the 20th century were ancient Rome pieces ... ''[[Cleopatra (1963 film)|Cleopatra]]'' and ''Caligula''".<ref>{{cite news |first=Joe |last=Holleman |title=Roman Warriors roam the big screen again |journal=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]] |date=May 5, 2000 |page=E1}}</ref> Christopher Armstead, reviewing ''Caligula'' for the website Film Critics United, stated, "Dollar for dollar, this could very well be the worst movie ever made."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://filmcriticsunited.com/caligula.html |title=Caligula |first=Christopher |last=Armstead |work=Film Critics United |access-date=January 10, 2014 |archive-date=January 10, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110125709/http://filmcriticsunited.com/caligula.html |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2011, Sean Bell of ''[[PopMatters]]'' wrote of its enduring legacy: "in the same way much of our attention-deficit civilisation may go through life vaguely aware that ''[[Citizen Kane]]'' is a masterpiece without ever seeing it, ... we know that ''Caligula'' is awful, usually without ever finding out for ourselves."<ref>{{cite web |last=Bell |first=Sean |title='Caligula's Ghost: Why Cinema Needs Epic Failure More than Mediocre Success, PopMatters |url=https://www.popmatters.com/151468-caligulas-ghost-why-cinema-needs-epic-failure-more-than-mediocre-suc-2495917054.html |website=[[PopMatters]] |access-date=January 18, 2022 |date=December 1, 2011 |archive-date=January 18, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220118182706/https://www.popmatters.com/151468-caligulas-ghost-why-cinema-needs-epic-failure-more-than-mediocre-suc-2495917054.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Although widely criticized, the film's "over-the-top combination of outré aesthetics [and] exploitation-film tropes" has gained it cult status over time, and in 2024, [[Thomas Negovan]] released an extensive re-edit, ''Caligula: The Ultimate Cut'', incorporating alternate takes and unused footage from the ''Penthouse'' archives to enhance narrative coherence while shortening the film's overall length. In a review in ''The New York Times'', Elisabeth Vincentelli said that it is a "rare re-edited version of a movie that features ''less'' graphic sex and violence than the original."<ref name=NYTCaligula>{{cite news |last=Vincentelli |first=Elisabeth |title='Caligula: The Ultimate Cut' Review: The Emperor's New Clothes |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/08/15/movies/caligula-the-ultimate-cut-review.html |url-access=limited |date=August 15, 2024 |access-date=August 15, 2024 |work=The New York Times |location=New York City |quote=Even more crucial is the belief that a masterpiece lurks within the mangled original release. Now attempting to prove that theory is "Caligula: The Ultimate Cut," the latest iteration of a film that has gone through an unfathomable number of edits over the decades. This is the rare re-edited version of a movie that features ''less'' graphic sex and violence than the original. What kind of world are we living in?}}</ref> In an interview with ''The Guardian'', McDowell praised the removal of sexually explicit material added by Guccione, and said ''The Ultimate Cut'' is "very much the movie I thought I was making".<ref>{{cite news |last=Pelley |first=Rich |title=Malcolm McDowell: 'Kubrick had stewed pears and sour chicken for lunch because Napoleon did' |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/article/2024/aug/01/malcolm-mcdowell-kubrick-had-stewed-pears-and-chicken-for-lunch-because-napoleon-did |work=The Guardian |location=London |date=August 1, 2024 |access-date=August 15, 2024}}</ref> ''The Ultimate Cut'' holds a 65% rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on 40 reviews;<ref>{{cite web |title=Caligula: The Ultimate Cut |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/caligula_the_ultimate_cut |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |access-date=March 24, 2025 |publisher=[[Fandango Media|Fandango]] |language=en }}</ref> however, Brass has publicly disowned it.<ref name=NYTCaligula/>

== 1980s ==

=== ''Heaven's Gate'' (theatrical version, 1980) ===
{{Main|Heaven's Gate (film){{!}}''Heaven's Gate'' (film)}}
