[[File:MichaelCiminoCannes1981.jpg|thumb|upright|The theatrical cut of ''[[Heaven's Gate (film)|Heaven's Gate]]'' destroyed the reputation of director [[Michael Cimino]] and bankrupted film distributor [[United Artists]],<ref name="bad cinema">[https://www.google.com/books/edition/Exploring_Film_through_Bad_Cinema/Sj1nEQAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1 Exploring Film Through Bad Cinema – Google Books (ch. "Heaven's Gate and the New Hollywood")]</ref> though re-edits of the film have been met with critical reevaluation.]]
The [[Western (genre)|Western]] epic ''[[Heaven's Gate (film)|Heaven's Gate]]'', loosely based on the [[Johnson County War]] in 1890s [[Wyoming]], was plagued by massive cost and time overruns, largely due to director [[Michael Cimino]]'s extreme attention to detail. He demanded 50 takes of at least one scene and refused to start shooting for another until a cloud he liked rolled across the sky. It cost over $44 million, but brought in only $3.5 million at the [[box office]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Bukszpan |first=Daniel |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2012/03/20/The-15-Biggest-Box-Office-Bombs.html?slide=9 |title=The 15 Biggest Box Office Bombs -> 8. Heaven's Gate (1980) |publisher=[[CNBC]] |date=March 20, 2012 |access-date=October 11, 2020 |archive-date=June 10, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110610231738/http://www.cnbc.com/id/38815985?slide=9 |url-status=live }}</ref> The original version ran at nearly four hours, but was pulled from release after only one week due to scathing reviews. It later resurfaced in a 149-minute version, but by then the damage was done. The film effectively ended not only the existence of [[United Artists]] as an independent Hollywood studio (its parent firm sold the company to [[Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer]], where it operated until 2019), but also, largely, Cimino's career; initially considered a director on the rise after directing ''[[The Deer Hunter]]'' (which won five Oscars, including Best Picture and Best Director), his reputation never recovered after ''Heaven's Gate''.<ref name="50decisions"/> The production is also notorious for the cruelty to animals that occurred both on screen and on site, including deliberately killing a horse with explosives.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1986/03/24/movies/cruel-camera-about-animal-abuse.html |date=March 24, 1986 |last=Corry |first=John |title='Cruel, Camera,' About Animal Abuse |work=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=October 11, 2020 |archive-date=February 17, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210217004121/https://www.nytimes.com/1986/03/24/movies/cruel-camera-about-animal-abuse.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The controversies surrounding ''Heaven's Gate''{{'}}s failure are credited for having a role in ending the "[[New Hollywood|auteur period]]" of the 1970s, with studios subsequently taking control back from directors.<ref name="50decisions"/>

[[Vincent Canby]] called it "an unqualified disaster", among other things. Roger Ebert called it "the most scandalous cinematic waste I've ever seen".<ref>{{cite news |author-link=Roger Ebert |last=Ebert |first=Roger |date=January 1, 1981 |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/heavens-gate-1981 |title=Heaven's Gate movie review & film summary (1981) |work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |access-date=October 11, 2020 |archive-date=October 17, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191017192105/https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/heavens-gate-1981 |url-status=live }}</ref> After word of his grandiose spending and defiant nature toward studio United Artists got out (detailed in ''Final Cut'' by [[Steven Bach]], a studio executive involved with the film from the beginning),<ref>{{cite book |url=https://archive.org/details/finalcutartmoney00bach |url-access=registration |page=[https://archive.org/details/finalcutartmoney00bach/page/6 6] |quote=heaven's gate april 16 1979. |isbn=9781557043740 |title=Final Cut: Art, Money, and Ego in the Making of Heaven's Gate, the Film that Sank United Artists |year=1999 |publisher=[[Newmarket Press]] |last=Bach |first=Steven |author-link=Steven Bach}}</ref> Cimino was awarded the 1980 [[Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Director]], and the film was nominated for four more Razzies, including Worst Picture.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://razzies.com/asp/content/XcNewsPlus.asp?cmd=view&articleid=21 |title=Summary of 1981 Razzies |work=Razzies.com |access-date=December 19, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140116032635/http://razzies.com/asp/content/XcNewsPlus.asp?cmd=view&articleid=21 |archive-date=January 16, 2014}}</ref> In 1999, ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' placed the film on a list of the 100 worst ideas of the 20th century, and ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' ranked it as one of the worst decisions in movie history.<ref name="worstideas"/><ref name="50decisions"/> In 2008, [[Joe Queenan (author)|Joe Queenan]] of ''[[The Guardian]]'' called it the worst film ever made, saying that it "defies belief".<ref name="queenan">{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2008/mar/21/1|title=Joe Queenan on the worst movie of all time|last=Queenan|first=Joe|author-link=Joe Queenan (author)|date=March 21, 2008|work=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=December 28, 2018|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077}}</ref> Readers of film magazine ''[[Empire (film magazine)|Empire]]'' later voted ''Heaven's Gate'' the sixth-worst film of all time, and ''Vanity Fair'' included it in its list of the worst films ever made.<ref name="The 50 Worst Movies Ever">{{cite web |url = https://www.empireonline.com/movies/features/50-worst-movies-ever-2/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200201223813/https://www.empireonline.com/movies/features/50-worst-movies-ever-2/ |title = The 50 Worst Movies Ever | work=[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]] |date=February 4, 2010 |archive-date=February 1, 2020 |access-date = March 17, 2014}}</ref><ref name="italianvanity"/>

Despite the vicious reviews, the film's reputation improved over time.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.newyorker.com/culture/richard-brody/movie-of-the-week-heavens-gate |last=Brody |first=Richard |author-link=Richard Brody |title=Movie of the Week: "Heaven's Gate" |magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |date=November 25, 2015 |access-date=October 11, 2020 |archive-date=September 26, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200926084352/https://www.newyorker.com/culture/richard-brody/movie-of-the-week-heavens-gate |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Holmes |first=Linda |title='My Year Of Flops': A Very Good Book About Some Very Bad Movies |url=https://www.npr.org/2010/10/19/130669942/my-year-of-flops-a-very-good-book-about-some-very-bad-movies |publisher=[[NPR]] |access-date=January 22, 2022 |language=en |date=October 19, 2010 |archive-date=February 2, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230202035326/https://www.npr.org/2010/10/19/130669942/my-year-of-flops-a-very-good-book-about-some-very-bad-movies |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="2024lineup">{{Cite web |date=Feb 14, 2024 |title=The Criterion Channel's March 2024 Lineup |url=https://www.criterion.com/current/posts/8388-the-criterion-channels-march-2024-lineup |website=The Criterion Channel |access-date=March 1, 2024 |archive-date=March 1, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240301234818/https://www.criterion.com/current/posts/8388-the-criterion-channels-march-2024-lineup |url-status=live }}</ref> In fall of 2012, the [[New York Film Festival]], the venue for its infamous opening, premiered the restored director's cut. In stark contrast, ''[[The Times]]'' called the restored version "a modern masterpiece" and its 1980 cut "one of the greatest injustices of cinematic history".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thetimes.com/world/us-world/article/heavens-gate-box-office-turkey-that-sank-a-studio-is-a-modern-masterpiece-vb8fdjn5mkm |title=Heaven's Gate: box office turkey that sank a studio is a modern masterpiece |last=Hoyle |first=Ben |newspaper=[[The Times]] |date=October 1, 2012 |access-date=November 18, 2013 |archive-date=August 26, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160826001131/http://www.thetimes.co.uk/tto/arts/film/article3554129.ece |url-status=live }}</ref> The film has also been released on Blu-ray and DVD by the [[Criterion Collection]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.criterion.com/films/28036-heaven-s-gate|title=Heaven's Gate|website=The Criterion Collection|access-date=November 15, 2018|archive-date=November 16, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181116000911/https://www.criterion.com/films/28036-heaven-s-gate|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Manohla Dargis]] of ''[[The New York Times]]'' said that the film "has been called a disaster and a disgrace, yet also anointed a masterpiece".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/03/17/movies/michael-ciminos-heavens-gate-returns-to-film-forum.html |title=The Second Coming of 'Heaven's Gate' |last=Dargis |first=Manohla |author-link=Manohla Dargis |date=March 15, 2013 |access-date=June 13, 2013 |work=[[The New York Times]] |archive-date=March 25, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130325031349/http://www.nytimes.com/2013/03/17/movies/michael-ciminos-heavens-gate-returns-to-film-forum.html |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2023, the French magazine ''[[Télérama]]'' ranked it 17th in its list of the 100 greatest films in the history of cinema, describing the work as "a post-classical, lyrical, and disenchanted Western".<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.telerama.fr/cinema/les-100-meilleurs-films-de-l-histoire-selon-telerama-0116-9283.php | title=Les 100 meilleurs films de l'histoire selon "Télérama" |magazine=[[Télérama]] |date=August 16, 2023 |access-date=November 12, 2023}}</ref>

=== ''The Apple'' (1980) ===
{{Main|The Apple (1980 film){{!}}''The Apple'' (1980 film)}}
''The Apple'' (also called ''Star Rock'') is a 1980 [[Science fiction film|science fiction]] [[Musical film|musical]] [[comedy film]] written and directed by [[Menahem Golan]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.insidehook.com/article/movies/movies-disco-1980-the-apple-xanadu|title=Revisiting 1980, The Year the Movies Killed Disco|website=InsideHook|access-date=October 10, 2022|archive-date=October 10, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221010135429/https://www.insidehook.com/article/movies/movies-disco-1980-the-apple-xanadu|url-status=live}}</ref> It stars [[Catherine Mary Stewart]] as a young singer named Bibi, who, in a futuristic 1994, signs to an evil label named Boogalow International Music. It deals with themes of conformity versus rebellion, and makes use of [[Bible#Christian Bibles|Biblical allegory]], including that of [[Adam and Eve]] and the [[rapture]].<ref name="Flavorwire2">{{cite web |last=Bailey |first=Jason |title=Bad Movie Night: The Distinctive Disco Cheese of 'The Apple' |url=http://flavorwire.com/607226/bad-movie-night-the-distinctive-disco-cheese-of-the-apple |date=July 10, 2017 |access-date=December 9, 2017 |website=[[Flavorwire]] |language=en |archive-date=December 10, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171210015918/http://flavorwire.com/607226/bad-movie-night-the-distinctive-disco-cheese-of-the-apple |url-status=live }}</ref>

Common criticism from both reviews that appeared in trade publications and major news outlets and the audience were a lack of originality,<ref name="afi"/> a weak script,<ref name="afi">{{cite web|url=http://www.afi.com/members/catalog/DetailView.aspx?s=&Movie=56362|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170710142839/http://www.afi.com/members/catalog/DetailView.aspx?s=&Movie=56362|publisher=[[American Film Institute]]|title=The Apple|access-date=January 31, 2016|archive-date=July 10, 2017}}</ref> uninspired music,<ref name="afi"/> poor execution,<ref name="afi"/> and Golan's inexperienced take on [[Counterculture of the 1960s|the 1960s hippie movement]].<ref name="SlashFilm2"/> During the 1980 [[Montreal World Film Festival]], some members of the audience threw [[vinyl records]] of music from the film at the screen.<ref name="SlashFilm2">{{cite web |last=Harris |first=Blake |title=The Apple Oral History: How Did This Get Made |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/542502/the-apple-oral-history/ |website=[[/Film]] |access-date=January 12, 2022 |date=February 5, 2016 |archive-date=January 12, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220112025341/https://www.slashfilm.com/542502/the-apple-oral-history/ |url-status=live }}</ref> At the [[1980 Stinkers Bad Movie Awards]], the film received seven nominations (including Worst Picture) and won two awards: Worst Director (Golan) and Least "Special" Special Effects.<ref name="Past Winners Database">{{Cite web|url=http://theenvelope.latimes.com/extras/lostmind/year/1980/1980st.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070815004414/http://theenvelope.latimes.com/extras/lostmind/year/1980/1980st.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 15, 2007|title=Past Winners Database|work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=August 15, 2007}}</ref> Stinkers co-founder Mike Lancaster later selected ''The Apple'' as the worst film he had ever seen.<ref name="Lancaster">{{cite web |title=Q & A with the Stinkers |url=http://thestinkers.com/qanda.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010413025218/http://thestinkers.com/qanda.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 13, 2001 |website=[[Stinkers Bad Movie Awards]] |access-date=July 9, 2022}}</ref> ''[[The Saturday Evening Post]]'' listed it as the worst movie musical ever,<ref>{{cite web |title=The Worst Movie Musicals Ever |url=https://www.saturdayeveningpost.com/2020/08/the-worst-movie-musicals-ever/ |work=[[The Saturday Evening Post]] |last=Brownfield |first=Troy |access-date=January 11, 2022 |date=August 7, 2020 |archive-date=January 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220111170729/https://www.saturdayeveningpost.com/2020/08/the-worst-movie-musicals-ever/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and critic Tim Brayton described it as "A completely unadulterated bundle of the worst of cinema all spun up into one ball of madness. It cannot be described, and it can barely be experienced."<ref name="rtapple">{{cite web |url=http://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/1001131-apple/ |title=The Apple (1980) |work=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |publisher=[[Fandango Media]] |access-date=July 7, 2019 |archive-date=August 5, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200805172044/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/1001131-apple |url-status=live }}</ref> Sean Burns in ''[[Philadelphia Weekly]]'' wrote: "''The Apple'' isn't just the worst disco musical ever made; it could very well be the worst movie ever made, period."<ref>{{cite news |title=Summer Camp |first=Sean |last=Burns |newspaper=[[Philadelphia Weekly]] |date=July 12, 2006}}</ref> ''The Apple'' was included in ''[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]''{{'}}s ''Bad Movie Diaries'' column, where critic Kenneth Lowe described it as "without a doubt the most cringe-inducing, the most mortifying, the absolutely most embarrassing feature we've ever watched".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lowe |first1=Kenneth |last2=Vorel |first2=Jim |title=Bad Movie Diaries: The Apple (1980) |url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/movies/bad-movie-diaries/bad-movie-diaries-the-apple-1980/ |website=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]] |access-date=January 11, 2022 |language=en |date=February 19, 2020 |archive-date=January 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220111133434/https://www.pastemagazine.com/movies/bad-movie-diaries/bad-movie-diaries-the-apple-1980/ |url-status=live }}</ref> It has also been covered by the ''[[How Did This Get Made?]]'' podcast and ''[[Flavorwire]]''{{'}}s ''Bad Movie Night'' column and ''[[Mental Floss]]'' listed it as one of the "Ten Really Bad Movies that Define 'Bad Movies'".<ref name="SlashFilm2"/><ref name="Flavorwire2"/><ref name="mental floss10">{{cite web |title=10 Really Bad Movies that Define "Bad Movies" |url=https://www.mentalfloss.com/article/12464/10-really-bad-movies-define-bad-movies |website=[[Mental Floss]] |access-date=July 21, 2022 |date=September 6, 2012}}</ref>

=== ''Inchon'' (1981) === <!-- This qualifies as a 1981 film, for it made its world premiere a year prior to its general release, a few months before "Mommie Dearest". -->
{{Main|Inchon (film){{!}}''Inchon'' (film)}}
The [[war film]] ''Inchon'', directed by [[Terence Young (director)|Terence Young]] and starring [[Laurence Olivier]] as General [[Douglas MacArthur]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tcm.com/tcmdb/title/3139/inchon|title=Inchon|website=Turner Classic Movies|access-date=July 13, 2022|archive-date=July 13, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220713185127/https://www.tcm.com/tcmdb/title/3139/inchon|url-status=dead}}</ref> was meant to depict the [[Battle of Inchon]] during the [[Korean War]]. Producer Mitsuharu Ishii was a senior member of the Japanese branch of the [[Unification Church]], whose leader, [[Sun Myung Moon]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wiWctDyWhDI|title=Slate's Bad Movies: Oscar Slumming|date=March 3, 2008 |via=YouTube|access-date=November 12, 2019|archive-date=March 12, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200312071510/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wiWctDyWhDI&gl=US&hl=en|url-status=live}}</ref> claimed he had the film made to show MacArthur's spirituality and connection to God and the Japanese people.<ref>[[s:U.S. v. Sun Myung Moon 532 F.Supp. 1360 (1982)]]</ref> Its eventual production cost of $46 million resulted in a $5 million box-office gross, and ''[[The New York Times]]'' review written by [[Vincent Canby]] calls the movie "the most expensive B-movie ever".<ref>{{cite news |title=Inchon (1981) – 'Inchon,' At Last |first=Vincent |last=Canby |authorlink=Vincent Canby |url=https://movies.nytimes.com/movie/review?res=9A03E0D8123BF934A2575AC0A964948260 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=September 17, 1982 |access-date=February 10, 2017 |archive-date=February 15, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120215194638/http://movies.nytimes.com/movie/review?res=9A03E0D8123BF934A2575AC0A964948260 |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[The Washington Post]]'' described ''Inchon'' as "one of the biggest commercial disasters in film history".<ref>{{cite news |title =Terence Young dies – Directed Bond movies | newspaper =[[The Washington Post]] |page =B6 |date =September 9, 1994}}</ref> Every conceivable kind of problem plagued production, including labor issues, the U.S. military withdrawing support due to the film's Unification Church connection, weather and natural disasters, customs difficulties, expensive directorial blunders, and the original director ([[Andrew McLaglen]]) quitting before the start of production. Olivier's performance was criticized, and he was awarded the [[3rd Golden Raspberry Awards|1982 Golden Raspberry award]] for Worst Actor.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.razzies.com/forum/forum_posts.asp?TID=332&PN=3 |title=1982 Razzie Nominees & "Winners" – The Official Razzie Forum |work=Razzies.com |access-date=January 17, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820075540/http://www.razzies.com/forum/forum_posts.asp?TID=332&PN=3 |archive-date=August 20, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The film itself took the 1982 Razzies for Worst Picture and Worst Screenplay, and Young's direction earned him a tie for Worst Director of 1982. A number of reviewers at various media outlets described ''Inchon'' as the worst film ever made, including ''The Washington Post'',<ref>{{cite news |last=Mayo |first=Mike |title =Hollywood's untapped resources – worthwhile movies don't always make it to video | newspaper =[[The Washington Post]] |date =April 13, 1997 |page=G7}}</ref> ''Newsweek'',<ref>{{cite news |last=Boedeker |first=Hal |title =The Magic of Olivier his film legacy sets standard for all actors | work =[[The Miami Herald]] |page =36G |date =July 21, 1989 |quote=The worst of his choices was probably taking on the role of Gen. Douglas MacArthur in 1982's Inchon. ''Newsweek'' called Inchon 'the worst movie ever made, a turkey the size of Godzilla.'}}</ref> ''TV Guide'',<ref>{{cite magazine |url=http://movies.tvguide.com/inchon/review/102041 |title=Inchon Review |magazine=[[TV Guide]] |date=November 28, 2012 |access-date=November 18, 2013 |archive-date=October 4, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111004195720/http://movies.tvguide.com/inchon/review/102041 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and the [[The Canadian Press|Canadian Press]].<ref>{{cite news |last=McKay |first=John ([[Canadian Press]]) |title =Welch fleshes out worst in film | work =The Record (Kitchener, Ontario, Canada) |page =E4 |date =March 23, 2004}}</ref> ''Inchon'' was later profiled in multiple books on worst in film, including ''[[The Hollywood Hall of Shame]]'' by Harry and Michael Medved,<ref>{{cite book |last1=Medved |first1=Harry |first2=Michael |last2=Medved |author2-link=Michael Medved |title=The Hollywood Hall of Shame: The Most Expensive Flops in Movie History |publisher=Perigee Books |location=[[New York City|New York]], [[New York (state)|NY]] |year=1984 |pages=[https://archive.org/details/hollywoodhallofs00medv/page/189 189–197] |isbn=0-399-51060-5 |title-link=The Hollywood Hall of Shame }}</ref> and ''The Worst Movies of All Time'' by Michael Sauter.{{sfn|Sauter|page=197}} To date, ''Inchon'' has never been released on home video in the United States although it was aired on the church's Good Life TV Network.

=== ''Tarzan, the Ape Man'' (1981) ===
{{Main|Tarzan, the Ape Man (1981 film){{!}}''Tarzan, the Ape Man'' (1981 film)}}
The [[adventure film]] ''Tarzan, the Ape Man'', loosely based on the novel ''[[Tarzan of the Apes]]'' by [[Edgar Rice Burroughs]], stars [[Miles O'Keeffe]] (who would later star in the 1982 ''[[Conan the Barbarian (1982 film)|Conan the Barbarian]]'' knock-off ''[[Ator the Invincible]]'', which [[Ator 2 - L'invincibile Orion|alongside its sequel]] featured in two episodes of the TV series ''[[Mystery Science Theater 3000]]'') in the [[Tarzan|title role]] and [[Bo Derek]] as his partner [[Jane Porter (Tarzan)|Jane Parker]], and is told from Jane's point of view. Despite being a box-office success, critics poorly received it upon its release due to its poor screenplay, bad acting, and unintentional humor. [[Leonard Maltin]], writing for his ''Movie Guide'', stated that the film "lacks action, humor and charm", and considered it so bad that it "nearly forced editors of this book to devise a rating lower than BOMB".<ref name="Maltin01211"/> [[Leslie Halliwell]] was equally harsh; he described ''Tarzan, the Ape Man'' as "certainly the worst of the Tarzan movies and possibly the banalest film so far made; even the animals give poor performances".<ref>Leslie Halliwell, John Walker, ''Halliwell's Film Guide''. HarperPerennial, 1996 (p. 1119).</ref> Writer Thomas S. Hischak described it thus: "Produced and directed without a shred of talent by [[John Derek]], ''Tarzan, the Ape Man'' often ranks high in the lists of the worst movies ever made."<ref>Thomas S. Hischak, ''American Literature on Stage and Screen: 525 Works and Their Adaptations'' McFarland, 2012. {{ISBN|0-7864-9279-1}} (p. 237)</ref> Film critic John Nesbit considered it "my pick for worst film ever",<ref>{{cite web|url=http://oldschoolreviews.com/rev_80/tarzan.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140304212347/http://oldschoolreviews.com/rev_80/tarzan.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 4, 2014 |title=John Derek, Tarzan the Ape Man |publisher=Old School Reviews |access-date=March 5, 2014}}</ref> while Matt Brunson of ''[[Creative Loafing]]'' wrote, "this cinematic atrocity truly is one of the all-time worsts".<ref>{{cite web |last=Brunson |first=Matt |url=http://clclt.com/charlotte/view-from-the-couch/Content?oid=2354590 |title=View From The Couch &#124; View from the Couch &#124; Creative Loafing Charlotte |work=Clclt.com |date=June 16, 2004 |access-date=March 5, 2014 |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304051036/http://clclt.com/charlotte/view-from-the-couch/Content?oid=2354590 |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Tarzan, the Ape Man'' was nominated for six awards at the [[2nd Golden Raspberry Awards]], winning one for Worst Actress (Bo Derek). It holds a 10% rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on 20 reviews.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://rottentomatoes.com/m/1020897-tarzan_the_ape_man|title=Tarzan, the Ape Man (1981)|website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]]|publisher=[[Fandango Media|Fandango]]|access-date=January 30, 2021|archive-date=March 7, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210307075545/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/1020897-tarzan_the_ape_man|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== ''Mommie Dearest'' (1981) ===
{{Main|Mommie Dearest (film){{!}}''Mommie Dearest'' (film)}}
[[File:Faye Dunaway on the set of A Place for Lovers, 1968.jpg|thumb|left|[[Faye Dunaway]] (pictured in ''[[A Place for Lovers]]'', also on this list) regretted her [[Razzie]]-winning portrayal of actress [[Joan Crawford]] in the [[Camp (style)|camp classic]] ''[[Mommie Dearest (film)|Mommie Dearest]]'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.washingtonblade.com/2021/10/14/camp-classic-mommie-dearest-turns-40/|title=Camp classic 'Mommie Dearest' turns 40|first=Gregg|last=Shapiro|date=October 14, 2021|access-date=October 22, 2021|archive-date=October 22, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211022143742/https://www.washingtonblade.com/2021/10/14/camp-classic-mommie-dearest-turns-40/|url-status=live}}</ref> yet it earned a spot at number 41 on [[AFI's 100 Years...100 Heroes & Villains|AFI's 100 Years... 100 Heroes and Villains]].]]
''Mommie Dearest'', directed by [[Frank Perry]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://collider.com/mommie-dearest-oscars-cult-classic/ |title=How 'Mommie Dearest' Went From Oscar Bait to Cult Classic{{!}}Collider |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |date=March 10, 2023 |access-date=December 10, 2023 |archive-date=July 22, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230722215022/https://collider.com/mommie-dearest-oscars-cult-classic/ |url-status=live }}</ref> was based on the [[Mommie Dearest|memoir of the same name]] by [[Christina Crawford]], about her upbringing by [[Joan Crawford]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mubi.com/de/films/mommie-dearest|title=Meine liebe Rabenmutter|via=mubi.com|access-date=January 28, 2019|archive-date=January 29, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190129005847/https://mubi.com/de/films/mommie-dearest|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-2006-06-06-0606060260-story.html|title='Mommie Dearest' meets John Waters|website=Chicago Tribune|date=June 6, 2006|access-date=June 5, 2021|archive-date=July 31, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210731191016/https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-2006-06-06-0606060260-story.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://catalog.afi.com/Catalog/moviedetails/68145|title=AFI&#124;Catalog|website=catalog.afi.com|access-date=June 5, 2021|archive-date=June 5, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210605163811/https://catalog.afi.com/Catalog/moviedetails/68145|url-status=live}}</ref> It was the first film to sweep the Golden Raspberry Awards nominations, winning a total of five Razzies out of the nine nominations, including "Worst Picture" and Worst Actress ([[Faye Dunaway]], shared with [[Bo Derek]]).{{sfn|Adams|page=188}} The same organization also named it "Worst Picture of the Decade" in 1989/90, and was nominated for "Worst Drama of Our First 25 Years" in 2004/05.<ref name="GR1">{{cite news|url=http://www.razzies.com/asp/content/XcNewsPlus.asp?cmd=view&articleid=12|title=Decade's Worst -The 80's|last=Wilson |first=John |author-link=John J. B. Wilson |publisher=[[Golden Raspberry Awards]]|date=March 15, 1990|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130511065558/http://www.razzies.com/asp/content/XcNewsPlus.asp?cmd=view&articleid=12|archive-date=May 11, 2013}}</ref> The film is part of the "100 most awful" in ''The Official Razzie Movie Guide'' and Michael Sauter's ''The Worst Movies of All Time''.<ref name="OFMG">{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/life/movies/movieawards/2005-02-24-razzies_x.htm|title=Razzies still knocking Hollywood down a peg after 25 years|agency=[[Associated Press]] |work=[[USA Today]]|date=February 24, 2005|access-date=October 11, 2020|archive-date=2023-02-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230202035338/https://usatoday30.usatoday.com/life/movies/movieawards/2005-02-24-razzies_x.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=ORG>{{cite book |last=Wilson |first=John |title =The official Razzie movie guide: enjoying the best of Hollywood's worst |publisher =[[Hachette (publisher)|Hachette]] |year =2005 |isbn =0-446-69334-0}}</ref>{{sfn|Sauter|page=189}} It earned, as film critic and TV host [[Richard Crouse]] put it, "some of the nastiest reviews ever".<ref name=RW>{{cite book |last=Crouse |first=Richard |author-link=Richard Crouse |title =Reel Winners: Movie Award Trivia |publisher =[[Dundurn Group]] |year =2005 |page =[https://archive.org/details/reelwinnersmovie0000crou/page/123 123] |isbn =1-55002-574-0 |url =https://archive.org/details/reelwinnersmovie0000crou/page/123 }}</ref> Eric Henderson of [[CBS Minneapolis]] named it at the top of his "Best 'Worst Movies Ever{{'"}} list.<ref name="WCCO">{{cite news|url=http://minnesota.cbslocal.com/2010/07/21/movie-blog-best-worst-movies-ever/|title=Movie Blog: Best 'Worst Movies Ever'|last=Henderson|first=Eric|publisher=[[CBS Minneapolis]]|date=June 21, 2010|access-date=June 13, 2013|archive-date=October 4, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151004063910/http://minnesota.cbslocal.com/2010/07/21/movie-blog-best-worst-movies-ever/|url-status=live}}</ref> Roger Ebert wrote of this film, "I can't imagine who would want to subject themselves to this movie. 'Mommie Dearest' is a painful experience that drones on endlessly, as Joan Crawford's relationship with her daughter, Christina, disintegrates from cruelty through jealousy into pathos."<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/mommie-dearest-1981 |title=Mommie Dearest movie review & film summary (1981) |first=Roger |last=Ebert |author-link=Roger Ebert |work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |date=January 1, 1981 |access-date=October 11, 2020 |archive-date=November 11, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171111205638/https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/mommie-dearest-1981 |url-status=live }}</ref> Of the performance of Faye Dunaway, ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' said "Dunaway does not chew scenery. Dunaway starts neatly at each corner of the set in every scene and swallows it whole, co-stars and all."<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://variety.com/1980/film/reviews/mommie-dearest-1200424940/ |title=Mommie Dearest Review – Read Variety's Analysis Of The Movie Mommie Dearest |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140715082555/http://variety.com/1980/film/reviews/mommie-dearest-1200424940/|archive-date=2014-07-15 |work=Variety |date=January 1, 1981}}</ref> ''Vanity Fair'' and Rotten Tomatoes subsequently included ''Mommie Dearest'' on their worst film lists.<ref name="italianvanity"/><ref name="sobad"/>

Despite the reviews at the time,<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2017/06/05/joan-crawfords-explosive-offscreen-life |title=Joan Crawford's Explosive Offscreen Life |last=Brody |first=Richard |author-link=Richard Brody |magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |date=May 26, 2017 |access-date=October 11, 2020 |archive-date=January 16, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210116100845/https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2017/06/05/joan-crawfords-explosive-offscreen-life |url-status=live }}</ref> the film was a box-office success, grossing $25 million worldwide on a $5 million budget. It has a 50% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on 46 reviews. The site's consensus reads, "''Mommie Dearest'' certainly doesn't lack for conviction, and neither does Faye Dunaway's legendary performance as a wire-wielding monster; unfortunately, the movie is too campy and undisciplined to transcend guilty pleasure".<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/mommie_dearest/ |title=Mommie Dearest (1981) |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |publisher=[[Fandango Media|Fandango]] |access-date=January 30, 2021 |archive-date=April 16, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190416101214/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/mommie_dearest/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== ''Dünyayı Kurtaran Adam'' (''The Man Who Saves the World'') (1982) ===
{{Main|Dünyayı Kurtaran Adam{{!}}''Dünyayı Kurtaran Adam''}}
The Turkish science-fiction adventure ''Dünyayı Kurtaran Adam'' (also commonly known as ''Turkish Star Wars'') was directed by [[Çetin İnanç]] and starred [[Cüneyt Arkın]]. It is notorious for illegally using footage from well-known science fiction films and shows, most notably ''[[Star Wars]]'', along with stealing the music score from films such as ''[[Moonraker (film)|Moonraker]]'' and ''[[Raiders of the Lost Ark]]''. The film is also criticized for its nonsensical plot, badly written dialogue, and crude special effects.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.austinchronicle.com/gyrobase/Issue/story?oid=oid%3A197912 |title=There Is No Try...: Foleyvision does the Turkish 'Star Wars' Austin Screens |publisher=AustinChronicle.com |date=February 20, 2004 |access-date=January 17, 2011 |archive-date=September 18, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090918185247/http://www.austinchronicle.com/gyrobase/Issue/story?oid=oid:197912 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://filmthreat.com/reviews/2341/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100312030851/https://filmthreat.com/reviews/2341/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 12, 2010 |title=The Turkish Star Wars |publisher=Film Threat |date=May 18, 2005 |access-date=January 17, 2011 }}</ref> It is also a fantasy [[martial arts film]], heavily influenced by 1970s [[Hong Kong martial arts films]] from [[Orange Sky Golden Harvest|Golden Harvest]].<ref name="Goldweber">{{cite book |last=Goldweber |first=David Elroy |title=Claws & Saucers: Science Fiction, Horror, and Fantasy Film 1902-1982: A Complete Guide |date=2015 |publisher=[[Lulu Press, Inc]] |isbn=978-1-312-28803-4 |page=1773 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hgJJzgEACAAJ&pg=PT1773 |access-date=February 27, 2024 |archive-date=February 27, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240227175610/https://books.google.com/books?id=hgJJzgEACAAJ&pg=PT1773 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Jos Kirps of [[ArticlesBase]] called it "The Worst Movie Ever", and stated, "There are many bad sci-fi movies, and for many years movie addicts even considered Ed Wood's ''Plan 9 From Outer Space'' the worst movie of all times. But ''Plan 9'' is still a pretty good movie when compared to ''Dünyayi Kurtaran Adam''."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.contour2002.org/article/the-worst-movie-ever-a-turkish-star-wars-clone|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140810150129/http://www.contour2002.org/article/the-worst-movie-ever-a-turkish-star-wars-clone|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 10, 2014|title=Contour2002.org|access-date=October 1, 2014}}</ref> ''[[Sabah (newspaper)|Sabah]]'' called it the "world's worst film".<ref>{{Cite web |language=tr |url=http://www.sabah.com.tr/Gunaydin/Magazin/2012/04/15/turkun-uzayla-imtihani-nereye-kadar-surecek |title=News article from Sabah newspaper |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160530010134/http://www.sabah.com.tr/gunaydin/magazin/2012/04/15/turkun-uzayla-imtihani-nereye-kadar-surecek |archive-date=May 30, 2016 |access-date=August 29, 2013}}</ref> ''[[Hürriyet]]'' described the film as "sitting on the throne of the king" when compared to other "so bad it's good" [[cult film]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |language=tr |url=http://www.hurriyet.com.tr/yazarlar/20291864.asp |title=News article from Hürriyet |date=April 7, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160302134628/http://www.hurriyet.com.tr/yazarlar/20291864.asp |archive-date=March 2, 2016 |access-date=August 29, 2013}}</ref> ''Toronto Standard'' called it a "dollar-store Star Wars" and compared it to the works of Ed Wood.<ref>{{cite news|title= Dollar-store Star Wars|publisher= Toronto Standard|date= May 4, 2012|url= http://torontostandard.com/culture/dollar-store-star-wars|access-date= August 24, 2013|archive-date= September 26, 2018|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20180926123159/http://www.torontostandard.com/culture/dollar-store-star-wars/|url-status= live}}</ref> When it became apparent that the film had inspired an enthusiastic international cult, a sequel, ''The Son of the Man Who Saved the World'' ([[Turks in Space|''Dünyayı Kurtaran Adam'ın Oğlu'']]), was shot in 2006 and featured many returning members of the original cast and crew.<ref>{{cite web|language=tr |url=http://www.sabah.com.tr/2006/04/13/gny/gny119-20060413-200.html |title=News article from Sabah newspaper |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090808044254/http://www.sabah.com.tr/2006/04/13/gny/gny119-20060413-200.html |archive-date=August 8, 2009 |access-date=July 29, 2006}}</ref> The film was included on ''Time Out''{{'}}s 40 Best Bad Movies Ever Made list.<ref name="timeoutlist"/>

=== ''Howard the Duck'' (1986) ===
{{Main|Howard the Duck (film){{!}}''Howard the Duck'' (film)}}
Directed by [[Willard Huyck]], written by Huyck and [[Gloria Katz]], and produced by [[George Lucas]], it is based on the [[Marvel Comics]] [[Howard the Duck|character of the same name]]. ''Howard the Duck'' received overwhelmingly negative reviews from film critics. ''[[Orange Coast Magazine]]'' writer Marc Weinberg and Leonard Maltin criticized the decision to shoot the film in live action.<ref>{{cite magazine |last= Weinberg |first= Marc |date = 1986 |title = Out-Foxed | magazine= [[Orange Coast Magazine]] | volume = 12 | issue = 9 |pages = 143–144 }}</ref><ref name="Maltin">{{cite book |last= Maltin |first= Leonard |title = Leonard Maltin's 2009 Movie Guide |year = 2008 |publisher = Penguin Group |isbn = 978-0-452-28978-9 |page = [https://archive.org/details/isbn_9780452289789/page/641 641] |chapter = H |url = https://archive.org/details/isbn_9780452289789/page/641 }}</ref> The appearance of Howard was criticized as being unconvincing due to his poorly functioning mouth and expressionless face. Reviewers also criticized the acting and humor and found the film boring.<ref name="Stanley">{{cite book |last= Stanley |first= John |title = Creature Features: The Science Fiction, Fantasy, and Horror Movie Guide |year = 2000 |publisher = Berkley Boulevard Books |page = 253 |isbn = 0-425-17517-0 | quote = For one, the duck costume and makeup are phony&nbsp;— Howard looks like a midget in a Halloween costume. }}</ref><ref name="Hunter">{{cite book |last= Hunter |first= Lew |title = Lew Hunter's Screenwriting 434: The Industry's Premier Teacher Reveals the Secrets of the Successful Screenplay |year = 2004 |publisher = Perigee |isbn = 0-399-52986-1 |page = 21 |chapter = Nothing in the Mind, Please | quote = Because we all know what a duck looks like, Lucas could not get an audience to suspend their belief that Howard was a little person in a duck suit. }}</ref> [[Dave Kehr]] of the ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'' said the movie's "crude, often embarrassing, sex jokes" seemed "out of place" with the more innocent aspects of the film.<ref name="DaveKehrHowardTheDuck">{{cite news|last=Kehr|first=Dave|date= August 1, 1986|title= UNLOVABLE DUCK MAKES 'HOWARD' AN UNLOVABLE FILM|work= [[Chicago Tribune]]|url= https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1986-08-01-8602250309-story.html|access-date= May 13, 2021|archive-date= October 24, 2020|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20201024095717/https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1986-08-01-8602250309-story.html|url-status= live}}</ref> Jay Carr of ''[[The Boston Globe]]'' claimed that "They Don't Get Much Worse Than ''Howard''{{-"}},<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/294411402|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151018024531/https://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/boston/doc/294411402.html?FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT&type=current&date=Aug%201,%201986&author=Jay%20Carr,%20Globe%20Staff&pub=Boston%20Globe%20%28pre-1997%20Fulltext%29&edition=&startpage=&desc=THEY%20DON%27T%20GET%20MUCH%20WORSE%20THAN%20%27HOWARD%27|title=They Don't Get Much Worse Than 'Howard'|work=[[The Boston Globe]]|url-access=subscription|access-date=September 30, 2013|first=Jay|last=Carr|date=August 1, 1986|url-status=live|archive-date=October 18, 2015| id={{ProQuest|294411402}} }}</ref> Glenn Heath Jr. of ''[[Slant Magazine]]'' wrote that it "has a rightful place in the canon of worst films ever",<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.slantmagazine.com/house/2011/07/summer-of-86-tarred-and-feathered-howard-the-duck/|title=Summer of '86: Tarred and Feathered: Howard the Duck|work=[[Slant Magazine]]|date=July 28, 2011|access-date=March 14, 2014|archive-date=March 16, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140316105914/http://www.slantmagazine.com/house/2011/07/summer-of-86-tarred-and-feathered-howard-the-duck/|url-status=live}}</ref> and ''[[TV Guide]]'' states it is "one of the worst big-budget movies ever made".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://movies.tvguide.com/howard-the-duck/review/101469|title=Howard the Duck|work=[[TV Guide]]|access-date=March 14, 2014|archive-date=September 30, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130930202246/http://movies.tvguide.com/howard-the-duck/review/101469|url-status=dead}}</ref> It was featured in ''Empire''{{'}}s poll of the 50 worst films ever made,<ref name="The 50 Worst Movies Ever"/> and ''[[Screen Rant]]'' and ''Vanity Fair'' have included it on their worst film lists.<ref name="Screen Rant">{{cite news|url=https://screenrant.com/worst-movies-list-all-time/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170811144052/https://screenrant.com/worst-movies-list-all-time/|title=25 Worst Movies in Film History|last=Kendrick|first=Ben|work=[[Screen Rant]]|date=November 13, 2015|access-date=August 11, 2017|archive-date=August 11, 2017}}</ref><ref name="italianvanity"/>

Rotten Tomatoes gives the film a score of 13% based on 86 reviews, making it the lowest-rated [[Lucasfilm]] production of those reviewed on the site. The site's consensus states: "While it has its moments, ''Howard the Duck'' suffers from an uneven tone and mediocre performances."<ref name="Tomatoes">{{cite web |url = https://rottentomatoes.com/m/howard_the_duck/ |title = ''Howard the Duck'' (1986) | website = [[Rotten Tomatoes]] |publisher = [[Fandango Media|Fandango]] |access-date = January 15, 2025 |archive-date = August 3, 2014 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140803155451/https://rottentomatoes.com/m/howard_the_duck/ |url-status = live }}</ref> It received seven [[Golden Raspberry Award]] nominations in 1987 including [[Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Supporting Actor|Worst Supporting Actor]] ([[Tim Robbins]]), [[Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Director|Worst Director]] (Willard Huyck) and [[Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Original Song|Worst Original Song]] ("Howard the Duck"). It won four trophies for [[Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Screenplay|Worst Screenplay]], [[Golden Raspberry Award for Worst New Star|Worst New Star]] ("the six guys and gals in the duck suit"), Worst Visual Effects, and [[Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Picture|Worst Picture]], tied with ''[[Under the Cherry Moon]]''.<ref name="Razzies">{{cite web |last= Wilson |first= John |title = 1986 Archive |url = http://www.razzies.com/asp/content/XcNewsPlus.asp?cmd=view&articleid=25 |publisher = [[Golden Raspberry Award]] |access-date = October 11, 2009 |url-status = dead |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130602153152/http://www.razzies.com/asp/content/XcNewsPlus.asp?cmd=view&articleid=25 |archive-date = June 2, 2013 }}</ref> The movie also won a [[Stinkers Bad Movie Awards]] for Worst Picture.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://theenvelope.latimes.com/extras/lostmind/year/1986/1986st.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061017172107/http://theenvelope.latimes.com/extras/lostmind/year/1986/1986st.htm|archive-date=October 17, 2006|title=1986 9th Hastings Bad Cinema Society Stinkers Awards|access-date=April 2, 2013|work=[[Stinkers Bad Movie Awards]]|publisher=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref> The negative reaction to the film took its toll on the cast, who found themselves unable to work on other projects as a result.<ref name="Release-2">{{cite video |people=Thompson, Lea; Jones, Jeffrey; Gale, Ed |date=2009 |title=Releasing the Duck |medium=DVD |publisher=Universal Home Video |id=UPC 025195052306}}</ref>

Over time, the film has remained a source of fascination and developed "a small, but loyal fanbase".<ref name="PrimerStories">{{cite web |last= Chipman |first= Bob |title = Duck Fails Hollywood Bets It All on Duck Boners |url = https://www.primerand.co/5/howard | work = Primer&Co. |access-date = May 9, 2021 |archive-date = September 27, 2021 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210927081429/https://www.primerand.co/5/howard |url-status = dead }}</ref><ref name="YahooTimRobbins">{{cite web |last= Alter |first= Ethan |title = Role Recall: Tim |url-status = live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cinemablend.com/news/2434140/lea-thompson-is-pitching-a-howard-the-duck-movie-to-marvel|title=Lea Thompson Is Pitching A Howard The Duck Movie To Marvel|first1=Dirk|last1=Libbey|date=June 12, 2018|website=Cinemablend|access-date=January 11, 2019|archive-date=January 11, has appeared in several [[Marvel Cinematic Universe]] movies and series beginning in 2014's ''[[Guardians of the Galaxy (film)|Guardians of the Galaxy]]'', in which he was voiced by [[Seth === ''Ishtar'' (1987) ===
{{Main|Ishtar (film){{!}}''Ishtar'' (film)}}
[[File:Elaine May - publicity1.jpg|thumb|upright|''[[Ishtar (film)|Ishtar]]'' director [[Elaine May]]<ref name="2024lineup"/> defended her 1987 box office flop, stating, "If all of the people who hate ''Ishtar'' had seen it, I would be a rich woman today."<ref name="elainemay">{{Cite web|url=https://forward.com/culture/434193/elaine-may-mounting-a-comeback-at-87-is-directing-a-new-film/|title=Elaine May, Mounting A Comeback At 87, Is Directing A New Film|last=Grisar|first=PJ|work=[[The Forward]]|access-date=April 28, 2020|date=November 4, 2019|archive-date=November 5, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191105155049/https://forward.com/culture/434193/elaine-may-mounting-a-comeback-at-87-is-directing-a-new-film/|url-status=live}}</ref>]]
''Ishtar'' was written and directed by [[Elaine May]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mubi.com/notebook/posts/the-not-so-savage-messiahs|title=The Not-So-Savage Messiahs|date=August 5, 2013|website=MUBI|access-date=August 2, 2022|archive-date=August 17, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220817111104/https://mubi.com/notebook/posts/the-not-so-savage-messiahs|url-status=live}}</ref> and starred [[Academy Award|Oscar]]-winning duo [[Warren Beatty]] and [[Dustin Hoffman]] as an ode to the ''[[Road to...]]'' film series featuring [[Bing Crosby]] and [[Bob Hope]]. Beatty and Hoffman star as Rogers and Clarke, two untalented lounge singers who travel to [[Morocco]] in hopes of finding a gig.<ref name="brody">{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.newyorker.com/culture/richard-brody/movie-of-the-week-ishtar|title=Movie of the Week: "Ishtar"|last=Brody|first=Richard|author-link=Richard Brody|magazine=[[The New Yorker]]|access-date=February 11, 2019|date=August 6, 2015|archive-date=January 9, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190109004100/https://www.newyorker.com/culture/richard-brody/movie-of-the-week-ishtar|url-status=live}}</ref> Due to unanticipated problems with filming in the desert—which resulted in numerous reshoots—the film ran over budget by $30 million. While its final budget cost was $55 million, ''Ishtar'' earned only $14,375,181 at the North American box office, leading ''Ishtar'' to become synonymous with "[[Box office bomb|box-office flop]]". It was also subject to harsh reviews from critics. The film was nominated for Worst Picture and Worst Screenplay in the [[8th Golden Raspberry Awards]], winning one for Worst Director. ''The [[San Jose Mercury News]]'' claimed that "Time has not improved this film's reputation as being one of the worst ever made."<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.mercurynews.com/movies-dvd/ci_17017300 |title=Review: 'Dinner for Schmucks' a savory comedy |newspaper=[[San Jose Mercury News]] |date=May 1, 2011 |access-date=September 20, 2013 |archive-date=September 21, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921061311/http://www.mercurynews.com/movies-dvd/ci_17017300 |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[Time Out (magazine)|Time Out]]'' suggested it was "so bad it could have been deliberate", and called it "one of the worst films ever made",<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.timeout.com/london/film/ishtar |title=Ishtar |magazine=[[Time Out (magazine)|Time Out]] |access-date=February 20, 2020 |archive-date=November 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181115225621/https://www.timeout.com/london/film/ishtar |url-status=live }}</ref> while [[Ed Morrissey]] referred to it as "The ''[[Citizen Kane]]'' of big-budget, A-list vehicular homicides."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://hotair.com/archives/2009/02/22/what-were-the-worst-movies-of-all-time/ |title=What were the worst movies of all time? |first=Ed |last=Morrissey |work=Hot Air |author-link=Ed Morrissey |date=February 22, 2009 |publisher=[[Hot Air (news site)|Hot Air]] |access-date=September 20, 2013 |archive-date=September 21, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921060444/http://hotair.com/archives/2009/02/22/what-were-the-worst-movies-of-all-time/ |url-status=live }}</ref> It was included in Michael Sauter's ''The Worst Movies of All Time'' book, Rotten Tomatoes placed it amongst "25 Movies So Bad They're Unmissable" and [[Richard Roeper]] included it on his list of the 40 worst films he had ever seen.{{sfn|Sauter|page=213–216}}<ref name="RichardRoeper">{{cite book|first=Richard|last=Roeper|authorlink=Richard Roeper|title=10 Sure Signs a Movie Character is Doomed and Other Surprising Movie Lists|location=New York City|publisher=[[Hachette Books|Hyperion Books]]|date=2003|ISBN=978-0786888306|pages=66–67}}</ref><ref name="sobad"/> In 1999, ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' placed the film on a list of the 100 worst ideas of the 20th century.<ref name="worstideas">{{cite magazine |url=http://content.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,991230,00.html |title=The 100 Worst Ideas Of The Century |date=June 14, 1999 |access-date=April 8, 2018 |url-access=subscription |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |first1=Melissa |last1=August |first2=Harriet |last2=Barovick |first3=Michelle |last3=Derrow |first4=Tam |last4=Gray |first5=Daniel S. |last5=Levy |first6=Lina |last6=Lofaro |first7=David |last7=Spitz |first8=Joel |last8=Stein |first9=Chris |last9=Taylor |archive-date=October 21, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181021051659/http://content.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,991230,00.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

The film has since become a cult classic.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.filminquiry.com/10-movies-low-ratings-actually-good/|title=10 Movies With Low Ratings That Are Actually Good|first=Alistair|last=Ryder|date=August 6, 2015|website=Film Inquiry|access-date=January 11, 2019|archive-date=January 12, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190112044239/https://www.filminquiry.com/10-movies-low-ratings-actually-good/|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Ishtar'' has seen a minor critical re-evaluation from some critics like [[Richard Brody]],<ref name="brody"/> and directors [[Quentin Tarantino]], [[Edgar Wright]], and [[Martin Scorsese]] have praised it in interviews.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.indiewire.com/2020/05/ishtar-box-office-flop-game-changer-setback-female-directors-1202231739/|title='Ishtar': How Hollywood Decided That One Box-Office Flop Spoke for All Female Directors|last=Brueggemann|first=Tom|date=May 17, 2020|website=[[IndieWire]]|language=en|access-date=December 9, 2022|archive-date=July 5, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220705130534/https://www.indiewire.com/2020/05/ishtar-box-office-flop-game-changer-setback-female-directors-1202231739/|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Gary Larson]], who initially lampooned the movie in ''[[The Far Side]]'', said he regrets writing that cartoon because he based it solely on ''Ishtar''{{'}}s reputation, and that he enjoyed the film when he later watched it. As of December 2022, it is the only cartoon he has publicly admitted to regretting.<ref>{{cite web|last=McGuire|first=Liam|title=Gary Larson Names the One Far Side Comic He Wants to Apologize For|website=[[ScreenRant]]|date=December 1, 2022|access-date=December 9, 2022|url=https://screenrant.com/far-side-gary-larson-apologize-ishtar-mistake/|archive-date=December 9, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221209004631/https://screenrant.com/far-side-gary-larson-apologize-ishtar-mistake/|url-status=live}}</ref> Defenders argue that the studio did not back May, resulting in a [[public relations]] disaster before it was released in theaters.<ref name="elainemay"/> [[Joe Queenan (author)|Joe Queenan]] compared the film to another comedy film considered the worst, ''[[Gigli]]'', and wrote that although it was considered one of the worst films ever made at the time of its release, it "has several comic moments" and does not get worse on subsequent viewings, unlike ''Gigli''.<ref name="queenan"/>

=== ''Leonard Part 6'' (1987) ===
{{Main|Leonard Part 6{{!}}''Leonard Part 6''}}
[[File:Bill cosby 1969.JPG|thumb|upright|[[Bill Cosby]] became the first person to [[List of people who have accepted Golden Raspberry Awards|accept a Golden Raspberry Award]] for ''[[Leonard Part 6]]'', which he admitted was the worst movie ever made.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://siskelebert.org/?p=2512|title=Worst of 1987 – Siskel and Ebert Movie Reviews|website=siskelebert.org|access-date=January 9, 2022|archive-date=January 9, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220109145300/https://siskelebert.org/?p=2512|url-status=live}}</ref>]]
''Leonard Part 6'', starring (as well as written and produced by) [[Bill Cosby]], was intended as a parody of spy movies. Leonard Parker, a former [[Central Intelligence Agency|CIA]] spy, is brought out of retirement to save the world from an evil vegetarian who brainwashes animals to kill people. Rita Kempley at ''[[The Washington Post]]'' noted the large number of Coca-Cola product placements and said "The only good thing about Bill Cosby's ''Leonard Part 6'' is that we didn't have to see Parts 1 through 5."<ref name="wprk">{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/style/longterm/movies/videos/leonardpart6pgkempley_a0ca2f.htm|title=Leonard Part 6 (PG)|last=Kempley|first=Rita|date=December 19, 1987|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|access-date=June 27, 2012|archive-date=September 21, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921220949/http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/style/longterm/movies/videos/leonardpart6pgkempley_a0ca2f.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> Scott Weinberg at DVD Talk noted the film as "truly one of the worst movies you'll ever see ... movies this bad should be handled with Teflon gloves and a pair of tongs".<ref name="weinberglp6">{{cite web|url=https://www.dvdtalk.com/reviews/15632/leonard-part-6/|title=Leonard Part 6|last=Weinberg|first=Scott|date=April 26, 2005|work=DVD Talk|access-date=June 27, 2012|archive-date=November 6, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121106000452/http://www.dvdtalk.com/reviews/15632/leonard-part-6/|url-status=live}}</ref> By 1990, Dennis King of the ''[[Tulsa World]]'' wrote that the film had "become synonymous with 'bomb{{'"}}.<ref>{{cite news|last=King|first=Dennis|title=Ghost Dad|date=July 6, 1990|newspaper=[[Tulsa World]]|url=http://www.tulsaworld.com/archives/ghost-dad/article_5b0372e5-e91b-5570-b2c7-c9edabbfae0a.html|access-date=January 27, 2019|archive-date=May 7, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190507042016/https://www.tulsaworld.com/archives/ghost-dad/article_5b0372e5-e91b-5570-b2c7-c9edabbfae0a.html|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Total Film'' and ''Vanity Fair'' subsequently included ''Leonard Part 6'' on their respective worst film lists.<ref name=TotalFilm/><ref name="italianvanity"/> Cosby himself disowned the film, and when it was released to theaters he publicly advised people not to see it. It earned [[Golden Raspberry]]s for Worst Actor (Cosby), Worst Picture, and Worst Screenplay. It was also nominated for two more Razzie Awards, for Worst Supporting Actress and Worst Director.<ref name=LATimes>{{cite news|title=Leonard RIP?|newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=December 20, 1987|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1987-12-20-ca-29856-story.html|access-date=December 26, 2010|first=Pat H.|last=Broeske|archive-date=January 19, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120119151239/http://articles.latimes.com/1987-12-20/entertainment/ca-29856_1_leonard-part|url-status=live}}</ref> Cosby became the first person to [[List of people who have accepted Golden Raspberry Awards|accept a Golden Raspberry Award]],<ref name="feran">{{Cite news |last= Feran |first= Tim |title = Section: Features – Accent & Arts – Intermission | newspaper = [[Columbus Dispatch]] |location = [[Columbus, Ohio]] |page = 01F |date = April 26, 1992}}</ref> and said "It was the worst movie I ever made – the worst movie anyone ever made".<ref>{{cite news |title=Stars take critics with a grain of salt |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=waFEAAAAIBAJ&pg=1013,2816922&dq=leonard+part+6+worst+ever&hl=en |newspaper=[[The Daily Union]] |date=May 12, 1991 |access-date=April 1, 2020 |archive-date=August 16, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220816054117/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=waFEAAAAIBAJ&pg=1013,2816922&dq=leonard+part+6+worst+ever&hl=en |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== ''Nukie'' (1987) ===
{{Main|Nukie{{!}}''Nukie''}}
''Nukie'' is a 1987 South African film directed by Sias Odendaal (credited as Sias Odendal) and Michael Pakleppa, and starring [[Steve Railsback]], Ronald France, and [[Glynis Johns]]. The plot concerns an alien, Nukie, who crash lands on Earth and seeks help from two children to reunite with his brother, Miko, who has been captured by the United States government. The film is considered to be a knock-off of [[Steven Spielberg]]'s 1982 film ''[[E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial]]''. Witney Seibold of ''[[/Film]]'' writes that "''Nukie'' is only remarkable for how undeniably terrible it is", noting that it appears on lists of the worst films ever made.<ref name="slash">{{cite web |last=Seibold |first=Witney |title=The Nukie Controversy Explained: Destroying Crappy Movies For Charity |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/1167319/the-nukie-controversy-explained-destroying-crappy-movies-for-charity/ |website=[[/Film]] |access-date=January 16, 2023 |date=January 13, 2023 |archive-date=January 14, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230114222128/https://www.slashfilm.com/1167319/the-nukie-controversy-explained-destroying-crappy-movies-for-charity/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[Comic Book Resources]]'' note that it is "regarded as one of the worst movies ever made",<ref>{{cite web |last=Trinos |first=Angelo Delos |title=10 Copycat Films That Are Worse Than What They're Ripping Off |url=https://www.cbr.com/copycat-films-worse-than-original/ |website=[[Comic Book Resources]] |date=15 August 2022 |access-date=11 January 2023 |archive-date=January 11, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230111233339/https://www.cbr.com/copycat-films-worse-than-original/ |url-status=live }}</ref> with critic [[The Cinema Snob|Brad Jones]] selecting ''Nukie'' as the worst film he has ever seen,<ref>{{cite web |last=Phalin |first=Mike |title=Schlock and the Snob: An Interview With Brad Jones |url=https://www.dreadcentral.com/news/185215/schlock-snob-interview-brad-jones/ |website=[[Dread Central]] |access-date=11 January 2023 |date=26 August 2016 |archive-date=January 1, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230101080206/https://www.dreadcentral.com/news/185215/schlock-snob-interview-brad-jones/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and [[Red Letter Media]] calling it "Possibly one of the worst films ever made."<ref>{{cite web |last=Newgent |first=Sean |title=VHS copy of forgotten 'E.T.' knock-off 'Nukie' sells for $80,600 |url=https://www.kgun9.com/entertainment/vhs-copy-of-forgotten-e-t-knock-off-nukie-sells-for-80-600 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230111230814/https://www.kgun9.com/entertainment/vhs-copy-of-forgotten-e-t-knock-off-nukie-sells-for-80-600 |publisher=[[KGUN-TV]] |access-date=11 January 2023 |language=en |date=10 January 2023 |archive-date=11 January 2023}}</ref> ''Total Film'' write that it is considered by some to be the "most painful movie ever made";<ref name="kidsmovie">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/50-worst-kids-movies/|title=50 Worst Kids Movies|last=Winning|first=Joshua|work=[[Total Film]]|publisher=[[GamesRadar]]|date=November 8, 2011|access-date=July 8, 2017 }}</ref> they listed ''Nukie'' the worst kids' movie ever made and one of the worst science-fiction films ever made.<ref name="kidsmovie"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/25-worst-science-fiction-films/|title=25 Worst Science-Fiction Films|last=Winning|first=Joshua|work=[[Total Film]]|publisher=[[GamesRadar]]|date=June 30, 2014|access-date=July 8, 2017|archive-date=July 14, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170714012719/http://www.gamesradar.com/25-worst-science-fiction-films/|url-status=live}}</ref> The film's co-director, Michael Pakleppa, referred to ''Nukie'' as "the most wrong-gone thing [he had] ever done in [his] life" and feared that the final product was "the worst film on Earth".<ref>{{cite web |last=Balmont |first=James |title=Nukie: the strange story behind the forgotten ET knock-off |url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/film-tv/article/58061/1/nukie-the-et-knock-off-film-awful-alien-vhs-interview |website=[[Dazed]] |access-date=January 30, 2023 |language=en |date=January 30, 2023 |archive-date=January 30, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230130102008/https://www.dazeddigital.com/film-tv/article/58061/1/nukie-the-et-knock-off-film-awful-alien-vhs-interview |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== ''The Garbage Pail Kids Movie'' (1987) ===
{{Main|The Garbage Pail Kids Movie{{!}}''The Garbage Pail Kids Movie''}}
''The Garbage Pail Kids Movie'' is a 1987 [[live-action]] adaptation of the then-popular [[Garbage Pail Kids|trading card series of the same name]], itself a gross-out parody of the then-popular [[Cabbage Patch Kids]] dolls co-created by [[Pulitzer Prize]]-winning cartoonist [[Art Spiegelman]]. The film is often criticized for its [[gross-out humor]], nonsensical plot, poor explanations, bad acting, and the unsettling appearance of the Garbage Pail Kids (the title characters are depicted by dwarf actors in low-budget costumes, with poorly functioning mouths and expressionless faces). It has a 0% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.<ref>{{Rotten Tomatoes|qid=Q7735810|title=The Garbage Pail Kids Movie}}</ref> On [[Metacritic]], the film holds a score of 1, making it tied for the lowest scoring film on the site.<ref name="Metacritic">{{cite web |url=https://www.metacritic.com/browse/movies/score/metascore/all?sort=asc |title=Best Movies of All Time |work=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |access-date=April 17, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230215194915/https://www.metacritic.com/browse/movies/score/metascore/all?sort=asc |archive-date=February 15, 2023 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Caryn James of ''[[The New York Times]]'' said the movie is "too repulsive for children or adults of any age" and is "enough to make you believe in strict and faraway boarding schools".<ref>{{cite news |first=Caryn |last=James |url=https://movies.nytimes.com/movie/review?res=9B0DE1D81030F931A1575BC0A961948260 |title=Movie Review – The Garbage Pail Kids Movie |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=June 6, 2010 |date=August 28, 1987 |archive-date=February 10, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120210083257/http://movies.nytimes.com/movie/review?res=9B0DE1D81030F931A1575BC0A961948260 |url-status=live }}</ref> Carlos Coto of the ''[[Sun-Sentinel]]'' called it "one of the worst ever made".<ref>{{cite news |url=http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/1987-09-05/features/8703110946_1_garbage-pail-kids-cabbage-patch-kids-kids-show |title=Trashy 'Garbage Pail Kids' Has No Value |newspaper=[[Sun-Sentinel]] |access-date=September 29, 2010 |date=September 5, 1987 |archive-date=January 13, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120113001340/http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/1987-09-05/features/8703110946_1_garbage-pail-kids-cabbage-patch-kids-kids-show |url-status=dead }}</ref> Internet critic [[Doug Walker (comedian)|Doug Walker]], best known for the series ''[[Nostalgia Critic]]'', stated in a 2012 video that it was not only the worst film he had ever reviewed as the Nostalgia Critic, but the worst movie he had ever seen overall, deeming that the film served to undermine its own moral. His mother had forbidden him from seeing it as a child, stating, "I, by all the heavenly blessings, thank my mother for stopping me from seeing this movie, because I'm very convinced that this movie would've taken away half my brain."<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?si=4-mps8wKdhD8nWDu&v=_8Ik0xbSjSY |work=Zachary Matthew James |title=Doug Walker on The Garbage Pail Kids Movie |via=[[YouTube]] |date=December 16, 2012 |access-date=May 17, 2024 |archive-date=May 17, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240517170607/https://www.youtube.com/watch?si=4-mps8wKdhD8nWDu&v=_8Ik0xbSjSY |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2025, Walker released an updated list of the worst films he had reviewed, with ''The Garbage Pail Kids Movie'' once again taking the top spot.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://youtube.com/watch?v=N5s747W621s |title=Doug's Top 10 Worst Movies |work=Channel Awesome |via=[[YouTube]] |date=May 9, 2025 |access-date=June 25, 2025 }}</ref>

Much of the film's content is said to be inappropriate for children, its intended audience. Throughout the movie, the Garbage Pail Kids steal, get in fights, bite people's toes off, flatulate in people's faces, threaten others with [[switchblade]]s, urinate upon themselves, and run over cars. In addition to scatological behavior, the movie has several scenes that feature sexual images, violence, and drinking. Offended parents launched a nationwide protest of the movie that successfully resulted in the movie being withdrawn from circulation.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://allmovie.com/work/the-garbage-pail-kids-movie-19217 |title=The Garbage Pail Kids Movie > Overview |website=[[AllMovie]] |access-date=June 6, 2010 |archive-date=June 1, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200601082028/https://www.allmovie.com/movie/the-garbage-pail-kids-movie-v19217 |url-status=live }}</ref> The shortened release contributed to the movie's poor gross of only $1,576,615.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/movies/?id=garbagepailkids.htm |title=The Garbage Pail Kids Movie (1987) |work=Box Office Mojo |access-date=March 7, 2011 |archive-date=March 23, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110323072054/http://boxofficemojo.com/movies/?id=garbagepailkids.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> It was nominated for three Razzies at the [[8th Golden Raspberry Awards]]: Worst Visual Effects, Worst New Star for the Garbage Pail Kids collectively, and Worst Original Song.

=== ''Silent Night, Deadly Night Part 2'' (1987) ===
{{Main|Silent Night, Deadly Night Part 2{{!}}''Silent Night, Deadly Night Part 2''}}
''Silent Night, Deadly Night Part 2'' is the sequel to the 1984 Christmas-themed [[slasher film]] ''[[Silent Night, Deadly Night]]'', which faced protests from parent groups and sharp criticism from ''[[At the Movies (1986 TV program)|At the Movies]]'' hosts Roger Ebert and Gene Siskel due to its promotional campaign featuring an ax-wielding [[Santa Claus]].<ref name="flavorwiresndnp2">{{cite web |last1=Bailey |first1=Jason |title=So Bad It's Good: It's Christmas Time (and Garbage Day) in 'Silent Night, Deadly Night Part 2' |url=https://www.flavorwire.com/493459/so-bad-its-good-its-christmas-time-and-garbage-day-in-silent-night-deadly-night-part-2 |website=[[Flavorwire]] |access-date=December 14, 2024 |language=en |date=December 12, 2014}}</ref> The film was a financial success despite the controversy, leading producers to enlist [[Lee Harry]] to repurpose its footage for a new project; however, $100,000 was eventually allocated to shoot additional original material.<ref name="sndnp2sr">{{cite web |last1=Kennedy |first1=Michael |title=Why Silent Night, Deadly Night 2 Was So Legendarily Bad |url=https://screenrant.com/silent-deadly-night-2-problems-production-bad/ |website=[[Screen Rant]] |access-date=December 14, 2024 |language=en |date=3 August 2022}}</ref> Nearly half of the ''Silent Night, Deadly Night Part 2''{{'}}s runtime consists of flashbacks to the first film, narrated by Ricky Caldwell (Eric Freeman), the brother of the original film's protagonist, as he recounts events before embarking on his own murderous rampage.<ref name="sndnp2sr"/>

Much of the film's reception and legacy centers on Freeman's performance, which ''Flavorwire'' states "may very well be the single worst performance ever committed to celluloid".<ref name="flavorwiresndnp2" /> A scene in which Ricky shouts "garbage day!" before shooting and killing a bystander taking out his trash became an [[Internet meme]] after being uploaded to [[YouTube]] in its early years.<ref name="flavorwiresndnp2" /> ''Screen Rant'' has since deemed the film to be "a masterpiece of the so bad it's good variety",<ref name="sndnp2sr" /> and "one of the worst movies ever made"<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gunning |first1=Cathal |title=Every Killer Santa Horror Movie Ranked |url=https://screenrant.com/killer-santa-horror-movies-ranked-worst-best/ |website=[[Screen Rant]] |access-date=December 14, 2024 |language=en |date=25 December 2022}}</ref> Emmett O'Regan of ''[[Comic Book Resources]]'' also selected it as the worst movie ever made,<ref>{{cite web |last1=O'Regan |first1=Emmett |title=Why Silent Night, Deadly Night Part 2 Is the Worst Movie of All Time |url=https://www.cbr.com/silent-night-deadly-night-worst-movie-all-time/ |website=[[Comic Book Resources]] |access-date=December 14, 2024 |language=en |date= December 11, 2022}}</ref> and an article in ''[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]'' asserted that: "in terms of filmmaking quality—it's hard to believe that in terms of pure, unadulterated crap, anything could ever surpass it."<ref name="20pastechristmas"/> Additionally, ''Flavorwire'', ''[[/Film]]'', and ''Paste'' have all listed it as the worst Christmas film ever made.<ref name="flavorwiresndnp2" /><ref>{{cite web |last1=Donato |first1=Matt |title='Silent Night, Deadly Night Part 2' Is The Best Worst Christmas Horror Movie And You Must Watch It |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/555210/silent-night-deadly-night-part-2/ |website=[[/Film]] |access-date=December 15, 2024 |date=December 22, 2017}}</ref><ref name="20pastechristmas">{{cite web |last1=Vorel |first1=Jim |title=The 20 Worst Christmas Movies of All Time |url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/movies/christmas/the-20-worst-christmas-movies-of-all-time |website=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]] |access-date=December 14, 2024}}</ref> ''Time Out'' and ''Flavorwire'' later included it on their respective lists of the worst films ever made.<ref name="timeoutlist"/><ref name="Flavorwire"/>

=== ''Hobgoblins'' (1988) ===
{{Main|Hobgoblins (film){{!}}''Hobgoblins'' (film)}}
''Hobgoblins'', by [[Rick Sloane]], is widely considered a low-budget [[Mockbuster|knock-off]] that capitalizes on the popularity of the 1984 film ''[[Gremlins]].''<ref name="hobstandard"/> It gained popularity in 1998 after being featured on an episode of ''Mystery Science Theater 3000''. ''MST3K'' writer [[Paul Chaplin]] later commented on ''Hobgoblins'', saying, "Oh, man. You have no idea the torture it was to watch this movie several times in the space of a week. It shoots right to the top of the list of the worst movies we've ever done." Specific points of the film that were lampooned were the extreme misogyny and atrocious treatment of women; the film's technical incompetence and repetitive scenes; its asinine, poorly conceived plot; its dreadful acting; and its ugly look and gratuitous vulgarity, particularly in regards to its characters and subject matter.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.castleforrester.com/media/guide/0907.htm |title=Episode Guide|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081013042500/http://www.castleforrester.com/media/guide/0907.htm |archive-date=October 13, 2008 }}</ref> David Cornelius of ''DVD Talk'' stated, "There's not one aspect of this movie that isn't the Worst Thing Ever."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dvdtalk.com/reviews/38236/mad-monster-rally/ |title=Mad Monster Rally : DVD Talk Review of the DVD Video |website=[[DVD Talk]]|access-date=March 5, 2014|last=Cornelius |first=David|date=August 18, 2009 |archive-date=February 24, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140224044732/http://www.dvdtalk.com/reviews/38236/mad-monster-rally/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[Evening Standard|The Standard]]''{{'}}s ''Bad Horror Club'' noted its status as one of the worst films of all time, commenting: "it's so preposterously badly made, terribly acted and ineptly constructed that it makes for some of the most fun you can ever have watching a movie."<ref name="hobstandard">{{cite web |last1=Embley |first1=Jochan |last2=Fletcher |first2=Harry |title=Remembering 80s disaster Hobgoblins in all its chaotic glory |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/culture/film/bad-horror-club-hobgoblins-80s-disaster-a4422426.html |website=[[Evening Standard|The Standard]] |access-date=December 8, 2024 |language=en |date=April 23, 2020}}</ref>

Sloane has embraced ''Hobgoblins''{{'}} status as one of the worst films of all time, stating that he fears that it will be forgotten if it is removed from IMDb's user-generated bottom 100 list.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dreadcentral.com/news/12169/rick-sloane-talks-hobgoblins/|title=Rick Sloane Talks Hobgoblins|author=Foywonder|date=June 23, 2009|website=[[Dread Central]]|language=en|access-date=December 8, 2024}}</ref> After seeing the ''MST3K'' episode himself, Sloane was inspired to direct [[Hobgoblins 2|a sequel]], which was released in 2009.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mubi.com/films/hobgoblins-2|title=Hobgoblins 2|via=[[Mubi (streaming service)|MUBI]]|access-date=May 10, 2020|archive-date=September 27, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210927043012/https://mubi.com/films/hobgoblins-2|url-status=live}}</ref> In addition to IMDb,<ref name="hobstandard"/> it has been featured on lists from ''Flavorwire'' and ''Total Film'',<ref name="Flavorwire"/><ref name=TotalFilm/> and ''[[ComicBook.com]]'' placed it at the top of their list of "Terrible Movies That Are So Bad They're A Must-Watch".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hathaway |first1=Ben |title=5 Terrible Movies That Are So Bad They're A Must-Watch |url=https://comicbook.com/movies/list/5-terrible-movies-that-are-so-bad-theyre-a-must-watch/ |website=[[ComicBook.com]] |access-date=February 28, 2026 |date=October 15, 2025}}</ref>

=== ''Mac and Me'' (1988) ===
{{Main|Mac and Me{{!}}''Mac and Me''}}
''Mac and Me'' is about a young boy in a wheelchair who meets and befriends an alien who has crash-landed on Earth. A box-office failure,<ref>{{cite news|title=Advertising is so much a part of life that it's understandable to find familiar products in films. But sometimes it goes too far.|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=August 29, 1999|url=https://articles.latimes.com/1999/aug/29/entertainment/ca-4591/3|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131204041237/http://articles.latimes.com/1999/aug/29/entertainment/ca-4591/3|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 4, 2013|access-date=May 17, 2012}}</ref> the film grossed $6,424,112 in the United States<ref>{{mojo title|macandme|Mac and Me}}</ref> on a $13 million budget.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://catalog.afi.com/Catalog/MovieDetails/58827|title=Mac and Me|website=[[AFI Catalog of Feature Films]]|access-date=April 27, 2018|archive-date=April 28, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180428093913/https://catalog.afi.com/Catalog/MovieDetails/58827|url-status=live}}</ref> It used to have a 0% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose critical consensus notes that it is "duly<!--sic: should be "dually"--> infamous" as both an imitation of ''[[E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial]]'' (1982), and a marketing vehicle for [[McDonald's]] and [[Coca-Cola]]<ref name="rottentomatoes1">{{Rotten Tomatoes|qid=Q1761515|title=Mac and Me}}</ref> (the filmmakers had admitted a profit-sharing arrangement with the former).<ref>{{cite news|title= Movie Review Mac and Me Takes a Big McBite Out of E.T.|newspaper= [[Los Angeles Times]]|url= https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1988-08-15-ca-300-story.html|access-date= December 5, 2010|archive-date= March 7, 2011|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110307085307/http://articles.latimes.com/1988-08-15/entertainment/ca-300_1_big-mac|url-status= live}}</ref> [[Leonard Maltin]] described the film as being "more like a TV commercial than a movie",<ref name="Maltin01211"/> and Marjorie Baumgarten of the ''[[Austin Chronicle]]'' called it a "shameless ''E.T.'' knockoff".<ref name="rottentomatoes1"/> ''Mac and Me'' is widely regarded as one of the worst films ever made,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://screenrant.com/movies-with-bizarre-weird-source-material/|title=15 Movies With Bizarre Source Material|last=McGranaghan|first=Mike|date=March 21, 2017|website=[[Screen Rant]]|access-date=June 23, 2018|archive-date=June 24, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180624035654/https://screenrant.com/movies-with-bizarre-weird-source-material/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite
